> Online: https://n1k1tas95.github.io/dashboard-kit/en/

# Accordion
Page: https://n1k1tas95.github.io/dashboard-kit/en/accordion.html

Sections that open and close, built on `<details>`: also without JavaScript, from the keyboard and with screen readers.

## Accordion

A list of sections that open and close, built on the native `<details>` element: it works without JavaScript, is used from the keyboard (Enter and Space on the title) and is already readable by screen readers. The container is `kit-accordion`, each item is a direct-child `<details>` with a `<summary>` as the title and the content inside `kit-accordion-body`. `open` on the `<details>` opens it initially. Where the browser supports it the opening is animated (not with "reduce motion").

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-accordion">
  <details open>
    <summary>How do I issue an invoice?</summary>
    <div class="kit-accordion-body"><p>From the <strong>Invoices</strong> menu choose "New", fill in the customer and lines and save: the number is assigned automatically.</p></div>
  </details>
  <details>
    <summary>Can I edit it after sending?</summary>
    <div class="kit-accordion-body"><p>No: a sent invoice is corrected with a credit note and a new invoice.</p></div>
  </details>
  <details>
    <summary>Where do I find rejected invoices?</summary>
    <div class="kit-accordion-body"><p>In the list, with the "Discarded" filter. The reason for the rejection is in the detail.</p></div>
  </details>
</div>
```

### Only one open

`data-kit-accordion="single"` (requires `kit.js`) closes the other items when one is opened; if several items start open only the first stays open. Without JavaScript the same effect is achieved with the same `name="…"` on all the `<details>`, which recent browsers honor by themselves. An accordion inside another's item is independent.

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-accordion" data-kit-accordion="single">
  <details open><summary>Company details</summary><div class="kit-accordion-body">Company name, VAT number and address.</div></details>
  <details><summary>Contacts</summary><div class="kit-accordion-body">Email, certified email and phone.</div></details>
  <details><summary>Payments</summary><div class="kit-accordion-body">IBAN and payment terms.</div></details>
</div>
```

### With a label and inside a card

`kit-accordion-meta` inside the `<summary>` puts a count or a badge on the right, before the arrow. `kit-accordion-flush` removes the box and shadows, for an accordion inside a card or a panel.

Example markup:

```html
<section class="kit-card">
  <div class="kit-card-body">
    <div class="kit-accordion kit-accordion-flush">
      <details open>
        <summary>To issue <span class="kit-accordion-meta"><span class="kit-badge kit-badge-warning">3</span></span></summary>
        <div class="kit-accordion-body">Three draft invoices.</div>
      </details>
      <details>
        <summary>Discarded <span class="kit-accordion-meta"><span class="kit-badge kit-badge-danger">1</span></span></summary>
        <div class="kit-accordion-body">One invoice rejected by the exchange system.</div>
      </details>
      <details>
        <summary>Archived <span class="kit-accordion-meta">128</span></summary>
        <div class="kit-accordion-body">Invoices from previous years.</div>
      </details>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>
```

### JavaScript

`Kit.accordion(element, { single })` does the same from code and returns `{ open(x), close(x), toggle(x), openAll(), closeAll(), items() }`, where `x` is the position (from 0) or the `<details>`. Every opening and closing fires `kit:accordion` with `{ item, index, open }`. When printing all items are shown open.

```js
const acc = Kit.accordion("#faq", { single: true });

acc.open(2);        // opens the third item (and closes the others)
acc.closeAll();

document.querySelector("#faq").addEventListener("kit:accordion", (e) => {
  console.log(e.detail.index, e.detail.open);
});
```

# Buttons
Page: https://n1k1tas95.github.io/dashboard-kit/en/buttons.html

Buttons of all kinds and sizes. A `.kit-btn` works on `<button>`, `<a>` and `<label>`.

## Variants

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-bar">
  <button class="kit-btn">Default</button>
  <button class="kit-btn kit-btn-primary">Primary</button>
  <button class="kit-btn kit-btn-ghost">Ghost</button>
  <button class="kit-btn kit-btn-danger">Danger</button>
  <button class="kit-btn" disabled>Disabled</button>
</div>
```

`kit-btn-primary` for the screen's main action (only one per area), `kit-btn-ghost` for secondary actions without a border, `kit-btn-danger` for destructive ones.

## Sizes

The base height is `--kit-ctl` (40px), the same as fields, so buttons and inputs line up. `kit-btn-lg` brings it to 48px.

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-bar">
  <button class="kit-btn">Normal</button>
  <button class="kit-btn kit-btn-primary kit-btn-lg">Large</button>
</div>
```

## With an icon

Put the `<svg class="kit-icon">` before the text. For icon-only buttons add `kit-btn-icon` (square) and an `aria-label`.

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-bar">
  <button class="kit-btn kit-btn-primary"><svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-download"/></svg>Download</button>
  <button class="kit-btn kit-btn-icon" aria-label="Search"><svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-search"/></svg></button>
  <button class="kit-btn kit-btn-ghost kit-btn-icon" aria-label="Download"><svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-download"/></svg></button>
</div>
```

## With a counter

Example markup:

```html
<button class="kit-btn">Filters <span class="kit-count">3</span></button>
```

## Group and link

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-btn-group">
  <button class="kit-btn">One</button>
  <button class="kit-btn">Two</button>
  <a class="kit-btn" href="#">A link</a>
</div>
```

---

# Cards and details
Page: https://n1k1tas95.github.io/dashboard-kit/en/cards.html

Cards, KPI cards, stats row, lists, key/value pairs and code blocks: the containers and details of a dashboard.

## Card

A container with a border, rounded corners and a light shadow (in the dark theme the shadow disappears). Every part is optional: `kit-card-head`, `kit-card-body`, `kit-card-foot`.

Example markup:

```html
<section class="kit-card">
  <div class="kit-card-head">Card title</div>
  <div class="kit-card-body">The card content.</div>
  <div class="kit-card-foot">
    <button class="kit-btn">Cancel</button>
    <button class="kit-btn kit-btn-primary">Save</button>
  </div>
</section>
```

Without `kit-card-body` the content touches the edges: fine for full-width tables and charts.

## KPI card

A label, a big value and a change. In a row with `kit-row-cols-*` add `kit-h-100` so they all reach the same height.

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-row kit-row-cols-2 kit-row-cols-lg-4">
  <div><div class="kit-card kit-kpi kit-h-100"><small>Documents</small><b>1,284</b><span class="kit-badge kit-badge-success">+4%</span></div></div>
  <div><div class="kit-card kit-kpi kit-h-100"><small>Total</small><b>€48,920.10</b><span class="kit-badge kit-badge-success">+1.2%</span></div></div>
  <div><div class="kit-card kit-kpi kit-h-100"><small>To review</small><b>17</b><span class="kit-badge kit-badge-warning">−3</span></div></div>
  <div><div class="kit-card kit-kpi kit-h-100"><small>Discarded</small><b>2</b><span class="kit-badge kit-badge-danger">+1</span></div></div>
</div>
```

## Stats row

More compact than KPIs: many figures in a single card, separated by a thin line. On the phone they stack.

Example markup:

```html
<section class="kit-card kit-stats">
  <div class="kit-stat"><small>Documents</small><b>1,284</b></div>
  <div class="kit-stat"><small>Total</small><b>€48,920.10</b><em>VAT included</em></div>
  <div class="kit-stat"><small>Received</small><b class="kit-success">€32,100</b></div>
  <div class="kit-stat"><small>Issued</small><b class="kit-danger">€16,820</b></div>
</section>
```

## List

Items stacked in the same box, like several joined cards: `kit-list` on the container, `kit-list-item` on each item. The container can be `<ul>`, `<ol>` or `<div>`; the items `<li>`, `<a>`, `<button>` or `<div>`. A badge or an icon inside the item aligns by itself; `kit-list-main` gathers title and description and takes the free space.

Example markup:

```html
<ul class="kit-list">
  <li class="kit-list-item">Received invoices</li>
  <li class="kit-list-item">Issued invoices <span class="kit-badge">12</span></li>
  <li class="kit-list-item">
    <span class="kit-list-main"><b>Credit notes</b><small>Last imported yesterday</small></span>
    <span class="kit-badge kit-badge-warning">3</span>
  </li>
</ul>
```

### Clickable items

With `<a>` or `<button>` the item highlights on mouse hover. `is-active` (or `aria-current`) marks the selected one, `aria-disabled="true"` the unavailable one. The container, in this case, is a `<div>`.

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-list">
  <a class="kit-list-item is-active" href="#list-actions" aria-current="true"><svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-info"/></svg>Overview</a>
  <a class="kit-list-item" href="#list-actions"><svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-download"/></svg>Exports</a>
  <button class="kit-list-item" type="button"><svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-edit"/></svg>Settings</button>
  <a class="kit-list-item" href="#list-actions" aria-disabled="true"><svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-trash"/></svg>Trash</a>
</div>
```

### States

To signal an item's outcome: `kit-list-item-success`, `-warning` and `-danger` give a soft background and colored text.

Example markup:

```html
<ul class="kit-list">
  <li class="kit-list-item kit-list-item-success">Import completed</li>
  <li class="kit-list-item kit-list-item-warning">2 documents to review</li>
  <li class="kit-list-item kit-list-item-danger">1 file discarded</li>
</ul>
```

### Separate cards and compact

`kit-list-cards` separates the items: each becomes a card with its own border, with a gap in between. It also works with clickable and active items and with the states. `kit-list-sm` reduces the space above and below each item and combines with the other variants.

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-list kit-list-cards">
  <a class="kit-list-item is-active" href="#list-cards" aria-current="true"><span class="kit-list-main"><b>Smith Ltd</b><small>Invoice 24/118</small></span><span class="kit-badge">To pay</span></a>
  <a class="kit-list-item" href="#list-cards"><span class="kit-list-main"><b>Brown &amp; Co.</b><small>Invoice 24/119</small></span><span class="kit-badge kit-badge-success">Paid</span></a>
  <div class="kit-list-item kit-list-item-danger"><span class="kit-list-main"><b>Green Inc</b><small>Rejected by the tax authority</small></span></div>
</div>
<ul class="kit-list kit-list-sm">
  <li class="kit-list-item">Compact item</li>
  <li class="kit-list-item">Another compact item <span class="kit-badge">2</span></li>
</ul>
```

### Numbered, horizontal, borderless

`kit-list-numbered` puts a number in front of each item. `kit-list-horizontal` lays them out in a row, of equal width (below 760px they stack again). `kit-list-flush` removes border, corners and shadow: it is for use inside a card, which already has its own box.

Example markup:

```html
<ol class="kit-list kit-list-numbered">
  <li class="kit-list-item">Choose the files</li>
  <li class="kit-list-item">Check the preview</li>
  <li class="kit-list-item">Confirm the import</li>
</ol>
<ul class="kit-list kit-list-horizontal">
  <li class="kit-list-item">Draft</li>
  <li class="kit-list-item">Sent</li>
  <li class="kit-list-item">Paid</li>
</ul>
<section class="kit-card">
  <div class="kit-card-head">Recent activity</div>
  <ul class="kit-list kit-list-flush">
    <li class="kit-list-item"><span class="kit-list-main"><b>Smith Ltd</b><small>Invoice 24/118</small></span><span>€1,250.00</span></li>
    <li class="kit-list-item"><span class="kit-list-main"><b>Brown &amp; Co.</b><small>Invoice 24/119</small></span><span>€380.40</span></li>
  </ul>
</section>
```

## Key / value

A two-column `<dl>`: gray labels, values on the right, with automatic wrapping for long texts. Useful for an item's details.

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-card kit-card-body">
  <dl class="kit-kv">
    <dt>Number</dt><dd>FT-0042</dd>
    <dt>Date</dt><dd>03/12/2026</dd>
    <dt>Customer</dt><dd>Alpha Services Ltd</dd>
    <dt>Description</dt><dd>Consulting and support for the month of March, with reimbursement of travel expenses.</dd>
  </dl>
</div>
```

## Code snippets

A code block colored like in an editor: tags, attributes, strings, keywords, functions and comments. You write a normal `<pre class="kit-code">` and with `data-kit-code` (with `kit.js`) the code colors itself. The value is the language: `html` (also with `<script>` and `<style>` inside), `js` or `css`; without it, `kit.js` guesses. The text must be written with entities (`&lt;` instead of `<`), as in any HTML page. Without `kit.js` the block stays readable, just without colors.

Example markup:

```html
  <pre class="kit-code" data-kit-code="html"><code>&lt;button class="kit-btn kit-btn-primary" data-kit-open="#new"&gt;
  &lt;svg class="kit-icon"&gt;&lt;use href="#i-plus"/&gt;&lt;/svg&gt; New invoice
&lt;/button&gt;</code></pre>
  <pre class="kit-code" data-kit-code="js"><code>// reload the documents and show the outcome
const n = await loadDocuments({ year: 2026, max: 50 });
Kit.toast(n + " documents", { type: "success" });</code></pre>
  <pre class="kit-code" data-kit-code="css"><code>.invoice:hover { background: var(--kit-hover); }
@media (max-width: 760px) { .invoice { padding: 8px; } }</code></pre>
```

### The "Copy" button

With `data-kit-code-copy` the block is put in a `kit-snippet` and the "Copy" button appears (on mouse hover, always visible on the phone). The attribute's value is the label; `data-kit-code-copied` is the one that appears after copying. When the text is copied the `kit:copy` event fires with `{ text }`.

Example markup:

```html
  <pre class="kit-code" data-kit-code="html" data-kit-code-copy><code>&lt;section class="kit-card"&gt;
  &lt;div class="kit-card-body"&gt;Hello&lt;/div&gt;
&lt;/section&gt;</code></pre>
```

### From JavaScript

`Kit.code(pre, { lang, text, copy })` colors a block and returns `{ set(text, lang), text() }`, useful when the code changes (a generated example, a preview). `Kit.highlight(text, lang)` instead returns an already colored DOM fragment, to insert wherever you like. Both build only text nodes and `<span>`s, never HTML: the displayed code is not executed, whatever it contains. Beyond 100,000 characters the text stays uncolored, so a huge text does not slow the page; an unknown language is guessed.

```js
const block = Kit.code("#example", { lang: "js", copy: true });
block.set("Kit.toast('Saved!');");              // changes the displayed code
element.append(Kit.highlight("<b>hello</b>", "html"));
```

The colors are the tokens `--kit-hl-tag`, `-attr`, `-str`, `-kw`, `-fn`, `-num` e `-com` (see [Themes and tokens](https://n1k1tas95.github.io/dashboard-kit/en/theming.html)), and change by themselves between light and dark theme.

---

# Charts
Page: https://n1k1tas95.github.io/dashboard-kit/en/charts.html

Bars, lines, donut and sparklines in SVG, no libraries. They require `kit.js`.

## Bar chart

`Kit.barChart(element, options)` draws a bar chart in SVG inside the element. The vertical axis has round values (1, 2, 2.5, 5, 10 for a power of ten) with thousands abbreviated as "k" and "M". Each bar has a tooltip. If there are many bars the chart scrolls horizontally and starts from the end, that is, from the most recent data. Colors, texts and grid follow the theme and the text size; the chart redraws itself when the window changes width.

Each element of `data` has a label (`label`), a value for each series (`values`) and, optionally, a `group`: it is written under the bar only when it changes, and is handy for the year.

Example markup:

```html
 v.toLocaleString("en-US", { style: "currency", currency: "EUR" })
});'>
  <div id="grafico"></div>
```

## Several series and clicks

With several series (`series`) each month has one bar per series and the legend appears. The default colors are `--kit-c1`…`--kit-c4`; for another color there is `color` in the series. With `onSelect` the bars become buttons reachable with Tab, activated with Enter or space; the element also receives the `kit:select` event with `{ index, series, item }`.

Example markup:

```html
 Kit.toast("Month: " + month.label + " " + month.group)
});'>
  <div id="grafico2"></div>
```

## Stacked bars

`stacked: true` puts the series one on top of the other: each month has a single bar, as tall as the sum. Useful to see how a total is made up.

Example markup:

```html
<div id="grafico3"></div>
```

## Lines

`Kit.lineChart` takes the same options as bars. A `null` value leaves a gap in the line (the month without data). The axis starts from the lowest value, not from zero, so variations are visible; `zero: true` brings it back to zero. Each series has a different symbol (circle, square, triangle), so they can be told apart even without the colors. `area: true` colors the space under the line, `markers: false` removes the points.

Example markup:

```html
 v.toFixed(3) + " €/l",
  axisFormat: (v) => v.toFixed(2) + " €"
});'>
  <div id="grafico4"></div>
```

Example markup:

```html
<div id="grafico5"></div>
```

## Donut

`Kit.donut` shows the parts of a total. In the center is the total (or the text of `centerValue` and `centerLabel`), beside it a legend with value and percentage. With `onSelect` the legend rows become buttons. Slices with a value of zero do not appear.

Example markup:

```html
 v.toLocaleString("en-US", { style: "currency", currency: "EUR", maximumFractionDigits: 0 }),
  centerLabel: "Spending 2026"
});'>
  <div id="grafico-ciambella"></div>
```

## Chart legend

The series colors are the `--kit-c1` and `--kit-c2` tokens, which change by themselves between light and dark theme. In SVG charts use them with `fill: var(--kit-c1)` (see the [sample dashboard](https://n1k1tas95.github.io/dashboard-kit/en/dashboard.html)).

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-legend">
  <span><i style="background: var(--kit-c1)"></i>Received</span>
  <span><i style="background: var(--kit-c2)"></i>Issued</span>
</div>
```

## Sparkline

`Kit.sparkline` is a tiny chart, with no axes, to put next to a number, for example in a [KPI card](https://n1k1tas95.github.io/dashboard-kit/en/cards.html#kpi). It takes `values` and, optionally, `type` (`"line"` or `"bar"`), `color`, `area` (`false` removes it) and `label`. The size is that of the element: change it with CSS (by default 6rem × 1.9rem).

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-stats">
  <div class="kit-kpi"><div class="kit-mute">Invoices</div><div class="kit-fs-3 kit-fw-bold">22</div><div id="spark1"></div></div>
  <div class="kit-kpi"><div class="kit-mute">Refuellings</div><div class="kit-fs-3 kit-fw-bold">5</div><div id="spark2"></div></div>
</div>
```

## Bar and line options

| Option | Values | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `data` | array of `{ label, group?, values: [n, …] }` | – |
| `series` | array of `{ name, color? }` | one "Total" series |
| `label` | description for screen reader users | `Bar chart` |
| `format` | function for the values in tooltips | number with the page language's separators |
| `axisFormat` | function for the axis values | abbreviation with "k" and "M" |
| `height` · `ticks` · `minSlot` | height in px, number of lines, minimum width of a column in px | `260` · `4` · `34` |
| `max` | maximum value of the axis | computed from the data, rounded |
| `legend` · `legendNote` | `true`/`false` · text added to the legend | legend only with several series |
| `stacked` | (bars) stacked series | `false` |
| `area` · `markers` · `zero` | (lines) colored area · points · axis from zero | `false` · `true` · `false` |
| `min` | minimum value of the axis | 0 for bars, computed for lines |
| `scrollEnd` | starts from the last bar when scrolling | `true` |
| `onSelect` | `(elemento, indice, serie) => …` | none: bars are not clickable |
| `empty` | text if `data` is empty | `No data` |

The function returns `{ update(options), destroy() }`. Calling it again on the same element updates the existing chart: `Kit.barChart(el, { data: newData })` changes only the data. Negative values are not supported in bars (they are drawn as zero). All four functions (`barChart`, `lineChart`, `donut`, `sparkline`) work this way and return `{ update, destroy }`.

The `kit-chart` class is added by itself. For the rest the tokens are used: `--kit-c1`…`--kit-c4` for the series, `--kit-line` for the grid and `--kit-mute` for the labels. The `kit-chart-bar`, `kit-chart-axis`, `kit-chart-label` and `kit-chart-group` classes let you touch up the single parts.

---

# Dates and times
Page: https://n1k1tas95.github.io/dashboard-kit/en/dates.html

Date and time fields with the kit's look, an optional calendar for a date, a range, date and time, and time only. Designed for the phone: on narrow screens the calendar slides up from the bottom, with 44-pixel targets.

## Native fields

`.kit-input` also works on `date`, `time`, `datetime-local`, `month` and `week`: the same height, border and focus ring as the other fields, aligned numbers and, on iOS, left-aligned text and the right height even when the field is empty. No JavaScript is needed: the picker is the browser's, which on a phone is usually the best. Min and max (`min`, `max`) and `aria-invalid="true"` work as for the other fields.

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-fields">
  <label class="kit-field">Date <input class="kit-input" type="date" value="2026-11-12"></label>
  <label class="kit-field">Time <input class="kit-input" type="time" value="09:30"></label>
  <label class="kit-field">Date and time <input class="kit-input" type="datetime-local" value="2026-11-12T09:30"></label>
  <label class="kit-field">Month <input class="kit-input" type="month" value="2026-11"></label>
  <label class="kit-field">Week <input class="kit-input" type="week" value="2026-W46"></label>
  <label class="kit-field">Invalid date <input class="kit-input" type="date" aria-invalid="true" value="2026-11-12"><small class="kit-danger">The date cannot be in the past.</small></label>
</div>
```

For a range without JavaScript a `kit-daterange` container with two fields is enough: they sit in a single frame, separated by a line.

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-field" style="max-width: 340px">
  <span>Period (browser picker)</span>
  <div class="kit-daterange"><input class="kit-input" type="date" aria-label="From" value="2026-11-01"><input class="kit-input" type="date" aria-label="To" value="2026-11-30"></div>
</div>
```

## Calendar

With `data-kit-datepicker` on the field (needs `kit.js`) the browser's picker gives way to a calendar that is the same everywhere. It is optional: without the attribute the field stays native, and without JavaScript the one with the attribute stays a normal `type="date"`.
- The field shows and accepts **mm/dd/yyyy** (the order follows the page's [language](https://n1k1tas95.github.io/dashboard-kit/en/javascript.html#languages): in Italian it is **dd/mm/yyyy**). You can also type it: the slashes are added by themselves and `3/5/26`, `03.05.2026`, `03052026`, `2026-03-05` all work.
- The value sent with the form is always **yyyy-mm-dd**, in a hidden field that takes the `name`: the server reads it without conversions.
- It opens with the calendar button or the down arrow. On a phone you just tap the field (the keyboard does not appear).
- The month title leads to the months, and the year title to the years: useful for birth dates.

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-fields">
  <label class="kit-field">Issue date <input class="kit-input" type="date" name="emissione" value="2026-11-12" data-kit-datepicker></label>
  <label class="kit-field">Due date <input class="kit-input" type="date" name="scadenza" data-kit-datepicker required><small data-doc-out>Value: –</small></label>
</div>
```

On change the field's `input` and `change` events fire (so htmx's `hx-trigger="change"` works too) and `kit:change` with `{ value, display }`: `value` in ISO, `display` as written in the field.

### Limits and excluded days

`min` and `max` (or `data-kit-min` and `data-kit-max`) set the allowed range. Besides the ISO date they accept `today` and an offset in days: `+30` is in thirty days, `-7` a week ago. `data-kit-disable` excludes days of the week (`mon`… `sun`) and specific dates. Excluded days are visible but cannot be chosen; if the date is typed by hand the field is invalid (`setCustomValidity`, so the form does not submit) and gets the red border.

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-fields">
  <label class="kit-field">Delivery (from today, Monday to Friday)
    <input class="kit-input" type="date" name="consegna" data-kit-datepicker data-kit-min="today" data-kit-max="+90" data-kit-disable="sat,sun,2026-12-25,2026-12-26">
    <small>Within 90 days, excluding Saturday, Sunday and Christmas.</small></label>
  <label class="kit-field">Date of birth
    <input class="kit-input" type="date" name="nascita" data-kit-datepicker max="today">
    <small>For distant years: month title, then year title.</small></label>
</div>
```

## Range

`data-kit-daterange` on a container with two `<input type="date">` (from, to). The calendar shows two months side by side, with a colored band between the two dates; while choosing the second one, hovering over the days shows a preview. You can also type the dates in the two fields. If "to" precedes "from" the field is invalid. The quick choices are on the left (on a phone they become a scrolling row above the calendar); `data-kit-presets` chooses which ones (`none` removes them).

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-field" style="max-width: 360px">
  <span>Period</span>
  <div class="kit-daterange" data-kit-daterange data-kit-presets="today,7,30,month,last-month">
    <input class="kit-input" type="date" name="dal" aria-label="From" value="2026-11-01">
    <input class="kit-input" type="date" name="al" aria-label="To" value="2026-11-12">
  </div>
  <small data-doc-out>Value: 2026-11-01 → 2026-11-12</small>
</div>
```

The available choices are `today`, `yesterday`, `7`, `30`, `90` (last N days), `month`, `last-month`, `year`, `last-year` (the old Italian names `oggi`, `ieri`, `mese`, `mese-scorso`, `anno`, `anno-scorso` still work). By default `7,30,month,last-month,year`. Those that fall outside `min` and `max` are shortened, or disabled if they stay entirely outside. The `kit:change` event has `{ from, to }`, and `input` and `change` fire on both fields.

## Date and time

On a `type="datetime-local"` the calendar has hour and minute columns next to it. The field shows **mm/dd/yyyy hh:mm** and sends `yyyy-mm-ddThh:mm`, like the native field. "Done" closes. If you only choose the time, the date becomes today; if you only choose the day, the time is 00:00. `data-kit-step="15"` (minutes) limits the minutes to multiples of 15; the `step` attribute in seconds works too.

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-fields">
  <label class="kit-field">Appointment <input class="kit-input" type="datetime-local" name="appuntamento" value="2026-11-12T09:30" data-kit-datepicker data-kit-step="15"><small data-doc-out>Value: 2026-11-12T09:30</small></label>
</div>
```

## Time only

On a `type="time"` (or with `data-kit-timepicker`) you choose hours and minutes in two columns. You can also type `9`, `9.30`, `930`. The value is `hh:mm` in 24 hours, the same as the native field. `min` and `max` count as times (`09:00`, `18:00`).

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-fields">
  <label class="kit-field">Opening <input class="kit-input" type="time" name="apertura" value="09:00" data-kit-timepicker data-kit-step="5" min="06:00" max="22:00"><small data-doc-out>Value: 09:00</small></label>
</div>
```

## Phone and touch
- Below 576 px the calendar becomes a **bottom sheet**, full width, with a darkened backdrop and a "Close" button; the backdrop edge or Esc closes it. The page below does not scroll.
- With a "coarse" pointer (fingers) days, months and hours are 44 px tall, even on a tablet.
- The field does not open the keyboard (`inputmode="none"`): a tap opens the calendar. With a mouse it stays a numeric field to type in.
- The field's text is at least 16 px, so iOS does not zoom the page.
- The calendar is in the page's top layer (`popover`): no card, scrolling table or dialog clips it.
- If you prefer the system picker for phones, do not add `data-kit-datepicker` and use the native field: its look is already the kit's.

Example markup:

```html
<button class="kit-btn" data-kit-open="#dlg-date">Date fields inside a dialog</button>
<dialog class="kit-dialog" id="dlg-date" aria-labelledby="dlg-date-t">
  <div class="kit-card-head"><h3 id="dlg-date-t">New appointment</h3></div>
  <div class="kit-card-body">
    <div class="kit-fields">
      <label class="kit-field">Day <input class="kit-input" type="date" data-kit-datepicker></label>
      <label class="kit-field">Time <input class="kit-input" type="time" data-kit-timepicker></label>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="kit-card-foot"><button class="kit-btn" data-kit-close>Close</button></div>
</dialog>
```

## Keyboard

| Where | Keys |
|---|---|
| Field | ↓ opens the calendar; you can type the date. Tab leaves the field. |
| Days | ← → one day, ↑ ↓ one week, Home and End start and end of the week, PageUp and PageDown one month, Shift + PageUp/PageDown one year. Enter or Space choose. |
| Months and years | Arrows to move, Enter to choose. |
| Hours and minutes | ↑ ↓ in the column, ← → from one column to the other, Home and End for the first and the last. |
| Open calendar | Esc closes and returns focus to the field. Tab goes through the controls and leaves from the last one. |

## Attributes and options

| Attribute | JS option | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `data-kit-datepicker` | `type` | Calendar on the field. The type (`date`, `datetime`, `time`) is read from `type="date\|datetime-local\|time"`; on a text field you write the value: `data-kit-datepicker="datetime"`. |
| `data-kit-timepicker` | – | As above, for time only. |
| `data-kit-daterange` | – | On a container with two date fields (from, to). |
| `min`, `max` (or `data-kit-min`, `-max`) | `min`, `max` on the field | Limits: ISO, `today`, `+N` or `-N` days; for times `hh:mm`. |
| `data-kit-disable` | `disable` | Excluded days: `sat,sun,2026-12-25`; from JavaScript also a function `(iso) => true`. |
| `data-kit-step` or `step` | `step` | Minutes step (1–30). 1 by default. |
| `data-kit-presets` | `presets` | Quick choices for the range (a list, or `none`). |
| `required` | – | The field is required and the calendar does not offer "Clear". |

## With Django and htmx

The visible field has no `name`: the hidden one has it, and it contains the ISO date. So `request.GET["dal"]` and `cleaned_data` receive `2026-11-12`, with no formats to configure.

```python
# forms.py — format="%Y-%m-%d" lets the native field (without JavaScript) show the initial value
class PeriodForm(forms.Form):
    dal = forms.DateField(required=False, widget=forms.DateInput(
        format="%Y-%m-%d", attrs={"type": "date", "class": "kit-input", "aria-label": "From"}))
    al = forms.DateField(required=False, widget=forms.DateInput(
        format="%Y-%m-%d", attrs={"type": "date", "class": "kit-input", "aria-label": "To"}))
```

```html
<form hx-get="{% url 'invoices' %}" hx-target="#results" hx-trigger="change">
  <div class="kit-daterange" data-kit-daterange>{{ form.dal }}{{ form.al }}</div>
</form>
```
- With htmx put `hx-get` and `hx-trigger="change"` on the **form** (or a container), not on the single field: the hidden field is in the form and gets included. The `change` event fires after every choice, with the value already updated. On a single field, `hx-include` names the other one.
- The fragments htmx inserts initialize by themselves (`htmx:load`); also with `hx-swap="outerHTML"` on the form.
- With django-filter, `DateFromToRangeFilter` and `RangeWidget(attrs={"type": "date", "class": "kit-input"})` produce two fields in a row, suited to `kit-daterange`.
- A server error on a field: add `aria-invalid="true"` and the message in `<small class="kit-danger">`, as for the other fields.

## JavaScript

```js
const field = Kit.datepicker("#due");                    // returns { get, set, clear, open, close }
field.set("2026-12-31");                                  // without an event (set(v, true) fires it)
field.get();                                              // "2026-12-31"

const period = Kit.daterange("#period", { presets: ["today", "7", "month"] });
period.set({ from: "2026-11-01", to: "2026-11-12" });
period.get();                                             // { from, to }

Kit.date.parse("3/5/26");                                 // "2026-03-05" ("" if empty, null if not a date; the order depends on the language)
Kit.date.format("2026-03-05");                            // "03/05/2026"
Kit.i18n.add("en", { date: { t: { today: "Now" } } });    // texts and month names can be replaced (see Languages)

document.addEventListener("kit:change", (e) => {
  console.log(e.detail);                                  // { value, display } or { from, to }
});
```

Dates are ISO strings and calculations are done in UTC, so the browser's time zone never shifts a day. "Today" is the device's local date.

---

# Alerts and progress
Page: https://n1k1tas95.github.io/dashboard-kit/en/feedback.html

Alerts, status badges, progress bars, empty states and a welcome screen.

## Alerts

A highlighted message inside the page: colored left border and soft background. Without a variant it is information; the others are `-success`, `-warning`, `-danger` and `-neutral`.

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-alert" role="status">Imported invoices stay on your computer.</div>
<div class="kit-alert kit-alert-success" role="status">Import completed: 24 invoices added.</div>
<div class="kit-alert kit-alert-warning" role="status">3 invoices are waiting for a receipt from the tax authority.</div>
<div class="kit-alert kit-alert-danger" role="alert">Unable to read the file: it is not a valid invoice.</div>
<div class="kit-alert kit-alert-neutral">Last updated: today at 09:41.</div>
```

### With an icon

Put a `<svg class="kit-icon kit-alert-icon">` as the first child: the alert leaves room on the left and the icon takes the variant's color. Icons come from your SVG sprite; here `i-info`, `i-ok`, `i-warn` and `i-error` (you will find them in this documentation's sprite).

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-alert" role="status"><svg class="kit-icon kit-alert-icon"><use href="#i-info"/></svg>Imported invoices stay on your computer.</div>
<div class="kit-alert kit-alert-success" role="status"><svg class="kit-icon kit-alert-icon"><use href="#i-ok"/></svg>Import completed: 24 invoices added.</div>
<div class="kit-alert kit-alert-warning" role="status"><svg class="kit-icon kit-alert-icon"><use href="#i-warn"/></svg>3 invoices are waiting for a receipt from the tax authority.</div>
<div class="kit-alert kit-alert-danger" role="alert"><svg class="kit-icon kit-alert-icon"><use href="#i-error"/></svg>Unable to read the file: it is not a valid invoice.</div>
```

For an important alert use `role="alert"` (it is read immediately by screen readers), for the others `role="status"`.

### With a title and a link

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-alert kit-alert-warning" role="status">
  <svg class="kit-icon kit-alert-icon"><use href="#i-warn"/></svg>
  <strong class="kit-alert-title">Deadline approaching</strong>
  You have until the 30th of the month. <a href="#alerts">Go to the invoices to send</a>.
</div>
```

### Dismissible

A `.kit-alert-close` button with `data-kit-dismiss` removes the alert. The `kit:dismiss` event bubbles up from the container, if you need to know.

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-alert kit-alert-success" role="status">
  Saved. You can close this message.
  <button class="kit-alert-close" data-kit-dismiss aria-label="Close"><svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-x"/></svg></button>
</div>
```

Color is not enough on its own: the alert's text must explain what happened.

## Badge

Status labels. Color conveys the outcome: green positive, yellow needs checking, red error, gray neutral.

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-bar">
  <span class="kit-badge">Info</span>
  <span class="kit-badge kit-badge-success">Issued</span>
  <span class="kit-badge kit-badge-warning">Received</span>
  <span class="kit-badge kit-badge-danger">Error</span>
  <span class="kit-badge kit-badge-neutral">Neutral</span>
</div>
```

Do not rely on color alone for meaning: the badge's text must be enough on its own.

## Progress bar

Progress is the `--kit-value` variable (0–100%) on the inner element. Change it from JavaScript with `el.style.setProperty("--kit-value", "40%")`.

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-progress"><i style="--kit-value: 25%"></i></div>
<div class="kit-progress"><i style="--kit-value: 62%"></i></div>
<div class="kit-progress"><i style="--kit-value: 100%"></i></div>
```

## Meter

A measure against a limit: space used, plan quota, score. It differs from the [progress bar](#progress) because it is not heading toward completion: the value is what it is, and the color says whether the level is fine (`is-success`), needs attention (`is-warning`) or is critical (`is-danger`). Without a state class the bar is in the accent color. As with the native `<meter>` element, it has `role="meter"` and its `aria-valuenow`, `-min` and `-max`; the accessible label is `aria-label`.

CSS only (fine for server-side rendering): the width is `--kit-value` and you choose the state. `kit-meter-head` puts name and value above the bar.

Example markup:

```html
<div>
  <div class="kit-meter-head"><span>Storage</span><b>32 GB of 100</b></div>
  <div class="kit-meter is-success" role="meter" aria-label="Storage" aria-valuenow="32" aria-valuemin="0" aria-valuemax="100" style="--kit-value: 32%"><i></i></div>
</div>
<div>
  <div class="kit-meter-head"><span>Requests this month</span><b>430 of 500</b></div>
  <div class="kit-meter is-warning" role="meter" aria-label="Requests this month" aria-valuenow="430" aria-valuemin="0" aria-valuemax="500" style="--kit-value: 86%"><i></i></div>
</div>
<div>
  <div class="kit-meter-head"><span>Seats taken</span><b>48 of 50</b></div>
  <div class="kit-meter is-danger" role="meter" aria-label="Seats taken" aria-valuenow="48" aria-valuemin="0" aria-valuemax="50" style="--kit-value: 96%"><i></i></div>
</div>
```

With `kit.js` just give the value and thresholds and the state is computed by itself. The attributes are `data-kit-value`, `data-kit-min` (0), `data-kit-max` (100), `data-kit-warn` and `data-kit-danger`, in the same unit as the value. By default higher is worse: from `warn` up it is orange, from `danger` up red, below it is green. With `data-kit-good="high"` (a score, a coverage) it reads the other way round: up to `warn` orange, up to `danger` red. Without thresholds it stays in the accent color. Meters inside a fragment inserted by htmx also set themselves up. Sizes: `kit-meter-sm` and `kit-meter-lg`.

Example markup:

```html
<div>
  <div class="kit-meter-head"><span>Disk</span><b>78 GB</b></div>
  <div class="kit-meter" data-kit-meter data-kit-value="78" data-kit-max="100" data-kit-warn="80" data-kit-danger="95" aria-label="Disk"><i></i></div>
</div>
<div>
  <div class="kit-meter-head"><span>Test coverage</span><b>45 %</b></div>
  <div class="kit-meter kit-meter-lg" data-kit-meter data-kit-value="45" data-kit-good="high" data-kit-warn="70" data-kit-danger="50" aria-label="Test coverage"><i></i></div>
</div>
<div>
  <div class="kit-meter-head"><span>Room</span><b>12 / 40</b></div>
  <div class="kit-meter kit-meter-sm" data-kit-meter data-kit-value="12" data-kit-max="40" aria-label="Room"><i></i></div>
</div>
```

`Kit.meter(element, options)` accepts the same things as options (`value`, `min`, `max`, `warn`, `danger`, `good`) and returns `{ set(value), value(), state() }`; `set()` updates width, ARIA and color, `state()` gives `"success"`, `"warning"`, `"danger"` or `null`.

Do not rely on color alone for the level: also write the value (with `kit-meter-head` or next to the bar), so it is understood even without telling colors apart.

## Spinner

A spinning ring, in the text color and as big as the font: inside a button or next to a sentence nothing else is needed. `kit-spinner-sm` and `-lg` change the size, `kit-spinner-accent` uses the accent color. Add `role="status"` and an `aria-label`, or text next to it, so that screen reader users know something is loading.

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-bar">
  <span class="kit-spinner kit-spinner-accent" role="status" aria-label="Loading"></span>
  <span class="kit-spinner kit-spinner-lg kit-spinner-accent" role="status" aria-label="Loading"></span>
  <button class="kit-btn kit-btn-primary" disabled><span class="kit-spinner kit-spinner-sm"></span> Importing…</button>
  <span class="kit-mute"><span class="kit-spinner kit-spinner-sm"></span> Loading documents…</span>
</div>
```

## Skeleton

Placeholders with a moving shine, to reserve space while data arrives. Put `aria-busy="true"` on the container and `aria-hidden="true"` on the placeholders, which are purely decorative. Parts: `kit-skeleton-text` (a line of text, the last one shorter), `-title`, `-circle` and `-block`.

Example markup:

```html
<section class="kit-card" aria-busy="true">
  <div class="kit-card-body kit-d-flex kit-gap-3" style="align-items:flex-start">
    <span class="kit-skeleton kit-skeleton-circle" aria-hidden="true"></span>
    <div style="flex:1;min-width:0">
      <div class="kit-skeleton kit-skeleton-title" aria-hidden="true"></div>
      <div class="kit-skeleton kit-skeleton-text" aria-hidden="true"></div>
      <div class="kit-skeleton kit-skeleton-text" aria-hidden="true"></div>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>
```

## Full-screen progress

For a long operation (reading a folder, importing a file) that blocks the rest of the page. `Kit.progress(text, options)` opens a dialog with the text and the bar and returns `{ update(text, value), close() }`. The value goes from 0 to 1; without a value (`null`) the bar runs by itself, for when you do not know how much is left. Esc and a click on the background do not close it: you close it with `close()`, or with `onCancel` a "Cancel" button appears (and Esc counts as Cancel). With `delay` (in ms) it appears only if the operation lasts longer than that, so quick operations do not flash.

Example markup:

```html
 Kit.toast("Reading cancelled") });
for (let i = 1; i &lt;= 40; i++) {
  await readInvoice(i);
  p.update("Reading " + i + " of 40", i / 40);
}
p.close();'>
  <button class="kit-btn" data-doc-run="progress-bar">With progress</button>
  <button class="kit-btn" data-doc-run="progress-indet">Without a value</button>
```

| Option | Values | Default |
|---|---|---|
| 1st argument | the text above the bar | empty |
| `value` | from 0 to 1, or `null` for the running bar | `null` |
| `delay` | milliseconds before showing it | `0` |
| `onCancel` · `cancel` | function called if the user cancels · button text | none: it cannot be cancelled · `Cancel` |

## Empty state

When a list or table has nothing to show yet, explain why and what to do.

Example markup:

```html
<section class="kit-card">
  <div class="kit-empty">
    <div class="kit-empty-icon">🗂️</div>
    <h2>No results</h2>
    <p>Try changing the filters or searching for another term.</p>
    <button class="kit-btn">Clear filters</button>
  </div>
</section>
```

## Welcome screen

`kit-hero` centers a message with a few buttons: the first screen when there is no data yet.

Example markup:

```html
<section class="kit-card kit-hero">
  <h2>Explore your data</h2>
  <p class="kit-mute">Open a file to get started. Nothing leaves your computer.</p>
  <button class="kit-btn kit-btn-primary kit-btn-lg">Open a file…</button>
</section>
```

---

# Forms: select and file
Page: https://n1k1tas95.github.io/dashboard-kit/en/form-controls.html

Custom select, file field, drop zone and combobox: the controls that need `kit.js`.

## Custom select

A dropdown menu with items, groups and a second line of text. It needs `kit.js`. On change the `kit:change` event fires (see [JavaScript](https://n1k1tas95.github.io/dashboard-kit/en/javascript.html#events)). For a plain `<select>` just use `class="kit-input"`.

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-field" style="max-width: 280px">
  <span>Period</span>
  <div class="kit-select" data-kit-select>
    <button type="button" class="kit-select-btn"><span class="kit-select-value"></span><svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-chev"/></svg></button>
    <div class="kit-pop" hidden>
      <div class="kit-pop-group">Quarters</div>
      <div class="kit-opt is-on" data-value="q1"><span class="kit-opt-text"><b>1st quarter</b></span><svg class="kit-icon kit-opt-check"><use href="#i-check"/></svg></div>
      <div class="kit-opt" data-value="q2"><span class="kit-opt-text"><b>2nd quarter</b><small>April – June</small></span><svg class="kit-icon kit-opt-check"><use href="#i-check"/></svg></div>
      <div class="kit-opt" data-value="q3"><span class="kit-opt-text"><b>3rd quarter</b></span><svg class="kit-icon kit-opt-check"><use href="#i-check"/></svg></div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <small data-doc-out>Value: q1</small>
</div>
```

The option with `is-on` is the initial one. `kit-pop-right` on the panel aligns it to the right of the button.

### From a native select

If the data is already in a `<select>` (even one generated by the server, inside a form, with `required`) just add `data-kit-select` to it: the kit hides it and puts a button and menu next to it. The `<select>` stays the source of the data: `value`, form submission and the `change` event work as usual (`kit:change` also fires, with `{ value, label }`). Use `<optgroup>` for groups; `data-kit-hint` on an option adds a second line and `data-kit-short` a shorter text for the button. From 21 items up the menu has a search field (`data-kit-search="8"` changes the threshold, `data-kit-search=""` always shows it, `data-kit-search="off"` never). Options and `disabled` can be changed later: the kit notices.

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-field" style="max-width: 280px">
  <label for="sel-nat">Document type</label>
  <select id="sel-nat" data-kit-select>
    <optgroup label="Invoices">
      <option value="TD01" selected data-kit-hint="Invoice">TD01</option>
      <option value="TD04" data-kit-hint="Credit note">TD04</option>
    </optgroup>
    <optgroup label="Other">
      <option value="TD16" data-kit-hint="Integration">TD16</option>
      <option value="TD99" disabled>Not available</option>
    </optgroup>
  </select>
  <small data-doc-out>Value: TD01</small>
</div>
```

From JavaScript: `Kit.select(el, { search, empty, placeholder })` does the same for a select added later (`Kit.init(root)` does it for all those inside `root`) and returns `{ sync(), open(), close() }`. If you change `select.value` from code, call `sync()` to update the button (a `change` fired by hand already does).

## File field

A field to choose one or more files: a button, the name of the chosen file and an "×" to remove it. It needs `kit.js` (without it, the browser's native field stays). Write a normal `<input type="file">` inside `kit-file` with `data-kit-file`; `accept` and `multiple` work as usual. The kit checks the type and, with `data-kit-file-max` (in MB), the size, and shows the error below the field. The files also stay in the form's field, so normal submission works.

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-field" style="max-width: 440px">
  <span>Invoices</span>
  <div class="kit-file" data-kit-file data-kit-file-max="2">
    <input type="file" accept=".xml,.p7m" multiple aria-label="Invoices">
  </div>
  <small data-doc-out>Accepts XML and P7M, up to 2 MB each.</small>
</div>
```

## Drop zone

The same thing, bigger: an area where you drag files, or click to choose. The native field covers the whole area, so the keyboard works (Tab and Enter). With `data-kit-file-dir` (or `webkitdirectory` on the field) it also accepts folders, which are read in full: files of another type are silently ignored, while a file of another type chosen directly gives an error. With `data-kit-file-page` you can drop anywhere on the page: while dragging, a veil appears with the given text.

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-dropzone" data-kit-file data-kit-file-dir data-kit-file-max="2">
  <svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-upload"/></svg>
  <b>Drag the invoices or a folder here</b>
  <span>or <u>choose from your computer</u></span>
  <small>XML or P7M, up to 2 MB each</small>
  <input type="file" accept=".xml,.p7m" multiple aria-label="Invoices">
</div>
<p class="kit-mute" data-doc-out style="margin-top: 8px">No file.</p>
```

When the files change the element receives `kit:files` with `{ files, items, rejected }`: `files` are the accepted `File`s, `items` pairs them with the path (`{ file, path }`, useful for folders) and `rejected` lists the discarded ones with the reason (`type`, `size`, `count`, `folder`). You can also pass `onFiles` to `Kit.file(element, options)`.

| Option | Attribute | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `accept` · `multiple` | those of the `<input>` field | any file, only one |
| `max` | `data-kit-file-max` (MB) | no limit |
| `directory` | `data-kit-file-dir` or `webkitdirectory` | folders not allowed |
| – | `data-kit-file-page="text"` on the zone | none: you only drop on the zone |
| `empty` · `button` · `clearLabel` | `data-kit-file-empty` · `-button` · `-clear` | from the [language](https://n1k1tas95.github.io/dashboard-kit/en/javascript.html#languages) dictionary (`No file` · `Choose file…` · `Remove selection`) |
| `messages` | – | error texts, with `{name}`, `{accept}` and `{max}` |

`Kit.file` returns `{ files(), items(), clear() }`.

## Combobox

A text field with a list of suggestions that narrows as you type. Unlike the [select](#select) you can also type a value that is not in the list. It needs `kit.js`. Up and down arrows move through the items, Enter chooses the highlighted one (on opening it is the first), Esc closes, Tab leaves. Choosing writes the value into the field and fires `input` and `kit:change` (`{ value, label }`).

Items are written in the HTML, as `kit-opt` inside a `kit-pop`; the button with the arrow is added automatically.

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-field" style="max-width: 320px">
  <span>Tax regime</span>
  <div class="kit-combo" data-kit-combo>
    <input class="kit-input" placeholder="Type or choose…" aria-label="Tax regime">
    <div class="kit-pop" hidden>
      <div class="kit-opt" data-value="RF01"><span class="kit-opt-text"><b>RF01</b><small>Ordinary</small></span></div>
      <div class="kit-opt" data-value="RF02"><span class="kit-opt-text"><b>RF02</b><small>Minimum taxpayers</small></span></div>
      <div class="kit-opt" data-value="RF19"><span class="kit-opt-text"><b>RF19</b><small>Flat rate</small></span></div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <small data-doc-out>Value: –</small>
</div>
```

For a long list, or one computed from data, use `Kit.combo`. `items` is an array (or a function returning one) of strings or of `{ value, label, hint }` objects. The filter searches label, note and value; if there are more than `max` items it shows `max` and invites you to keep typing.

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-field" style="max-width: 320px">
  <span>Customer (240 items, shows 8)</span>
  <div id="cliente"><input class="kit-input" placeholder="Search a customer…" aria-label="Customer"></div>
  <small data-doc-out>Value: –</small>
</div>
```

| Option | Attribute | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `items` | (JavaScript only) array, or a function that receives the typed text | the `kit-opt`s already in the HTML |
| `max` | `data-kit-combo-max` | `50` |
| `empty` | `data-kit-combo-empty` | `No results` (`""` to show nothing) |
| `more` | `data-kit-combo-more` | `{n} more results: keep typing to narrow down` |
| `filter` | – | `true`; with `false` the `items` function filters by itself (useful to search on a server) |
| `autoActive` | – | `true`: Enter chooses the first item; with `false` an arrow is needed first |

`Kit.combo` returns `{ setItems(list), open(), close() }`. The field has `role="combobox"` and `aria-activedescendant`; the items have `role="option"`.

---

# Forms: layout and validation
Page: https://n1k1tas95.github.io/dashboard-kit/en/form-layout.html

Labels, help text, required fields, column, grid, horizontal and sectioned forms, valid and invalid states with messages, automatic validation, sizes, icons inside fields, field groups, floating labels, card-style checkboxes and the other controls.

## Labels, help and required fields

A field is a `.kit-field`: it can be a `<label>` wrapping the input (as on the [Forms: basic fields](https://n1k1tas95.github.io/dashboard-kit/en/forms.html) page) or a `<div>` with a `<label class="kit-label" for="…">` and the input next to it. The second form is needed when there are help text and messages below the field, and for the horizontal layout; it is also the one Django generates. `.kit-hint` is the help text, linked to the field with `aria-describedby`.

`.kit-required` on the label adds the red asterisk; `.kit-optional` adds "(optional)", which you change with `--kit-optional-text`. The field's `required` attribute remains what counts for the browser and the server.

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-fields">
  <div class="kit-field">
    <label class="kit-label kit-required" for="fl-mail">Email</label>
    <input class="kit-input" id="fl-mail" type="email" placeholder="name@company.com" required aria-describedby="fl-mail-h">
    <div class="kit-hint" id="fl-mail-h">We only write to you for the confirmation.</div>
  </div>
  <div class="kit-field">
    <label class="kit-label kit-optional" for="fl-tel">Phone</label>
    <input class="kit-input" id="fl-tel" type="tel" placeholder="+1 …">
    <div class="kit-hint">With the international prefix.</div>
  </div>
</div>
```

## Layout

### Column and grid

`.kit-form` puts the fields in a column with the kit's spacing (`--kit-sp`). For several fields on the same row there are two ways: `.kit-fields` (an adaptive grid, `kit-field-wide` takes two columns) or the [12-column grid](https://n1k1tas95.github.io/dashboard-kit/en/grid.html) with `.kit-row` and `.kit-col-*`, as in Bootstrap, to decide the width of each field and where they wrap.

Example markup:

```html
<form class="kit-form">
  <div class="kit-row">
    <div class="kit-col-12 kit-col-md-6"><div class="kit-field"><label class="kit-label" for="g-nome">First name</label><input class="kit-input" id="g-nome" placeholder="Jane"></div></div>
    <div class="kit-col-12 kit-col-md-6"><div class="kit-field"><label class="kit-label" for="g-cogn">Last name</label><input class="kit-input" id="g-cogn" placeholder="Smith"></div></div>
    <div class="kit-col-12"><div class="kit-field"><label class="kit-label" for="g-ind">Address</label><input class="kit-input" id="g-ind" placeholder="Street, number"></div></div>
    <div class="kit-col-6 kit-col-md-5"><div class="kit-field"><label class="kit-label" for="g-cit">City</label><input class="kit-input" id="g-cit"></div></div>
    <div class="kit-col-6 kit-col-md-4"><div class="kit-field"><label class="kit-label" for="g-pr">Country</label><select class="kit-input" id="g-pr"><option>Italy</option><option>France</option><option>Spain</option></select></div></div>
    <div class="kit-col-12 kit-col-md-3"><div class="kit-field"><label class="kit-label" for="g-cap">Postal code</label><input class="kit-input" id="g-cap" inputmode="numeric" placeholder="20100"></div></div>
  </div>
</form>
```

### Horizontal

`.kit-form-h` on the form (or `.kit-field-h` on a single field) puts the label on the left and the field, help and messages on the right. The label width is `--kit-label-w` (`11rem`). Below 576 px the fields go back to a column. It needs the form with `<div class="kit-field">` and `.kit-label`.

Example markup:

```html
<form class="kit-form kit-form-h">
  <div class="kit-field"><label class="kit-label" for="h-rag">Company name</label><input class="kit-input" id="h-rag" value="Smith Ltd"></div>
  <div class="kit-field"><label class="kit-label" for="h-iva">VAT number</label><input class="kit-input" id="h-iva" value="01234567890"><div class="kit-hint">11 digits, without the IT prefix.</div></div>
  <div class="kit-field"><label class="kit-label" for="h-note">Notes</label><textarea class="kit-input" id="h-note" rows="3"></textarea></div>
  <div class="kit-form-foot kit-form-foot-end"><button type="button" class="kit-btn">Cancel</button><button type="button" class="kit-btn kit-btn-primary">Save</button></div>
</form>
```

### Inline

`.kit-form-inline` aligns fields and buttons on one row that wraps by itself: for filters and searches.

Example markup:

```html
<form class="kit-form-inline">
  <div class="kit-field"><label class="kit-label" for="i-q">Search</label><input class="kit-input" id="i-q" placeholder="Number or customer"></div>
  <div class="kit-field"><label class="kit-label" for="i-st">Status</label><select class="kit-input" id="i-st"><option>All</option><option>Paid</option><option>Unpaid</option></select></div>
  <button type="button" class="kit-btn kit-btn-primary">Filter</button>
</form>
```

### Sections and groups

`.kit-form-section` divides a long form into blocks, with a title and explanation on the left and the fields on the right (from 768 px; below that they stack). To group related fields, or radios, use `<fieldset class="kit-fieldset">` with the `<legend>`: a `disabled` on the fieldset disables the whole group.

Example markup:

```html
<form class="kit-form">
  <section class="kit-form-section">
    <div><h3 class="kit-form-section-title">Profile</h3><p class="kit-form-section-desc">How other users see you.</p></div>
    <div class="kit-form-section-body">
      <div class="kit-field"><label class="kit-label" for="s-nome">Display name</label><input class="kit-input" id="s-nome" value="Jane S."></div>
      <div class="kit-field"><label class="kit-label" for="s-bio">Bio</label><textarea class="kit-input" id="s-bio" rows="3" maxlength="120"></textarea><div class="kit-field-foot"><span class="kit-hint">One line about you.</span><span class="kit-counter" data-kit-count="#s-bio"></span></div></div>
    </div>
  </section>
  <section class="kit-form-section">
    <div><h3 class="kit-form-section-title">Notifications</h3><p class="kit-form-section-desc">When to get an email.</p></div>
    <div class="kit-form-section-body">
      <fieldset class="kit-fieldset">
        <legend>Notify me when</legend>
        <label class="kit-check"><input type="checkbox" checked> an invoice arrives</label>
        <label class="kit-check"><input type="checkbox"> an invoice is due</label>
      </fieldset>
    </div>
  </section>
</form>
```

## States: valid, invalid, warning

`is-valid`, `is-invalid` and `is-warning` go on the field, or on its `.kit-field`, and apply to everything it contains: border, focus ring and, for groups, all the parts. `aria-invalid="true"` counts as `is-invalid` (and is needed by screen readers). The message is a `.kit-feedback` with `-valid`, `-invalid` or `-warning`, which can be preceded by an icon. The states also work on select, combobox, file field, drop zone and date range.

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-fields">
  <div class="kit-field is-valid">
    <label class="kit-label" for="st-ok">Customer code</label>
    <input class="kit-input" id="st-ok" value="CL-2041">
    <div class="kit-feedback kit-feedback-valid"><svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-check"/></svg>Code available.</div>
  </div>
  <div class="kit-field is-invalid">
    <label class="kit-label" for="st-ko">Email</label>
    <input class="kit-input" id="st-ko" value="jane@" aria-invalid="true" aria-describedby="st-ko-m">
    <div class="kit-feedback kit-feedback-invalid" id="st-ko-m"><svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-error"/></svg>Enter a complete address.</div>
  </div>
  <div class="kit-field is-warning">
    <label class="kit-label" for="st-w">Price</label>
    <input class="kit-input" id="st-w" value="0.00">
    <div class="kit-feedback kit-feedback-warning"><svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-warn"/></svg>The price is zero.</div>
  </div>
</div>
```

With the classes on a `.kit-field` the other parts react too, with no extra markup:

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-fields">
  <div class="kit-field is-invalid">
    <span class="kit-label">Document type</span>
    <div class="kit-select" data-kit-select>
      <button type="button" class="kit-select-btn is-empty"><span class="kit-select-value">Choose…</span><svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-chev"/></svg></button>
      <div class="kit-pop" hidden><div class="kit-opt" data-value="a"><span class="kit-opt-text"><b>Invoice</b></span></div><div class="kit-opt" data-value="b"><span class="kit-opt-text"><b>Credit note</b></span></div></div>
    </div>
    <div class="kit-feedback kit-feedback-invalid">Choose a type.</div>
  </div>
  <div class="kit-field is-invalid">
    <span class="kit-label">Period</span>
    <div class="kit-daterange" data-kit-daterange><input class="kit-input" type="date" aria-label="From"><input class="kit-input" type="date" aria-label="To"></div>
    <div class="kit-feedback kit-feedback-invalid">Enter the period.</div>
  </div>
  <div class="kit-field is-invalid">
    <span class="kit-label">Terms</span>
    <label class="kit-check"><input type="checkbox"> I accept the terms of sale</label>
    <div class="kit-feedback kit-feedback-invalid">You must accept to continue.</div>
  </div>
</div>
```

For a CSS-only check after the user has touched the field, `class="kit-validate"` on the form uses `:user-invalid`: the border turns red (and with `kit-validate-ok` green) when the HTML rules are not met. It does not write messages: for those there is the validation below.

## Validation in the browser

`data-kit-validate` on a `<form>` (needs `kit.js`) checks the fields with the HTML rules you already know (`required`, `type="email"`, `pattern`, `min`, `max`, `minlength`…): on submit it marks `is-invalid`, writes the message into the `.kit-feedback-invalid` (creating it if missing), links the message to the field with `aria-describedby`, moves focus to the first error and blocks submission, htmx included. A field turns red on blur only if the user typed in it, and the error disappears as soon as the value is correct. With `data-kit-validate="ok"` the correct fields get `is-valid`.

The messages are the browser's (in its language). To write your own: `data-kit-msg` on the field for any error, or `data-kit-msg-required`, `-type`, `-pattern`, `-min`, `-max`, `-minlength`, `-maxlength`, `-step`. It works with the kit's fields: calendar (its `min`, `max` and excluded-days rules), select, checkboxes and radios, file.

Example markup:

```html
<form class="kit-form" data-kit-validate="ok" autocomplete="off">
  <div class="kit-field">
    <label class="kit-label kit-required" for="v-mail">Email</label>
    <input class="kit-input" id="v-mail" name="email" type="email" required data-kit-msg-required="Enter your email." data-kit-msg-type="Something is missing: name@domain.com">
    <div class="kit-feedback kit-feedback-valid">Perfect.</div>
  </div>
  <div class="kit-field">
    <label class="kit-label kit-required" for="v-pw">Password</label>
    <div class="kit-control">
      <input class="kit-input" id="v-pw" name="pw" type="password" required minlength="8" data-kit-msg-minlength="At least 8 characters." data-kit-msg-required="Choose a password.">
      <button type="button" class="kit-control-end" data-kit-password><svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-eye"/></svg></button>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="kit-field">
    <label class="kit-label kit-required" for="v-d">Delivery date</label>
    <input class="kit-input" id="v-d" type="date" required data-kit-datepicker data-kit-min="today" data-kit-msg-required="Choose the date.">
  </div>
  <div class="kit-field">
    <label class="kit-check"><input type="checkbox" name="cond" required data-kit-msg-required="You must accept to continue."> I accept the terms</label>
  </div>
  <div class="kit-form-foot"><button type="reset" class="kit-btn">Reset</button><button type="submit" class="kit-btn kit-btn-primary">Send</button></div>
</form>
```

From JavaScript: `Kit.validate(form)` runs the same check and returns `true` or `false` (options `{ ok, focus }`); `Kit.validate.reset(form)` clears states and messages (the form's `reset` does it by itself too). If there are errors the form fires `kit:invalid` with `{ fields }`, the list of invalid fields. The server has the last word: the errors it sends back are shown with `is-invalid` and `.kit-feedback-invalid` written in the HTML, and the kit leaves them as they are.

## Sizes

`kit-input-sm` and `kit-input-lg` on a field; `kit-field-sm|lg` on a field with its buttons and selects; `kit-form-sm|lg` on the whole form; `kit-input-group-sm|lg` on a group. They change `--kit-ctl` (the height shared by fields and buttons), so they always stay at the same height. `kit-btn-sm` is the matching button.

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-form">
  <input class="kit-input kit-input-sm" placeholder="Small" aria-label="Small">
  <input class="kit-input" placeholder="Normal" aria-label="Normal">
  <input class="kit-input kit-input-lg" placeholder="Large" aria-label="Large">
  <div class="kit-input-group kit-input-group-lg"><input class="kit-input" placeholder="Large group" aria-label="Large group"><button type="button" class="kit-btn kit-btn-primary">Search</button></div>
</div>
```

## Icons inside fields

`.kit-control` wraps the field and leaves room for an icon on the left (`.kit-control-start`) and an icon or a button on the right (`.kit-control-end`): the field makes room by itself. With `is-valid`, `is-invalid` or `is-warning` on the `.kit-control` (or on its `.kit-field`) the result icon appears on the right, drawn by CSS: a check, a cross or an exclamation mark, so with no images. `data-kit-password` on a button shows and hides the password (`aria-pressed` and the text for screen readers change by themselves).

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-fields">
  <div class="kit-field"><label class="kit-label" for="ic-q">Search</label>
    <div class="kit-control"><span class="kit-control-start"><svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-search"/></svg></span><input class="kit-input" id="ic-q" placeholder="Search a customer…"></div></div>
  <div class="kit-field"><label class="kit-label" for="ic-pw">Password</label>
    <div class="kit-control"><input class="kit-input" id="ic-pw" type="password" value="secret123"><button type="button" class="kit-control-end" data-kit-password><svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-eye"/></svg></button></div></div>
  <div class="kit-field is-valid"><label class="kit-label" for="ic-ok">User</label>
    <div class="kit-control"><span class="kit-control-start"><svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-user"/></svg></span><input class="kit-input" id="ic-ok" value="jane.smith"></div></div>
  <div class="kit-field is-invalid"><label class="kit-label" for="ic-ko">Email</label>
    <div class="kit-control"><span class="kit-control-start"><svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-info"/></svg></span><input class="kit-input" id="ic-ko" value="jane@" aria-invalid="true"></div>
    <div class="kit-feedback kit-feedback-invalid">Incomplete address.</div></div>
  <div class="kit-field is-warning"><label class="kit-label" for="ic-w">Amount</label>
    <div class="kit-control"><input class="kit-input" id="ic-w" value="0.00"></div>
    <div class="kit-feedback kit-feedback-warning">Check the amount.</div></div>
</div>
```

## Field groups

`.kit-input-group` joins text (`.kit-input-text`), icons, fields and buttons into a single block with merged borders. It also works with a native select, a `.kit-select`, a combobox or a field with a calendar. The states (`is-invalid`…) color all the parts.

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-fields">
  <div class="kit-field kit-field-wide"><label class="kit-label" for="gr-imp">Amount</label>
    <div class="kit-input-group"><span class="kit-input-text">€</span><input class="kit-input" id="gr-imp" inputmode="decimal" value="1,250.00"><span class="kit-input-text">VAT excluded</span></div></div>
  <div class="kit-field kit-field-wide"><label class="kit-label" for="gr-url">Website</label>
    <div class="kit-input-group"><span class="kit-input-text">https://</span><input class="kit-input" id="gr-url" placeholder="company"><span class="kit-input-text">.com</span></div></div>
  <div class="kit-field"><label class="kit-label" for="gr-c">Discount code</label>
    <div class="kit-input-group"><input class="kit-input" id="gr-c" placeholder="SPRING"><button type="button" class="kit-btn kit-btn-primary">Apply</button></div></div>
  <div class="kit-field"><label class="kit-label" for="gr-s">Price and currency</label>
    <div class="kit-input-group"><input class="kit-input" id="gr-s" value="99.00"><select class="kit-input" aria-label="Currency" style="max-width: 6rem"><option>EUR</option><option>USD</option></select></div></div>
  <div class="kit-field is-invalid"><label class="kit-label" for="gr-i">User</label>
    <div class="kit-input-group"><span class="kit-input-text">@</span><input class="kit-input" id="gr-i" value="jane smith" aria-invalid="true"></div>
    <div class="kit-feedback kit-feedback-invalid">No spaces.</div></div>
</div>
```

## Floating label

`.kit-float`: the label sits inside the field and, when the field is filled or focused, rises and shrinks. CSS only. The field comes **before** the label and has `placeholder=" "` (a space). It works for input, textarea and select. It is not used on fields with the calendar.

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-fields">
  <div class="kit-float"><input class="kit-input" id="f-n" placeholder=" "><label for="f-n">Full name</label></div>
  <div class="kit-float"><input class="kit-input" id="f-m" type="email" placeholder=" " value="jane@company.com"><label for="f-m">Email</label></div>
  <div class="kit-float"><select class="kit-input" id="f-s"><option>Milan</option><option>Turin</option></select><label for="f-s">Office</label></div>
  <div class="kit-float kit-field-wide"><textarea class="kit-input" id="f-t" placeholder=" "></textarea><label for="f-t">Message</label></div>
</div>
```

## Checkboxes, radios and cards

`.kit-check` works for checkboxes and radios. `.kit-check-text` adds a line of explanation below; `.kit-check-group` lays them out in a column and `kit-check-inline` in a row; `.kit-check-card` turns them into selectable cards (`.kit-check-cards` puts them in a grid). Wrap the group in a `fieldset` with a `legend`. The `is-invalid` state marks the border of the radio or card.

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-fields">
  <fieldset class="kit-check-group">
    <legend>Delivery</legend>
    <label class="kit-check"><input type="radio" name="cons" checked> <span class="kit-check-text">Standard<small>2–3 working days</small></span></label>
    <label class="kit-check"><input type="radio" name="cons"> <span class="kit-check-text">Express<small>Next day, +€5</small></span></label>
    <label class="kit-check"><input type="radio" name="cons" disabled> Pick-up in store</label>
  </fieldset>
  <fieldset class="kit-check-group">
    <legend>Options</legend>
    <div class="kit-check-inline">
      <label class="kit-check"><input type="checkbox" checked> Gift</label>
      <label class="kit-check"><input type="checkbox"> Invoice</label>
      <label class="kit-check"><input type="checkbox"> Insurance</label>
    </div>
  </fieldset>
</div>
<fieldset class="kit-check-group" style="margin-top: var(--kit-sp)">
  <legend>Plan</legend>
  <div class="kit-check-cards">
    <label class="kit-check kit-check-card"><input type="radio" name="piano" checked><span class="kit-check-text"><b>Basic</b><small>Up to 3 users</small></span></label>
    <label class="kit-check kit-check-card"><input type="radio" name="piano"><span class="kit-check-text"><b>Team</b><small>Up to 20 users</small></span></label>
    <label class="kit-check kit-check-card"><input type="radio" name="piano"><span class="kit-check-text"><b>Company</b><small>Unlimited users</small></span></label>
  </div>
</fieldset>
```

## Other controls

`.kit-input` also applies to `<textarea>` (free height, resizable; `kit-textarea-auto` makes it grow with the text where the browser allows), to a native `<select>` (with the arrow drawn by CSS), to `type="file"` and `type="color"`. `.kit-range` is for `type="range"`. `readonly` and `disabled` have a different background; `.kit-input-plain` shows a value as text, without a frame. `data-kit-count="#id"` on a text element writes "n / maxlength" and turns yellow near the limit and red at the limit.

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-fields">
  <div class="kit-field"><label class="kit-label" for="o-t">Message</label><textarea class="kit-input" id="o-t" rows="3" maxlength="60" placeholder="Write here…"></textarea><div class="kit-field-foot"><span class="kit-hint">At most 60 characters.</span><span class="kit-counter" data-kit-count="#o-t"></span></div></div>
  <div class="kit-field"><label class="kit-label" for="o-s">Native select</label><select class="kit-input" id="o-s"><option>One</option><option>Two</option><option>Three</option></select></div>
  <div class="kit-field"><label class="kit-label" for="o-f">File</label><input class="kit-input" id="o-f" type="file"></div>
  <div class="kit-field"><label class="kit-label" for="o-c">Color</label><input class="kit-input" id="o-c" type="color" value="#2f5fd0"></div>
  <div class="kit-field"><label class="kit-label" for="o-r">Quantity</label><input class="kit-range" id="o-r" type="range" min="0" max="10" value="4"></div>
  <div class="kit-field"><label class="kit-label" for="o-ro">Read only</label><input class="kit-input" id="o-ro" value="FT-2026-0041" readonly></div>
  <div class="kit-field"><label class="kit-label" for="o-d">Disabled</label><input class="kit-input" id="o-d" value="Cannot be edited" disabled></div>
  <div class="kit-field"><span class="kit-label">As text</span><div class="kit-input kit-input-plain">jane@company.com</div></div>
</div>
```

## With Django

The class names are the ones Django writes in widgets; the error messages from `form.errors` go into a `.kit-feedback-invalid`. A filter or template tag, or a widget with `attrs`, puts the classes on the field.

```python
# forms.py
class ContactForm(forms.Form):
    name = forms.CharField(widget=forms.TextInput(attrs={"class": "kit-input"}))
    email = forms.EmailField(widget=forms.EmailInput(attrs={"class": "kit-input"}))
    message = forms.CharField(max_length=300, widget=forms.Textarea(attrs={"class": "kit-input", "rows": 4}))
```

```html
<!-- _field.html: {% include "_field.html" with field=form.email %} -->
<div class="kit-field{% if field.errors %} is-invalid{% endif %}">
  <label class="kit-label{% if field.field.required %} kit-required{% endif %}" for="{{ field.id_for_label }}">{{ field.label }}</label>
  {{ field }}
  {% if field.help_text %}<div class="kit-hint">{{ field.help_text }}</div>{% endif %}
  {% for e in field.errors %}<div class="kit-feedback kit-feedback-invalid">{{ e }}</div>{% endfor %}
</div>
```

The invalid field gets its border from the `is-invalid` class on the `.kit-field`; to tell screen readers too that it is wrong, `aria-invalid="true"` is added from the widget, or with `data-kit-validate` on the form `kit.js` writes it at the first check. With htmx the inserted fragments initialize by themselves.

---

# Forms: basic fields
Page: https://n1k1tas95.github.io/dashboard-kit/en/forms.html

Text field, search, checkbox and switch. Buttons and fields have the same height (`--kit-ctl`), so they sit well on the same row.

## Fields

`.kit-field` is the label with the field below it; `.kit-input` applies to `<input>`. `.kit-fields` lays out several fields in a grid that adapts.

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-fields">
  <label class="kit-field">Name <input class="kit-input" placeholder="Jane Smith"></label>
  <label class="kit-field">Date <input class="kit-input" type="date"></label>
  <label class="kit-field">Amount <input class="kit-input" type="number" step="0.01" placeholder="€"></label>
  <label class="kit-field kit-field-wide">Note <input class="kit-input" placeholder="Takes two columns (kit-field-wide)"><small>A help text below the field.</small></label>
</div>
```

The rest of the forms is on these pages: [Layout and validation](https://n1k1tas95.github.io/dashboard-kit/en/form-layout.html) (labels, help text, column, grid and horizontal forms, valid and invalid states with error messages, validation, sizes, icons inside fields, selectable groups and cards), [Select and file](https://n1k1tas95.github.io/dashboard-kit/en/form-controls.html) (custom select, file field, drop zone, combobox) and [Dates and times](https://n1k1tas95.github.io/dashboard-kit/en/dates.html) (optional calendar, designed for the phone too).

## Search

A field with a magnifier and a keyboard shortcut. It stretches to fill the row (`flex: 1`).

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-bar">
  <label class="kit-search"><svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-search"/></svg><input class="kit-input" type="search" placeholder="Search…" aria-label="Search"><kbd>/</kbd></label>
  <button class="kit-btn kit-btn-primary">Search</button>
</div>
```

## Checkbox and form footer

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-form-foot">
  <label class="kit-check"><input type="checkbox" checked> Hide duplicates</label>
  <div class="kit-btn-group">
    <button class="kit-btn">Reset</button>
    <button class="kit-btn kit-btn-primary">Apply</button>
  </div>
</div>
```

## Switch

An on/off that takes effect immediately, unlike a checkbox that is confirmed with a button. It is a normal `<input type="checkbox">` with `role="switch"`: `checked`, `disabled` and the `change` event work as usual. `kit-switch-between` puts the text on the left and the switch at the far right.

Example markup:

```html
<label class="kit-switch"><input type="checkbox" role="switch" checked> Hide duplicates</label>
<label class="kit-switch"><input type="checkbox" role="switch"> Also show discarded</label>
<label class="kit-switch"><input type="checkbox" role="switch" disabled> Not available</label>
<label class="kit-switch kit-switch-between"><span>Notifications</span><input type="checkbox" role="switch" checked></label>
```

---

# Grid
Page: https://n1k1tas95.github.io/dashboard-kit/en/grid.html

A 12-column flexbox grid, with the same names as Bootstrap. It is built with rows and columns and changes as the screen width changes.

## How it works
- A `.kit-row` contains `.kit-col-*` columns; each row has **12** columns and wraps by itself.
- It is **mobile first**: a class without a breakpoint applies everywhere, `kit-col-md-6` applies from 768px up.
- The row has negative margins that compensate the columns' padding (the _gutters_): put it inside a container with padding, like `.kit-main` or `.kit-card-body`.
