- The row's direct children are all columns: even a `<div>` without a class is 100% wide.

| Abbreviation | From | Example |
|---|---|---|
| _none_ | 0px | `kit-col-6` |
| `sm` | 576px | `kit-col-sm-6` |
| `md` | 768px | `kit-col-md-6` |
| `lg` | 992px | `kit-col-lg-6` |
| `xl` | 1200px | `kit-col-xl-6` |

## Columns

`kit-col-N` with N from 1 to 12: the column takes N twelfths of the row.

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-row">
  <div class="kit-col-4"><div class="kit-card kit-card-body kit-center">kit-col-4</div></div>
  <div class="kit-col-4"><div class="kit-card kit-card-body kit-center">kit-col-4</div></div>
  <div class="kit-col-4"><div class="kit-card kit-card-body kit-center">kit-col-4</div></div>
</div>
<div class="kit-row">
  <div class="kit-col-8"><div class="kit-card kit-card-body kit-center">kit-col-8</div></div>
  <div class="kit-col-4"><div class="kit-card kit-card-body kit-center">kit-col-4</div></div>
</div>
```

## Responsive

Combine several classes: a full-width column on the phone, half from `md`, a quarter from `xl`. **Resize the window** to see them change.

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-row">
  <div class="kit-col-12 kit-col-md-6 kit-col-xl-3"><div class="kit-card kit-card-body kit-center">12 → md 6 → xl 3</div></div>
  <div class="kit-col-12 kit-col-md-6 kit-col-xl-3"><div class="kit-card kit-card-body kit-center">12 → md 6 → xl 3</div></div>
  <div class="kit-col-12 kit-col-md-6 kit-col-xl-3"><div class="kit-card kit-card-body kit-center">12 → md 6 → xl 3</div></div>
  <div class="kit-col-12 kit-col-md-6 kit-col-xl-3"><div class="kit-card kit-card-body kit-center">12 → md 6 → xl 3</div></div>
</div>
```

## Flexible columns

`kit-col` splits the remaining space in equal parts; `kit-col-auto` is as wide as its content.

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-row">
  <div class="kit-col"><div class="kit-card kit-card-body kit-center">kit-col</div></div>
  <div class="kit-col-auto"><div class="kit-card kit-card-body kit-center">kit-col-auto</div></div>
  <div class="kit-col"><div class="kit-card kit-card-body kit-center">kit-col</div></div>
</div>
<div class="kit-row">
  <div class="kit-col"><div class="kit-card kit-card-body kit-center">kit-col</div></div>
  <div class="kit-col-6"><div class="kit-card kit-card-body kit-center">kit-col-6</div></div>
  <div class="kit-col"><div class="kit-card kit-card-body kit-center">kit-col</div></div>
</div>
```

## Columns per row

On the row, `kit-row-cols-N` (N from 1 to 6) decides how many cells fit in a row, with no classes on the cells. It is the most convenient way for KPI cards.

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-row kit-row-cols-2 kit-row-cols-md-4">
  <div><div class="kit-card kit-card-body kit-center">1</div></div>
  <div><div class="kit-card kit-card-body kit-center">2</div></div>
  <div><div class="kit-card kit-card-body kit-center">3</div></div>
  <div><div class="kit-card kit-card-body kit-center">4</div></div>
  <div><div class="kit-card kit-card-body kit-center">5</div></div>
  <div><div class="kit-card kit-card-body kit-center">6</div></div>
  <div><div class="kit-card kit-card-body kit-center">7</div></div>
  <div><div class="kit-card kit-card-body kit-center">8</div></div>
</div>
```

## Offset and order

`kit-offset-N` moves the column right by N twelfths. `kit-order-first`, `kit-order-last` and `kit-order-0…5` change the display order without touching the HTML.

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-row">
  <div class="kit-col-md-6 kit-offset-md-3"><div class="kit-card kit-card-body kit-center">kit-col-md-6 kit-offset-md-3</div></div>
</div>
<div class="kit-row">
  <div class="kit-col-4 kit-order-last"><div class="kit-card kit-card-body kit-center">1st in the code, last</div></div>
  <div class="kit-col-4"><div class="kit-card kit-card-body kit-center">2nd</div></div>
  <div class="kit-col-4 kit-order-first"><div class="kit-card kit-card-body kit-center">3rd in the code, first</div></div>
</div>
```

## Alignment

On the row, `kit-align-items-*` aligns vertically and `kit-justify-content-*` horizontally. On a single column `kit-align-self-*` applies.

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-row kit-align-items-center">
  <div class="kit-col-4"><div class="kit-card kit-card-body kit-center kit-py-4">align-items-center</div></div>
  <div class="kit-col-4"><div class="kit-card kit-card-body kit-center">centered</div></div>
  <div class="kit-col-4"><div class="kit-card kit-card-body kit-center kit-py-5">centered</div></div>
</div>
<div class="kit-row kit-justify-content-center">
  <div class="kit-col-4"><div class="kit-card kit-card-body kit-center">justify-content-center</div></div>
</div>
```

## Gutter

The space between columns is adjusted with `kit-g-0…5` (horizontal and vertical), `kit-gx-*` and `kit-gy-*`. By default it is `--kit-sp`, so it tightens by itself on the phone; with `kit-g-md-4` it changes from a breakpoint.

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-row kit-g-0">
  <div class="kit-col-6"><div class="kit-card kit-card-body kit-center">kit-g-0</div></div>
  <div class="kit-col-6"><div class="kit-card kit-card-body kit-center">kit-g-0</div></div>
</div>
<div class="kit-row kit-g-4">
  <div class="kit-col-6"><div class="kit-card kit-card-body kit-center">kit-g-4</div></div>
  <div class="kit-col-6"><div class="kit-card kit-card-body kit-center">kit-g-4</div></div>
  <div class="kit-col-6"><div class="kit-card kit-card-body kit-center">kit-g-4</div></div>
  <div class="kit-col-6"><div class="kit-card kit-card-body kit-center">kit-g-4</div></div>
</div>
```

## Nested rows

Inside a column you can put another row, with its own 12 columns. Remember the container's padding (here `kit-card-body`).

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-row">
  <div class="kit-col-md-8">
    <div class="kit-card kit-card-body">
      <p class="kit-mute">kit-col-md-8, with a row inside</p>
      <div class="kit-row">
        <div class="kit-col-6"><div class="kit-card kit-card-body kit-center">kit-col-6</div></div>
        <div class="kit-col-6"><div class="kit-card kit-card-body kit-center">kit-col-6</div></div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="kit-col-md-4"><div class="kit-card kit-card-body kit-center">kit-col-md-4</div></div>
</div>
```

## Cards of equal height

The columns of a row already have the same height, but the card inside does not. Add `kit-h-100` to the card.

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-row">
  <div class="kit-col-md-6"><div class="kit-card kit-card-body kit-h-100">A little text.</div></div>
  <div class="kit-col-md-6"><div class="kit-card kit-card-body kit-h-100">Much more text, which runs over several lines and makes the column taller than the other: with kit-h-100 the two cards end at the same height.</div></div>
</div>
```

## Alternative: CSS Grid

When you do not need per-column breakpoints, `kit-grid` fills the row with as many columns as fit (at least 240px each). `kit-grid-2` and `kit-grid-3` fix 2 or 3 columns (just one below 900px).

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-grid">
  <div class="kit-card kit-card-body kit-center">kit-grid 1</div>
  <div class="kit-card kit-card-body kit-center">kit-grid 2</div>
  <div class="kit-card kit-card-body kit-center">kit-grid 3</div>
  <div class="kit-card kit-card-body kit-center">kit-grid 4</div>
</div>
```

## Structure of a dashboard

The most common scheme: KPIs at the top, a chart with a side panel, then a full-width table. The complete result is in the [sample dashboard](https://n1k1tas95.github.io/dashboard-kit/en/dashboard.html).

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-row kit-row-cols-2 kit-row-cols-lg-4">
  <div><div class="kit-card kit-kpi kit-h-100"><small>Documents</small><b>1,284</b><span class="kit-badge kit-badge-success">+4%</span></div></div>
  <div><div class="kit-card kit-kpi kit-h-100"><small>Total</small><b>€48,920</b><span class="kit-badge kit-badge-success">+1.2%</span></div></div>
  <div><div class="kit-card kit-kpi kit-h-100"><small>To review</small><b>17</b><span class="kit-badge kit-badge-warning">−3</span></div></div>
  <div><div class="kit-card kit-kpi kit-h-100"><small>Discarded</small><b>2</b><span class="kit-badge kit-badge-danger">+1</span></div></div>
</div>
<div class="kit-row">
  <div class="kit-col-12 kit-col-xl-8"><section class="kit-card kit-card-body kit-h-100 kit-center kit-mute kit-py-5">Chart (kit-col-xl-8)</section></div>
  <div class="kit-col-12 kit-col-xl-4"><section class="kit-card kit-card-body kit-h-100 kit-center kit-mute kit-py-5">Side panel (kit-col-xl-4)</section></div>
</div>
<div class="kit-row">
  <div class="kit-col-12"><section class="kit-card kit-card-body kit-center kit-mute">Table (kit-col-12)</section></div>
</div>
```

---

# Icons
Page: https://n1k1tas95.github.io/dashboard-kit/en/icons.html

The kit's icons: an SVG sprite you include with one line of JavaScript.

## Usage

Icons are strokes on a 24×24 grid that take the text color (`currentColor`). They are used with `<svg class="kit-icon">` and `<use>`; the name is the symbol's id, preceded by `i-`.

Example markup:

```html
<button class="kit-btn kit-btn-primary"><svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-download"/></svg>Download</button>
<button class="kit-btn kit-btn-icon" aria-label="Edit"><svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-edit"/></svg></button>
<button class="kit-btn kit-btn-icon kit-btn-danger" aria-label="Delete"><svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-trash"/></svg></button>
```

An icon on its own, without text, needs an `aria-label` on the button that contains it. If it is only decorative, add `aria-hidden="true"` to the `<svg>`.

## Installation

Sprites cannot be loaded from another domain with a `<use>` that points to an SVG file: that is why the kit inserts them with a small script. Add it before closing `</body>`:

```html
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/N1K1TAS95/dashboard-kit@v0.11.0/dist/kit-icons.js"
        integrity="sha384-HrtxdGgc5dQOvkslXHapNsTNVhGGEfQ6FWYOn5zdFAIrc/6z/AbizR+W6xdilWS9"
        crossorigin="anonymous"></script>
```

If you prefer not to use JavaScript, copy the content of `dist/kit-icons.svg` to the start of the `<body>` (this is what this documentation does) or keep only the icons you need in the sprite.

If you already have your own sprite with the same ids, the first one the browser finds wins: there is no conflict, but check that the icons are the ones you expect.

## Size and color

The icon is 18px and takes the text color. To change it use `width`/`height` and `color`.

Example markup:

```html
<svg class="kit-icon" style="width: 14px; height: 14px"><use href="#i-info"/></svg>
<svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-info"/></svg>
<svg class="kit-icon" style="width: 28px; height: 28px"><use href="#i-info"/></svg>
<svg class="kit-icon" style="color: var(--kit-success)"><use href="#i-ok"/></svg>
<svg class="kit-icon" style="color: var(--kit-danger)"><use href="#i-error"/></svg>
```

## List

All the available icons, with the name to use after `#i-`.

`chev` `chev-up` `chev-left` `chev-right` `arrow-up` `arrow-down` `arrow-left` `arrow-right` `expand` `external` `plus` `minus` `check` `x` `search` `download` `upload` `refresh` `edit` `trash` `copy` `filter` `sliders` `menu` `more` `more-v` `home` `user` `bell` `calendar` `file` `folder` `eye` `sun` `text` `moon` `auto` `info` `ok` `warn` `error`

## Adding an icon

Icons are defined in `tools/icons.py` (name → SVG strokes). Add a line, then run `python3 tools/icons.py`: it regenerates `dist/kit-icons.svg` and `dist/kit-icons.js`. Draw them on 24×24, stroke only, with no fixed colors.

---

# Introduction
Page: https://n1k1tas95.github.io/dashboard-kit/en/index.html

Dashboard Kit is a small CSS framework, with optional JavaScript, for building dashboards. A single file, no dependencies, light and dark themes, and a 12-column grid like Bootstrap.

## Installation

From a CDN (jsDelivr), with the version pinned and the `integrity` attribute (SRI): if the file were tampered with, the browser rejects it.

```html
<link rel="stylesheet"
      href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/N1K1TAS95/dashboard-kit@v0.11.0/dist/kit.css"
      integrity="sha384-caI9z5CMWhN61so69TJdI2W0CNgg9S/+kpJOHLXAtH+BJfDxBaY1a+izk6JVhNZY"
      crossorigin="anonymous">

<!-- optional: theme, select, tabs, dialog, menus, toasts -->
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/N1K1TAS95/dashboard-kit@v0.11.0/dist/kit.js"
        integrity="sha384-VQpUqPK9ZCxfCao7rrz7IGAfbpWrhxw7Fh3uVC/AKUcA4D99T3fnMuw01VWFatYr"
        crossorigin="anonymous"></script>
```

Or locally: copy `dist/kit.css` (and `dist/kit.js`) into your project and link them with a relative path.

If your site has a Content-Security-Policy, allow `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net` in `style-src` and `script-src`. Avoid `@main` or `@latest`: they are not pinned versions and jsDelivr caches them for hours.

The texts `kit.js` writes by itself (button labels, "No results", the calendar…) follow `<html lang>`: English if missing, Italian with `lang="it"`. See [Languages](https://n1k1tas95.github.io/dashboard-kit/en/javascript.html#languages).

## Page template

The minimal skeleton with a fixed header and a grid for the content. In the editor you get it by typing `kit-page` + Tab (see [VS Code snippets](https://n1k1tas95.github.io/dashboard-kit/en/snippets.html)).

```html
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
  <meta name="color-scheme" content="light dark">
  <title>My dashboard</title>
  <script src="dist/kit.js"></script>
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="dist/kit.css">
</head>
<body>
<header class="kit-header">
  <h1 class="kit-brand">Name <span>app</span></h1>
</header>
<main class="kit-main">
  <div class="kit-container">
    <div class="kit-row">
      <div class="kit-col-12 kit-col-lg-8"><section class="kit-card kit-card-body">…</section></div>
      <div class="kit-col-12 kit-col-lg-4"><section class="kit-card kit-card-body">…</section></div>
    </div>
  </div>
</main>
</body>
</html>
```

## Icons

The kit does not include icons: `.kit-icon` only gives an `<svg>` its size and stroke. You use an inline sprite in the page and call it with `<use>`, so the icons take the text color.

```html
<svg width="0" height="0" style="position:absolute" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><defs>
  <symbol id="i-search" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><circle cx="11" cy="11" r="7"/><path d="m20 20-3.5-3.5"/></symbol>
</defs></svg>

<button class="kit-btn"><svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-search"/></svg>Search</button>
```

## Supported browsers

The light/dark colors use `light-dark()`, so you need Chrome/Edge 123+, Safari 17.5+ or Firefox 120+. The rest (flexbox, grid, `color-mix()`, `:has()` only in the documentation pages) is supported by those same versions.

## If you know Bootstrap

The grid, the utilities and the names follow Bootstrap, with the `kit-` prefix. The differences to keep in mind:

| Bootstrap | Dashboard Kit | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `.row`, `.col-md-6` | `.kit-row`, `.kit-col-md-6` | Identical, but with default gutters equal to `--kit-sp` (they tighten on phones). |
| `.btn btn-primary` | `.kit-btn kit-btn-primary` | Variants are separate classes, not double-dash modifiers. |
| `.d-flex`, `.mt-3` | `.kit-d-flex`, `.kit-mt-3` | Spacing scale 0–5 in px: 0, 4, 8, 16, 24, 48. |
| `.modal`, `.dropdown` | `<dialog class="kit-dialog">`, `.kit-dropdown` | The dialog is the browser's native element. |
| Theme with `data-bs-theme` | `data-theme` on `<html>` | Automatic by default, can be forced to light or dark. |
| `xxl` breakpoint | — | Not present: add it in `tools/gen-grid.py`. |

---

# JavaScript
Page: https://n1k1tas95.github.io/dashboard-kit/en/javascript.html

JavaScript is optional. Without `kit.js` all the styling works; you only need it for the parts that move: theme, tabs, select, menus, dialogs and toasts.

## Principles
- No dependencies and no build step: a single file, `dist/kit.js`.
- It is activated with `data-kit-*` attributes, without writing code.
- It uses no `innerHTML`, `eval` or inline scripts: it works with `script-src 'self'`.
- Handlers are delegated to the document, so they also apply to HTML added after load.

## Attributes

| Attribute | Where | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `data-kit-theme-set="auto\|light\|dark"` | a button or a menu item | Sets the theme and remembers it. |
| `data-kit-fs-set="md\|lg\|xl"` | a button or a menu item | Sets the text size of the whole page and remembers it. |
| `data-kit-fs-step="1\|-1"` | a button | Makes the text one step larger (`1`) or smaller (`-1`); it disables itself at the ends. |
| `data-kit-reset` | a button | Restores theme, text size and width (see the [settings panel](https://n1k1tas95.github.io/dashboard-kit/en/overlays.html#settings)). |
| `data-kit-layout-set="boxed\|fluid"` | a button | Chooses centered or full-width content and remembers it. |
| `data-kit-layout-toggle` | a button | Switches between the two widths. |
| `data-kit-nav="#id"` | the button of a [navbar](https://n1k1tas95.github.io/dashboard-kit/en/navbar.html) | Opens or closes the given collapsible menu (`.kit-navbar-menu`); Esc or a click outside closes it. |
| `data-kit-toggle="#id"` | a button | Opens or closes the given `.kit-pop`. |
| `data-kit-select` | `.kit-select` | Turns the list of options into a select. On a native `<select>` it replaces it with the kit's menu ([details](https://n1k1tas95.github.io/dashboard-kit/en/form-controls.html#native-select)). |
| `data-kit-tabs` | `.kit-tabs` | Activates the tabs; each `.kit-tab` has `data-kit-panel="#id"`. |
| `data-kit-open="#id"` | a button | Opens the given `<dialog>`. |
| `data-kit-confirm="Question?"` | a button, a link or a `<form>` | First asks for confirmation in a dialog; the action goes on only if the user confirms. See [Asking for confirmation](https://n1k1tas95.github.io/dashboard-kit/en/overlays.html#confirm). |
| `data-kit-sort`, `data-kit-filter="#id"`, `data-kit-page="N"` | `<table>`; the search field; `<table>` | Sorting from the headers, text filter and pagination ([details](https://n1k1tas95.github.io/dashboard-kit/en/tables.html#sorting)). |
| `data-kit-datepicker`, `data-kit-timepicker`, `data-kit-daterange` | `<input type="date\|datetime-local\|time">`; a container with two date fields | Calendar, time picker and date range, with an ISO value in the form ([details](https://n1k1tas95.github.io/dashboard-kit/en/dates.html)). |
| `data-kit-validate`, `data-kit-password`, `data-kit-count="#id"` | a `<form>`; a button next to a password field; a text element | Validation with messages and states, show/hide password, character counter ([details](https://n1k1tas95.github.io/dashboard-kit/en/form-layout.html#validation)). |
| `data-kit-close` | inside a `<dialog>` | Closes the dialog. |

## API

```js
Kit.toast("Saved!");            // temporary message; options: type, title, duration, position, action, progress (see Dialogs and menus)
Kit.toast.clear();              // closes all toasts
await Kit.confirm("Delete?", { danger: true });      // confirmation dialog → true / false (options: text, confirm, cancel, danger, type)
Kit.undo("Deleted", { onUndo, onCommit });           // the action happens now, with an "Undo" toast; onCommit if it is not undone
Kit.theme.get();                // "auto" | "light" | "dark"
Kit.theme.set("dark");          // sets and saves the theme
Kit.fontSize.get();             // "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl"
Kit.fontSize.set("lg");         // sets and saves the text size
Kit.fontSize.step(1);           // one step larger (-1: smaller)
Kit.reset();                    // restores theme, text and width
Kit.layout.get();               // "boxed" | "fluid"
Kit.layout.set("fluid");        // full-width content (remembered)
Kit.layout.toggle();            // switches
Kit.table("#table", { sort: true, size: 10 });     // sorting, filter and pages of a table (see Tables); Kit.paginate("#table", 10) for pages only
Kit.datepicker("#due");         // calendar on a date, date-time or time field (see Dates and times); Kit.daterange("#period") for the range
Kit.validate("#form");          // checks a form (true/false) and marks its fields; Kit.validate.reset(form) clears states and messages
Kit.date.parse("3/5/26");       // "2026-03-05" (Kit.date.format, Kit.date.today); the day/month order depends on the language
Kit.i18n.lang("en");            // language of the kit's texts (see Languages)
Kit.init(element);              // re-reads selects and tabs in an area added after load
```

Example markup:

```html
<button class="kit-btn kit-btn-primary" data-doc-toast="Saved!">Show a toast</button>
<button class="kit-btn" data-kit-theme-set="light">Light theme</button>
<button class="kit-btn" data-kit-theme-set="dark">Dark theme</button>
<button class="kit-btn" data-kit-theme-set="auto">Automatic</button>
```

## Languages

The texts `kit.js` writes by itself (the "Cancel" and "Confirm" buttons, labels for screen readers, "No results", table pages, the calendar) come from a dictionary per language. **English** (the base language) and **Italian** are built in. The language is the one in `<html lang="…">`: without the attribute English is used, so on an Italian page remember to write `<html lang="it">`.

With a language that has a region (`pt-BR`) it looks for that first, then the language without the region (`pt`), then English: a dictionary can contain only what changes. Attributes and options (`data-kit-empty`, `Kit.confirm(…, { cancel })`) always win over the dictionary.

The calendar and the tables follow the language too: the date order (`mm/dd/yyyy` in English, `dd/mm/yyyy` in Italian), the first day of the week (Sunday in English, Monday in Italian), month and day names, and the decimal separator used to sort the numbers in a column (`1,250.50` or `1.250,50`). The submitted value is always ISO.

```js
Kit.i18n.lang();                 // "en": the language in use (from <html lang>)
Kit.i18n.lang("de");             // sets it by hand, ignoring <html lang>; Kit.i18n.lang("") goes back to <html lang>

// Another language: just write what you need, the rest stays in English
Kit.i18n.add("de", {
    cancel: "Abbrechen", confirm: "Bestätigen", close: "Schließen", noResults: "Keine Ergebnisse",
    num: { dec: "," },
    date: { order: "dmy", first: 1, months: ["Januar", /* … */], days: ["mo", "di", /* … */], t: { today: "Heute", clear: "Löschen" } }
});

// A regional variant: British English writes the day before the month and starts the week on Monday
Kit.i18n.add("en-GB", { date: { order: "dmy", first: 1 } });
```

The keys are in the dictionary at the top of `dist/kit.js` (`I18N`): `en` is the complete model. `Kit.i18n.t("cancel")` reads an entry in the current language. Languages must be added before the page builds the components: put `Kit.i18n.add(…)` right after `kit.js`.

## Events

They are `CustomEvent`s that bubble up the DOM: listen on the document or on the element.

| Event | On | `detail` |
|---|---|---|
| `kit:change` | `.kit-select` | `{ value }`: the chosen `data-value` (for a native select also `label`) |
| `kit:sort`, `kit:filter`, `kit:page` | `<table>` | `{ column, direction }`, `{ query, count }`, `{ page, pages, size, total }` |
| `kit:change` | date, time or range field | `{ value, display }` (ISO and the field's text) or `{ from, to }` |
| `kit:invalid` | `<form data-kit-validate>` | `{ fields }`: the fields that are invalid at submit time |
| `kit:tab` | `.kit-tabs` | `{ tab }`: the activated tab element |
| `kit:theme` | `<html>` | the theme that was set |
| `kit:fs` | `<html>` | the text size that was set (`sm`, `md`, `lg` or `xl`) |
| `kit:reset` | `<html>` | the settings were restored |
| `kit:layout` | `<html>` | the width that was set (`boxed` or `fluid`) |

```js
document.addEventListener("kit:change", (e) => {
  console.log("Chosen:", e.detail.value);
});
```

## Keyboard
- **Open menus and selects**: up/down arrows to move through the items, Enter or Space to choose, Esc to close (focus returns to the button).
- **Tabs**: left/right arrows move to the neighboring tab.
- **Dialog**: Esc closes it (native behavior); so does a click on the backdrop.

---

# Layout
Page: https://n1k1tas95.github.io/dashboard-kit/en/layout.html

Container, fixed header, element bars, stacking and side panel: the structure of a page. For columns see the [grid](https://n1k1tas95.github.io/dashboard-kit/en/grid.html).

## Page structure

A page is a fixed `.kit-header` at the top and a `.kit-main` containing a `.kit-container`. Inside the container you use the [grid](https://n1k1tas95.github.io/dashboard-kit/en/grid.html) or `.kit-stack`.

```html
<header class="kit-header">
  <h1 class="kit-brand">Name <span>app</span></h1>
  <span class="kit-spacer"></span>
  <!-- buttons, menus, theme… -->
</header>
<main class="kit-main">
  <div class="kit-container kit-stack">
    …
  </div>
</main>
```
- `.kit-header`: `--kit-hh` tall, stays stuck to the top (sticky). Table headers stick right below it.
- `.kit-brand`: a title whose second word, in a `<span>`, is colored with the accent.
- `.kit-main`: 24px of inner margin (16px below 900px) and 80px at the bottom.
- `.kit-container`: centered content, at most `--kit-container-w` (1200px) wide. See [Content width](#content-width).

## Content width

Narrow, centered content reads better for texts and forms; a dashboard with tables and charts often does better at full width. The kit allows both, at two levels.

| Class | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `kit-container` | Centered, at most `--kit-container-w` wide. It follows the **global switch** (below): with `data-layout="fluid"` it fills the whole window. |
| `kit-container-boxed` | Always centered, whatever the switch. |
| `kit-container-fluid` | Always full width. |

### Global switch

Put `data-layout="boxed"` or `"fluid"` on `<html>` to choose the width of the whole page (`boxed` by default). With `kit.js` the user can change it from a button and the choice is remembered, like the theme. The width only changes when the window is wider than `--kit-container-w`.

```html
<!-- full-width content by default -->
<html lang="en" data-layout="fluid">

<!-- a button that lets the user choose (it is remembered) -->
<button class="kit-btn kit-btn-ghost kit-btn-icon" data-kit-layout-toggle aria-label="Full-width content">…</button>
```

```js
Kit.layout.set("fluid");   // or "boxed"; Kit.layout.toggle() switches
```

These documentation pages use `kit-container-boxed` and always stay centered. To see the switch in action open the [sample dashboard](https://n1k1tas95.github.io/dashboard-kit/en/dashboard.html): it starts at full width and has the button with the arrows at the top right.

### Header aligned with the content

If you put a `.kit-container` inside `.kit-header`, it becomes the header's inner row and its content aligns with the page's, both centered and full width. Without a container the header always fills the whole window.

```html
<header class="kit-header">
  <div class="kit-container">
    <h1 class="kit-brand">Name <span>app</span></h1>
    <span class="kit-spacer"></span>
    <button class="kit-btn kit-btn-ghost kit-btn-icon" data-kit-layout-toggle aria-label="Content width">…</button>
  </div>
</header>
```

## Stacking: kit-stack

It lays out its children in a column with a constant gap (`--kit-sp`). It is the simplest way to put cards one under the other.

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-stack">
  <div class="kit-card kit-card-body">First card</div>
  <div class="kit-card kit-card-body">Second card</div>
  <div class="kit-card kit-card-body">Third card</div>
</div>
```

## Element bar: kit-bar

Elements side by side and vertically centered, wrapping when there is no room: toolbars, filters, groups of buttons. `.kit-spacer` pushes what follows to the right.

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-bar">
  <button class="kit-btn kit-btn-primary">New</button>
  <button class="kit-btn">Import</button>
  <span class="kit-spacer"></span>
  <button class="kit-btn kit-btn-ghost">Settings</button>
</div>
```

`kit-bar` is not the grid's row: for columns use `kit-row`.

## Side panel: kit-split

A list with, next to it, a detail panel that opens when a row is selected. Above 900px the panel sits next to the list and stays put while the list scrolls. Below 900px it covers the page from the right, with a dark veil behind it, and a click on the veil closes it. With `kit-split-lg` instead of `kit-split` the switch happens below 1250px, for lists that need a lot of room.

With `kit.js` three attributes are enough: `data-kit-split-open="#id"` on whatever opens it (a row, a button), `data-kit-split-close` and `data-kit-split-full` inside the panel. The second closes, the third toggles between "next to the list" and "full width" (the list disappears). With `data-kit-split` on the container Esc closes the panel, or brings it back next to the list if it was full width. On opening, focus goes to the panel and on closing it returns to whatever opened it.

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-split" id="demo-split" data-kit-split>
  <div class="kit-card">
    <div class="kit-table-wrap"><table class="kit-table kit-table-hover"><thead><tr><th>Invoice</th><th>Customer</th><th class="kit-right">Amount</th></tr></thead><tbody>
      <tr data-kit-split-open="#demo-split" style="cursor: pointer"><td>2026/014</td><td>Smith Ltd</td><td class="kit-right kit-num">€1,240.00</td></tr>
      <tr data-kit-split-open="#demo-split" style="cursor: pointer"><td>2026/015</td><td>Brown Inc</td><td class="kit-right kit-num">€860.50</td></tr>
      <tr data-kit-split-open="#demo-split" style="cursor: pointer"><td>2026/016</td><td>Green Services</td><td class="kit-right kit-num">€3,075.00</td></tr>
    </tbody></table></div>
  </div>
  <aside class="kit-split-panel" aria-label="Invoice detail">
    <div class="kit-split-head">
      <div class="kit-split-title"><h3>Invoice 2026/014</h3><small>Smith Ltd</small></div>
      <button class="kit-btn kit-btn-ghost kit-btn-icon" data-kit-split-full aria-label="Full width" title="Full width"><svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-expand"/></svg></button>
      <button class="kit-btn kit-btn-ghost kit-btn-icon" data-kit-split-close aria-label="Close" title="Close (Esc)"><svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-x"/></svg></button>
    </div>
    <div class="kit-split-body">
      <dl class="kit-kv"><dt>Date</dt><dd>03/12/2026</dd><dt>Taxable amount</dt><dd>€1,016.39</dd><dt>VAT 22%</dt><dd>€223.61</dd><dt>Total</dt><dd>€1,240.00</dd></dl>
    </div>
  </aside>
</div>
```

The panel is made of `kit-split-head` (title in `kit-split-title` and buttons) and `kit-split-body`, which is the part that scrolls. Width next to the list: `--kit-split-w` (40%); width when it covers the page: `--kit-split-overlay-w` (860px). Without JavaScript just add or remove `is-open` (and `is-full`) on the container.

| JavaScript | Effect |
|---|---|
| `Kit.split("#id")` | returns `{ open(), close(), full(on), isOpen(), isFull() }` |
| `kit:split` event | on the container, with `{ open, full }`: useful to update the selected row or free the detail's data |

Moving to the previous or next row (arrows, "j" and "k") depends on the list and is not included: write it with two buttons and a handler that calls your own open function.

## Base spacing

Three tokens govern the interface's breathing room (see [Themes and tokens](https://n1k1tas95.github.io/dashboard-kit/en/theming.html)): `--kit-sp` (margins, distance between cards, inner padding, gutter), `--kit-rad` (corners) and `--kit-ctl` (height of buttons and fields). Below 760px `--kit-sp` goes down from 16 to 8px.

---

# Navbar
Page: https://n1k1tas95.github.io/dashboard-kit/en/navbar.html

The top bar with logo, items, dropdown menus, actions and a collapsible menu on small screens.

## Basic navbar

The navbar is a `.kit-header` with the `kit-navbar` class. Inside go, in this order, the logo (`kit-brand`), the menu (`kit-navbar-menu`) with the list of items (`kit-nav`) and, if needed, actions on the right, and finally the button that opens the menu on small screens (`kit-navbar-toggler`).

With `kit-navbar-expand-md` the menu is inline from 768px up and, below that, it hides behind the three-line button. Try narrowing the window. The button has `data-kit-nav` with the menu's id: `kit.js` is needed.

Example markup:

```html
<header class="kit-header kit-navbar kit-navbar-expand-md">
  <a class="kit-brand" href="#base">Invoices <span>app</span></a>
  <nav class="kit-navbar-menu" id="nav-base" aria-label="Main">
    <ul class="kit-nav">
      <li><a class="kit-nav-link" href="#base" aria-current="page">Home</a></li>
      <li><a class="kit-nav-link" href="#base">Documents</a></li>
      <li><a class="kit-nav-link" href="#base">Customers</a></li>
      <li><a class="kit-nav-link" href="#base" aria-disabled="true">Archive</a></li>
    </ul>
    <span class="kit-spacer"></span>
    <button class="kit-btn kit-btn-primary">New</button>
  </nav>
  <button class="kit-btn kit-btn-ghost kit-btn-icon kit-navbar-toggler" data-kit-nav="#nav-base" aria-controls="nav-base" aria-expanded="false" aria-label="Menu"><svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-menu"/></svg></button>
</header>
```

## Items

`kit-nav-link` is used on an `<a>` (or on a `<button>`). The current page is marked with `aria-current="page"` (or with the `is-active` class): besides the color, screen readers read it too. To disable an item there is `aria-disabled="true"` or the `disabled` attribute. Inside the item you can put an icon or a `kit-badge`.

Example markup:

```html
<ul class="kit-nav">
  <li><a class="kit-nav-link is-active" href="#items"><svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-home"/></svg>Home</a></li>
  <li><a class="kit-nav-link" href="#items">Messages <span class="kit-badge kit-badge-danger">3</span></a></li>
  <li><a class="kit-nav-link" href="#items" aria-disabled="true">Disabled</a></li>
</ul>
```

## Items with a dropdown menu

An item can open a menu: it is the same [dropdown menu](https://n1k1tas95.github.io/dashboard-kit/en/overlays.html) as for buttons (`kit-dropdown`, `kit-pop`, `kit-opt`), placed inside an `<li>`. The up and down arrows move through the items, Enter selects, Esc closes. In the collapsible menu the dropdowns open inline, below the item.

Example markup:

```html
<header class="kit-header kit-navbar kit-navbar-expand-md">
  <a class="kit-brand" href="#dropdown">Invoices <span>app</span></a>
  <nav class="kit-navbar-menu" id="nav-dd" aria-label="Main">
    <ul class="kit-nav">
      <li><a class="kit-nav-link" href="#dropdown" aria-current="page">Home</a></li>
      <li class="kit-dropdown">
        <button class="kit-nav-link" data-kit-toggle="#nav-dd-doc" aria-haspopup="menu" aria-expanded="false">Documents<svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-chev"/></svg></button>
        <div class="kit-pop" id="nav-dd-doc" role="menu" hidden>
          <div class="kit-pop-group">Invoices</div>
          <a class="kit-opt" role="menuitem" href="#dropdown">Received</a>
          <a class="kit-opt" role="menuitem" href="#dropdown">Issued</a>
          <div class="kit-pop-sep"></div>
          <a class="kit-opt" role="menuitem" href="#dropdown">Credit notes</a>
        </div>
      </li>
      <li class="kit-dropdown">
        <button class="kit-nav-link" data-kit-toggle="#nav-dd-rep" aria-haspopup="menu" aria-expanded="false">Report<svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-chev"/></svg></button>
        <div class="kit-pop" id="nav-dd-rep" role="menu" hidden>
          <a class="kit-opt" role="menuitem" href="#dropdown">By year</a>
          <a class="kit-opt" role="menuitem" href="#dropdown">By supplier</a>
        </div>
      </li>
    </ul>
  </nav>
  <button class="kit-btn kit-btn-ghost kit-btn-icon kit-navbar-toggler" data-kit-nav="#nav-dd" aria-controls="nav-dd" aria-expanded="false" aria-label="Menu"><svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-menu"/></svg></button>
</header>
```

## Search, theme and actions

After `kit-spacer` goes what sits on the right: a search field, the settings panel, a user menu. What you put _inside_ `kit-navbar-menu` hides with the menu. What you put in `kit-navbar-actions`, _after_ the menu and before the button, always stays visible: it is the right place for theme and user.

Example markup:

```html
<header class="kit-header kit-navbar kit-navbar-expand-lg">
  <a class="kit-brand" href="#actions">Invoices <span>app</span></a>
  <nav class="kit-navbar-menu" id="nav-az" aria-label="Main">
    <ul class="kit-nav">
      <li><a class="kit-nav-link" href="#actions" aria-current="page">Home</a></li>
      <li><a class="kit-nav-link" href="#actions">Documents</a></li>
      <li><a class="kit-nav-link" href="#actions">Customers</a></li>
    </ul>
    <span class="kit-spacer"></span>
    <input class="kit-input" type="search" placeholder="Search…" aria-label="Search" style="max-width: 16rem">
  </nav>
  <div class="kit-navbar-actions">
    <div class="kit-dropdown">
      <button class="kit-btn kit-btn-icon kit-btn-ghost" data-kit-toggle="#nav-user" aria-haspopup="menu" aria-expanded="false" aria-label="Account"><svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-user"/></svg></button>
      <div class="kit-pop kit-pop-right" id="nav-user" role="menu" hidden>
        <a class="kit-opt" role="menuitem" href="#actions">Profile</a>
        <a class="kit-opt kit-opt-danger" role="menuitem" href="#actions">Sign out</a>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <button class="kit-btn kit-btn-ghost kit-btn-icon kit-navbar-toggler" data-kit-nav="#nav-az" aria-controls="nav-az" aria-expanded="false" aria-label="Menu"><svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-menu"/></svg></button>
</header>
```

The order in the code matters: logo, menu, `kit-navbar-actions`, button. The collapsible menu is out of the flow, so on a small screen only the logo, actions and button remain on the bar.

## When it opens inline

| Class | Inline from |
|---|---|
| `kit-navbar-expand-sm` | 576px |
| `kit-navbar-expand-md` | 768px |
| `kit-navbar-expand-lg` | 992px |
| `kit-navbar-expand-xl` | 1200px |
| none | never: the button is always there |

They are the same breakpoints as the [grid](https://n1k1tas95.github.io/dashboard-kit/en/grid.html). With too many items pick a higher one: if the items do not fit, they wrap or overflow the bar.

## Collapsible menu

On a small screen the menu drops below the bar, full width, and scrolls if it is taller than the window. Below, the navbar without `kit-navbar-expand-*`, so the button is always there.

Example markup:

```html
<header class="kit-header kit-navbar">
  <a class="kit-brand" href="#collapsible">Invoices <span>app</span></a>
  <nav class="kit-navbar-menu" id="nav-sc" aria-label="Main">
    <ul class="kit-nav">
      <li><a class="kit-nav-link" href="#collapsible" aria-current="page">Home</a></li>
      <li class="kit-dropdown">
        <button class="kit-nav-link" data-kit-toggle="#nav-sc-d" aria-haspopup="menu" aria-expanded="false">Documents<svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-chev"/></svg></button>
        <div class="kit-pop" id="nav-sc-d" role="menu" hidden>
          <a class="kit-opt" role="menuitem" href="#collapsible">Received</a>
          <a class="kit-opt" role="menuitem" href="#collapsible">Issued</a>
        </div>
      </li>
      <li><a class="kit-nav-link" href="#collapsible">Customers</a></li>
    </ul>
    <input class="kit-input" type="search" placeholder="Search…" aria-label="Search">
  </nav>
  <button class="kit-btn kit-btn-ghost kit-btn-icon kit-navbar-toggler" data-kit-nav="#nav-sc" aria-controls="nav-sc" aria-expanded="false" aria-label="Menu"><svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-menu"/></svg></button>
</header>
```
- It closes with a second click on the button, with Esc (focus returns to the button), by clicking outside the bar or by choosing a link in the menu.
- If the window widens past the breakpoint, the "open" state is reset.
- The button has `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`, updated by `kit.js`.

## Aligned with the content: kit-container

As with the normal header, put a container inside the navbar: the bar stays as wide as the window (with the background and border), but logo, items and actions align with the page content. The container becomes the navbar's inner row. The collapsible menu stays as wide as the window.

| Class | Effect on the navbar |
|---|---|
| `kit-container` | Centered, with maximum width `--kit-container-w`. It follows the global switch `data-layout="boxed\|fluid"`: with `fluid` it fills the whole window, like the content. |
| `kit-container-boxed` | Always centered, whatever the switch. |
| `kit-container-fluid` | Always full width. |
| none | The whole window, with only the header's side margin. |

In the examples the maximum width is reduced to 36rem, just to show the difference; the dashed box is the container. The first is `kit-container-boxed`, the second `kit-container-fluid`.

Example markup:

```html
<header class="kit-header kit-navbar kit-navbar-expand-md" style="--kit-container-w: 36rem">
  <div class="kit-container-boxed">
    <a class="kit-brand" href="#container">Boxed</a>
    <nav class="kit-navbar-menu" id="nav-c1" aria-label="Main">
      <ul class="kit-nav">
        <li><a class="kit-nav-link" href="#container" aria-current="page">Home</a></li>
        <li><a class="kit-nav-link" href="#container">Documents</a></li>
      </ul>
      <span class="kit-spacer"></span>
      <button class="kit-btn kit-btn-primary">New</button>
    </nav>
    <button class="kit-btn kit-btn-ghost kit-btn-icon kit-navbar-toggler" data-kit-nav="#nav-c1" aria-controls="nav-c1" aria-expanded="false" aria-label="Menu"><svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-menu"/></svg></button>
  </div>
</header>
```

Example markup:

```html
<header class="kit-header kit-navbar kit-navbar-expand-md" style="--kit-container-w: 36rem">
  <div class="kit-container-fluid">
    <a class="kit-brand" href="#container">Fluid</a>
    <nav class="kit-navbar-menu" id="nav-c2" aria-label="Main">
      <ul class="kit-nav">
        <li><a class="kit-nav-link" href="#container" aria-current="page">Home</a></li>
        <li><a class="kit-nav-link" href="#container">Documents</a></li>
      </ul>
      <span class="kit-spacer"></span>
      <button class="kit-btn kit-btn-primary">New</button>
    </nav>
    <button class="kit-btn kit-btn-ghost kit-btn-icon kit-navbar-toggler" data-kit-nav="#nav-c2" aria-controls="nav-c2" aria-expanded="false" aria-label="Menu"><svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-menu"/></svg></button>
  </div>
</header>
```

The container goes inside the navbar and the page content (`.kit-main`) uses the same one: this way navbar and page stay aligned, even when the user changes width from the [settings](https://n1k1tas95.github.io/dashboard-kit/en/theming.html).

The collapsible menu (`kit-navbar-menu`) is positioned relative to the navbar, not to the container: that is why it stays full width.

## Vertical list

`kit-nav-col` lays the items out in a column: for a side menu, or for a list of sections.

Example markup:

```html
<ul class="kit-nav kit-nav-col" style="max-width: 14rem">
  <li><a class="kit-nav-link is-active" href="#vertical">Overview</a></li>
  <li><a class="kit-nav-link" href="#vertical">Documents</a></li>
  <li><a class="kit-nav-link" href="#vertical">Settings</a></li>
</ul>
```

## Accessibility
- Put the list inside a `<nav>` with `aria-label` (if there is more than one on the page).
- Items are real links and buttons: they can be reached with Tab and have a focus ring.
- The menu button has an `aria-label`, because it contains only an icon.

---

# Tabs and breadcrumb
Page: https://n1k1tas95.github.io/dashboard-kit/en/navigation.html

Tabs, segmented control, pills, chips and breadcrumb: ways to choose what to show, to filter and to find your way.

## Tabs

With `data-kit-tabs` and `kit.js` the tabs show the panel indicated by `data-kit-panel` and move with the arrow keys. Inside the tab bar you can put `kit-spacer` and some buttons on the right.

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-tabs" data-kit-tabs>
  <button class="kit-tab is-on" data-kit-panel="#tab-uno">Documents</button>
  <button class="kit-tab" data-kit-panel="#tab-due">Customers</button>
  <span class="kit-spacer"></span>
  <button class="kit-btn kit-btn-ghost"><svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-download"/></svg>Export</button>
</div>
<section class="kit-card kit-card-body kit-tabpanel" id="tab-uno">Documents content.</section>
<section class="kit-card kit-card-body kit-tabpanel" id="tab-due" hidden>Customers content.</section>
```

## Segmented control

A few exclusive options, to change view or filter. The active option has `is-on` (or `aria-pressed="true"`): activating it is your code's job.

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-seg" role="group" aria-label="Direction" data-doc-seg>
  <button class="is-on">All</button><button>Received</button><button>Issued</button>
</div>
```

## Pill

Selectable filters, optionally with a counter in `<small>`.

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-bar" data-doc-seg>
  <button class="kit-pill is-on">2026 <small>124</small></button>
  <button class="kit-pill">2025 <small>98</small></button>
  <button class="kit-pill">2024 <small>71</small></button>
</div>
```

## Chip

Active filters, removable with a click. Here the example really removes them.

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-bar">
  <button class="kit-chip"><b>Year</b> 2026 <i>×</i></button>
  <button class="kit-chip"><b>Amount</b> &gt; €100 <i>×</i></button>
</div>
```

## Breadcrumb

It shows where you are in the site hierarchy and lets you go back up. It is CSS only: a `<nav class="kit-breadcrumb">` with an `<ol>`, one `<li>` per level and `aria-current="page"` on the last one, which is the current page and not a link. The separator is drawn by CSS, so the screen reader reads only the names. The `<nav>` needs an `aria-label` (for example "Breadcrumb") to tell it apart from the others.

Example markup:

```html
<nav class="kit-breadcrumb" aria-label="Breadcrumb">
  <ol>
    <li><a href="#">Home</a></li>
    <li><a href="#">Invoices</a></li>
    <li><a href="#">2026</a></li>
    <li aria-current="page">FT-0042</li>
  </ol>
</nav>
```

### Separator and icon

By default the separator is a small arrow; `kit-breadcrumb-slash` uses the slash. An icon (`kit-icon`) before an item's text aligns by itself: usually the house for the first one.

Example markup:

```html
<nav class="kit-breadcrumb kit-breadcrumb-slash" aria-label="Breadcrumb">
  <ol>
    <li><a href="#"><svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-home"/></svg>Home</a></li>
    <li><a href="#">Customers</a></li>
    <li aria-current="page">Alpha Services Ltd</li>
  </ol>
</nav>
```

### Long paths on narrow screens

With `kit-breadcrumb-collapse`, below 576px only the first and last items remain, on a single line (the last one is shortened with an ellipsis if it does not fit). In place of the hidden items a `kit-breadcrumb-more` item with "…" appears, which you write after the first one and which is only visible on those screens; it is `aria-hidden` because the hidden items are not read. Narrow the window to see it.

Example markup:

```html
<nav class="kit-breadcrumb kit-breadcrumb-collapse" aria-label="Breadcrumb">
  <ol>
    <li><a href="#">Home</a></li>
    <li class="kit-breadcrumb-more" aria-hidden="true">…</li>
    <li><a href="#">Accounting</a></li>
    <li><a href="#">Sales invoices</a></li>
    <li><a href="#">2026</a></li>
    <li aria-current="page">FT-0042 · Alpha Services Ltd</li>
  </ol>
</nav>
```

With a `kit-header` or at the top of a page the breadcrumb sits well above the title, with a `margin-bottom` of one or two spacing units. If the server computes the levels (Django, for example) a loop is enough that writes an `<li>` with a link for each ancestor and the last one with `aria-current`.

---

# Dialogs and menus
Page: https://n1k1tas95.github.io/dashboard-kit/en/overlays.html

Dialog windows, pop-up menus and temporary messages. They require `kit.js`.

## Dialog

It uses the native `<dialog>` element: the browser handles focus, the Esc key and the darkened backdrop. The kit adds the style and two attributes: `data-kit-open` to open it, `data-kit-close` to close it. A click on the backdrop closes it.

The dialog is a [card](https://n1k1tas95.github.io/dashboard-kit/en/cards.html#card) overlay: it has the same three parts (`kit-card-head`, `kit-card-body`, `kit-card-foot`), the same padding and the same border. If the content is tall, only the body scrolls; title and buttons stay visible. This also holds if the three parts are inside a `<form>` (`<form method="dialog">`). If instead the content is placed directly in the dialog, without `kit-card-body`, the whole dialog scrolls.

The width is chosen with a class: `kit-dialog-sm` (340px), no class (440px), `kit-dialog-lg` (700px, also `kit-dialog-wide`), `kit-dialog-xl` (960px) and `kit-dialog-full` (the whole window minus the margins). For your own value set `--kit-dialog-w`: on a single dialog (`style="--kit-dialog-w: 520px"`) or on all of them (`:root { --kit-dialog-w: 520px }`). On narrow screens the dialog never goes outside the window.

Example markup:

```html
  <button class="kit-btn" data-kit-open="#dlg-sm">Small</button>
  <button class="kit-btn" data-kit-open="#dlg-lg">Wide</button>
  <button class="kit-btn" data-kit-open="#dlg-xl">Extra wide</button>
  <button class="kit-btn" data-kit-open="#dlg-custom">Custom 520px</button>
<dialog class="kit-dialog kit-dialog-sm" id="dlg-sm"><div class="kit-card-head">kit-dialog-sm</div><div class="kit-card-body">340px.</div><div class="kit-card-foot"><button class="kit-btn" data-kit-close>Close</button></div></dialog>
<dialog class="kit-dialog kit-dialog-lg" id="dlg-lg"><div class="kit-card-head">kit-dialog-lg</div><div class="kit-card-body">700px.</div><div class="kit-card-foot"><button class="kit-btn" data-kit-close>Close</button></div></dialog>
<dialog class="kit-dialog kit-dialog-xl" id="dlg-xl"><div class="kit-card-head">kit-dialog-xl</div><div class="kit-card-body">960px.</div><div class="kit-card-foot"><button class="kit-btn" data-kit-close>Close</button></div></dialog>
<dialog class="kit-dialog" id="dlg-custom" style="--kit-dialog-w: 520px"><div class="kit-card-head">--kit-dialog-w: 520px</div><div class="kit-card-body">Custom width.</div><div class="kit-card-foot"><button class="kit-btn" data-kit-close>Close</button></div></dialog>
```

On opening, focus goes to the dialog itself, so no ring appears on the first button. To bring it to a field put `autofocus` on that field.

Example markup:

```html
<button class="kit-btn kit-btn-primary" data-kit-open="#dlg">Open the dialog</button>
<dialog class="kit-dialog" id="dlg">
  <div class="kit-card-head">
    Dialog title
    <button class="kit-btn kit-btn-ghost kit-btn-icon" data-kit-close aria-label="Close"><svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-x"/></svg></button>
  </div>
  <div class="kit-card-body">
    <p class="kit-mute">It closes with Esc, with a click on the backdrop, with the X or with the buttons.</p>
    <label class="kit-field">Name <input class="kit-input" placeholder="John Smith"></label>
  </div>
  <div class="kit-card-foot">
    <button class="kit-btn" data-kit-close>Cancel</button>
    <button class="kit-btn kit-btn-primary" data-kit-close>Confirm</button>
  </div>
</dialog>
```

## Drawer

A dialog that slides in from an edge of the window: for a detail, an advanced filter or a long form, when you want to keep the page in view. It is the same `<dialog>`, with the same parts, the same attributes (`data-kit-open`, `data-kit-close`) and the same Esc, backdrop click and focus; you only add the `kit-drawer` class. By default it comes from the right; `kit-drawer-left`, `kit-drawer-top` and `kit-drawer-bottom` change the side. On a narrow screen it takes the full width.

Example markup:

```html
<button class="kit-btn" data-kit-open="#drw-right">From the right</button>
<button class="kit-btn" data-kit-open="#drw-left">From the left</button>
<button class="kit-btn" data-kit-open="#drw-bottom">From the bottom</button>
<dialog class="kit-dialog kit-drawer" id="drw-right">
  <div class="kit-card-head">
    Filters
    <button class="kit-btn kit-btn-ghost kit-btn-icon" data-kit-close aria-label="Close"><svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-x"/></svg></button>
  </div>
  <div class="kit-card-body kit-stack">
    <label class="kit-field">Customer <input class="kit-input" placeholder="Smith Ltd"></label>
    <label class="kit-field">From <input class="kit-input" type="date"></label>
    <label class="kit-field">To <input class="kit-input" type="date"></label>
  </div>
  <div class="kit-card-foot">
    <button class="kit-btn" data-kit-close>Cancel</button>
    <button class="kit-btn kit-btn-primary" data-kit-close>Apply</button>
  </div>
</dialog>
<dialog class="kit-dialog kit-drawer kit-drawer-left kit-drawer-sm" id="drw-left">
  <div class="kit-card-head">Menu<button class="kit-btn kit-btn-ghost kit-btn-icon" data-kit-close aria-label="Close"><svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-x"/></svg></button></div>
  <div class="kit-card-body"><p class="kit-mute">A narrow drawer from the left: <code>kit-drawer-left kit-drawer-sm</code>.</p></div>
</dialog>
<dialog class="kit-dialog kit-drawer kit-drawer-bottom" id="drw-bottom">
  <div class="kit-card-head">Summary<button class="kit-btn kit-btn-ghost kit-btn-icon" data-kit-close aria-label="Close"><svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-x"/></svg></button></div>
  <div class="kit-card-body"><p class="kit-mute">From the bottom, at most <code>--kit-drawer-h</code> tall (40% of the window).</p></div>
</dialog>
```

The width is `--kit-drawer-w` (420px), or a class: `kit-drawer-sm` (320px), `kit-drawer-lg` (640px), `kit-drawer-xl` (860px). For top and bottom drawers the maximum height is `--kit-drawer-h`. The animation (0.25 s) is turned off by `prefers-reduced-motion` and, like the dialog's, requires a recent browser. If the detail has to stay next to a list rather than overlay it, use the [side panel](https://n1k1tas95.github.io/dashboard-kit/en/layout.html#split).

## Asking for confirmation

A dialog with "Confirm" and "Cancel" interrupts whoever is working, and if it appears too often people learn to press "Confirm" without reading. It is better to choose based on how serious the mistake would be.

| If the action… | Use |
|---|---|
| can be undone (archiving, moving, deleting with a trash) | [Undo](#undo): the action runs immediately and the toast offers "Undo" |
| cannot be undone (deleting forever, sending, paying) | [Confirm](#confirm-js) with `Kit.confirm` or `data-kit-confirm` |
| is very serious or concerns a lot of data (deleting an archive) | Confirm by [typing the name](#confirm-name) |

In any case: write the precise verb on the confirm button ("Delete 12 invoices", not "OK"), and say in the text what happens.

### Kit.confirm

`Kit.confirm(question, options)` opens the dialog by itself, without HTML, and returns a promise: `true` if the user confirms, `false` with "Cancel", Esc or a click on the backdrop. With `danger: true` the button is red and focus starts on "Cancel", so an absent-minded Enter does no harm; without it, focus is on "Confirm".

Example markup:

```html
<button class="kit-btn" data-doc-run="confirm-base">Simple confirmation</button>
<button class="kit-btn kit-btn-danger" data-doc-run="confirm-danger">Dangerous action</button>
```

| Option | Values | Default |
|---|---|---|
| 1st argument | the question (dialog title) | `Confirm the action?` |
| `text` | explanation under the question | none |
| `confirm` · `cancel` | text of the two buttons | `Confirm` · `Cancel` |
| `danger` | `true`: red button, warning icon, focus on "Cancel" | `false` |
| `type` | text to type to enable the confirmation | none |

The text is always plain text, never HTML: you can also pass a name entered by the user. The dialog is a `<dialog>` with `role="alertdialog"`: Tab stays inside, Esc cancels and on closing focus returns to the button that opened it.

### Typing the name

For truly irreversible actions, `type` asks to write a text (usually the name of what is being deleted): until it matches, "Confirm" stays disabled. Case matters; spaces at the edges do not. Enter in the field confirms, if the text is right.

Example markup:

```html
<button class="kit-btn kit-btn-danger" data-doc-run="confirm-type">Delete the archive…</button>
```

### Without JavaScript: data-kit-confirm

Put `data-kit-confirm="Question?"` on a button, a link or a `<form>`: the click (or the form submit) opens the dialog and, only if the user confirms, the action proceeds as if nothing had been in between. The confirmation runs _before_ your click handlers, which only fire after the "yes". The other options are attributes: `data-kit-confirm-text`, `-ok`, `-cancel`, `-danger` (no value) and `-type`.

Example markup:

```html
<button class="kit-btn kit-btn-danger" data-kit-confirm="Delete invoice 2026/014?" data-kit-confirm-text="It will stay in the trash for 30 days." data-kit-confirm-ok="Delete invoice" data-kit-confirm-danger data-doc-toast="Invoice deleted" data-doc-type="success">Delete invoice</button>
<button class="kit-btn" data-kit-confirm="Send the invoices to the exchange system?" data-kit-confirm-ok="Send" data-doc-toast="Invoices sent" data-doc-type="success">Send</button>
```

### Undo instead of asking

For actions that can be undone, asking first is the worst choice: it slows everyone down to protect a few. `Kit.undo` does the opposite: the interface changes immediately and a toast with a time bar offers "Undo". When the time runs out (or the toast closes, or the page is left) `onCommit` runs, the real and final action; with "Undo" `onUndo` runs and `onCommit` never does.

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-bar" id="doc-undo-row">
  <span>Invoice 2026/014 · Smith Ltd</span>
  <span class="kit-spacer"></span>
  <button class="kit-btn kit-btn-danger" data-doc-run="undo">Delete</button>
</div>
<p class="kit-mute" id="doc-undo-note" hidden>The invoice is gone: now look at the toast.</p>
```

Options: `onUndo`, `onCommit`, `duration` (default 6000 ms), `label` (default "Undo"), `type` and `position` as in [toasts](#toast). It returns `{ undo(), commit() }` to decide from code. If `onCommit` has to reach a server, remember that when the page closes the browser may interrupt the request: use `fetch` with `keepalive: true`.

### Animation

All `kit-dialog`s appear and disappear with a short fade (0.18 s), a slight upward slide and the backdrop darkening. It turns itself off with `prefers-reduced-motion`. A recent browser is needed (Chrome 117, Safari 17.4, Firefox 129): in the others the dialog appears and disappears without animation, but works just the same.

## Pop-up menu

`.kit-pop` is a panel that can be used on its own, for any menu: a row's actions, a button's items, the theme selector. A button with `data-kit-toggle="#id"` opens the indicated `.kit-pop` (inside a `.kit-dropdown`, which positions it under the button). It closes with Esc, by clicking outside or by choosing an item; the arrow keys move through the items, Enter activates them.

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-dropdown">
  <button class="kit-btn" data-kit-toggle="#menu-actions" aria-haspopup="menu" aria-expanded="false">Actions<svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-chev"/></svg></button>
  <div class="kit-pop" id="menu-actions" role="menu" hidden>
    <div class="kit-opt" role="menuitem"><svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-download"/></svg><span class="kit-opt-text"><b>Export CSV</b><small>All the filtered rows</small></span></div>
    <div class="kit-opt" role="menuitem"><svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-search"/></svg><span class="kit-opt-text"><b>Search documents</b></span></div>
  </div>
</div>
```

### Items: buttons, links, separators

A `.kit-opt` item can be a `<div>`, a `<button>` or an `<a>`: use the button for an action and the link to change page. `kit-opt-danger` colors destructive actions, `kit-pop-sep` separates groups, `kit-pop-group` titles them and `aria-disabled="true"` disables an item.

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-dropdown">
  <button class="kit-btn" data-kit-toggle="#menu-items-1" aria-haspopup="menu" aria-expanded="false">Invoice<svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-chev"/></svg></button>
  <div class="kit-pop" id="menu-items-1" role="menu" hidden>
    <div class="kit-pop-group">Document</div>
    <button class="kit-opt" role="menuitem" data-doc-toast="Copied"><svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-copy"/></svg><span class="kit-opt-text"><b>Copy number</b></span></button>
    <a class="kit-opt" role="menuitem" href="#menu-items"><svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-external"/></svg><span class="kit-opt-text"><b>Open in a page</b></span></a>
    <button class="kit-opt" role="menuitem" aria-disabled="true"><svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-download"/></svg><span class="kit-opt-text"><b>Download PDF</b><small>Not available</small></span></button>
    <div class="kit-pop-sep" role="separator"></div>
    <button class="kit-opt kit-opt-danger" role="menuitem" data-doc-toast="Deleted"><svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-trash"/></svg><span class="kit-opt-text"><b>Delete</b></span></button>
  </div>
</div>
```

### Icon-only button

The classic "more actions" menu of a row. With `kit-pop-right` the panel aligns to the button's right edge, so it does not go off the page.

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-bar" style="justify-content: space-between">
  <span>Invoice 2026/0142</span>
  <div class="kit-dropdown">
    <button class="kit-btn kit-btn-ghost kit-btn-icon" data-kit-toggle="#menu-more" aria-haspopup="menu" aria-expanded="false" aria-label="More actions"><svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-more-v"/></svg></button>
    <div class="kit-pop kit-pop-right" id="menu-more" role="menu" hidden>
      <button class="kit-opt" role="menuitem"><svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-edit"/></svg><span class="kit-opt-text"><b>Edit</b></span></button>
      <button class="kit-opt" role="menuitem"><svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-copy"/></svg><span class="kit-opt-text"><b>Duplicate</b></span></button>
      <div class="kit-pop-sep" role="separator"></div>
      <button class="kit-opt kit-opt-danger" role="menuitem"><svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-trash"/></svg><span class="kit-opt-text"><b>Delete</b></span></button>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

### Split button

The main action on the left, the arrow with the alternatives on the right. `kit-btn-split` joins the two buttons.

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-btn-split">
  <button class="kit-btn kit-btn-primary"><svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-download"/></svg>Export CSV</button>
  <div class="kit-dropdown">
    <button class="kit-btn kit-btn-primary kit-btn-icon" data-kit-toggle="#menu-split-1" aria-haspopup="menu" aria-expanded="false" aria-label="Other formats"><svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-chev"/></svg></button>
    <div class="kit-pop kit-pop-right" id="menu-split-1" role="menu" hidden>
      <button class="kit-opt" role="menuitem"><span class="kit-opt-text"><b>Export Excel</b></span></button>
      <button class="kit-opt" role="menuitem"><span class="kit-opt-text"><b>Export PDF</b></span></button>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

### Upwards

Near the bottom edge of the page add `kit-pop-up`: the panel opens above the button.

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-dropdown">
  <button class="kit-btn" data-kit-toggle="#menu-up-1" aria-haspopup="menu" aria-expanded="false">Sort by<svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-chev"/></svg></button>
  <div class="kit-pop kit-pop-up" id="menu-up-1" role="menu" hidden>
    <button class="kit-opt" role="menuitem"><span class="kit-opt-text"><b>Date</b></span></button>
    <button class="kit-opt" role="menuitem"><span class="kit-opt-text"><b>Amount</b></span></button>
    <button class="kit-opt" role="menuitem"><span class="kit-opt-text"><b>Supplier</b></span></button>
  </div>
</div>
```

### Always visible

Without a button and without `hidden`, with `kit-pop-static`, the panel stays in the page flow: it is for a side menu or a list of actions. The items are normal buttons or links, so they can be reached with Tab.

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-pop kit-pop-static" role="menu" style="max-width: 260px">
  <div class="kit-pop-group">Account</div>
  <a class="kit-opt" role="menuitem" href="#menu-static"><svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-user"/></svg><span class="kit-opt-text"><b>Profile</b></span></a>
  <a class="kit-opt" role="menuitem" href="#menu-static"><svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-sliders"/></svg><span class="kit-opt-text"><b>Settings</b></span></a>
  <div class="kit-pop-sep" role="separator"></div>
  <button class="kit-opt kit-opt-danger" role="menuitem"><span class="kit-opt-text"><b>Sign out</b></span></button>
</div>
```

## Tooltip

A short hint on any element, with CSS only: the `data-kit-tip` attribute is enough. It appears on mouse hover (after a short wait) and on keyboard focus; with `kit.js` the Esc key hides it. The mouse can reach the tooltip without it disappearing.

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-bar">
  <button class="kit-btn kit-btn-icon" data-kit-tip="Download the list as CSV" aria-label="Download"><svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-download"/></svg></button>
  <button class="kit-btn kit-btn-icon" data-kit-tip="Refresh" aria-label="Refresh"><svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-refresh"/></svg></button>
  <span class="kit-badge kit-badge-warning" data-kit-tip="Waiting for the tax authority receipt">Received</span>
  <a href="#tooltip" data-kit-tip="Back to the start of this section">A link</a>
</div>
```

### Position

`data-kit-tip-pos` chooses the side: `top` (default), `bottom`, `left`, `right`.

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-bar" style="justify-content: center">
  <button class="kit-btn" data-kit-tip="Above" data-kit-tip-pos="top">Top</button>
  <button class="kit-btn" data-kit-tip="Below" data-kit-tip-pos="bottom">Bottom</button>
  <button class="kit-btn" data-kit-tip="To the left" data-kit-tip-pos="left">Left</button>
  <button class="kit-btn" data-kit-tip="To the right" data-kit-tip-pos="right">Right</button>
</div>
```

The tooltip is not a way to provide a label: an icon-only button must still have `aria-label`. Do not put essential information, links or buttons in it, because on touch and for screen reader users it may not appear. A `disabled` button does not receive the mouse: put the tooltip on a `<span>` that contains it.

A container with hidden or scrolling `overflow` (for example `.kit-table-wrap`) clips the tooltip: in that case choose a side that stays inside the container.

## Toast

A short message that appears at the bottom and disappears by itself. It is shown from JavaScript with `Kit.toast("text")`; several toasts stack, up to six at a time. The neutral toast is inverted relative to the theme (dark on light, light on dark), so it always stands out from the content; colored ones fill the whole background.

Example markup:

```html
<button class="kit-btn" data-doc-toast="Saved!">Show a toast</button>
```

### Types, title and icon

The `type` option (`info`, `success`, `warning`, `danger`) colors the whole toast and adds the icon, if the page has the [icons](https://n1k1tas95.github.io/dashboard-kit/en/icons.html) sprite (`kit-icons.js`); `title` adds a title. `warning` and `danger` toasts are announced immediately by screen readers (`role="alert"`), the others discreetly.

Example markup:

```html
<button class="kit-btn" data-doc-toast="A new version is available." data-doc-type="info">Info</button>
<button class="kit-btn" data-doc-toast="24 invoices added." data-doc-type="success" data-doc-title="Import completed">Success</button>
<button class="kit-btn" data-doc-toast="Check the VAT number." data-doc-type="warning">Warning</button>
<button class="kit-btn" data-doc-toast="Unable to read the file." data-doc-type="danger" data-doc-title="Error">Error</button>
```

### Action and closing

With `action` the toast has a button (typically "Undo") and stays visible until you use it or close it with the **×**. `duration` is in milliseconds (default 4000); with `0` the toast does not disappear by itself. A bar at the bottom of the toast shows how long is left before closing (remove it with `progress: false`). The time stops while the mouse or focus is on the toast, and the bar goes back to full: when you leave, the countdown restarts from the beginning. `Kit.toast` returns an object with `close()` to close it from code, and `Kit.toast.clear()` closes them all.

Example markup:

```html
<button class="kit-btn" data-doc-toast="Invoice deleted." data-doc-action="Undo">With an action</button>
<button class="kit-btn" data-doc-toast="Syncing…" data-doc-duration="0">Stays until you close it</button>
<button class="kit-btn kit-btn-ghost" data-doc-toast-clear>Close all</button>
```

### Position

`position` chooses where it appears: `bottom` (default), `top`, `bottom-start`, `bottom-end`, `top-start`, `top-end`. The corners are the most used in dashboards, because they do not cover the central content.

Example markup:

```html
<button class="kit-btn" data-doc-toast="Top center" data-doc-pos="top">Top</button>
<button class="kit-btn" data-doc-toast="Top right" data-doc-pos="top-end" data-doc-type="success">Top right</button>
<button class="kit-btn" data-doc-toast="Bottom right" data-doc-pos="bottom-end" data-doc-type="info">Bottom right</button>
<button class="kit-btn" data-doc-toast="Bottom left" data-doc-pos="bottom-start">Bottom left</button>
```

| Option | Values | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `type` | `info` · `success` · `warning` · `danger` | neutral |
| `title` | text | no title |
| `duration` | milliseconds; `0` = does not disappear | `4000` |
| `position` | see above | `bottom` |
| `action` | `{ label, onClick }` | none |
| `progress` | `true` · `false` | `true` (remaining-time bar, if `duration` > 0) |
| `closable` | `true` · `false` | `true` with an action or `duration: 0` |

The toast text is always plain text: `Kit.toast` never interprets HTML, so you can also pass a value entered by the user.

## Settings panel

A single menu for the user's preferences: **theme** (automatic, light, dark), **text size** and **content width**, plus "Reset". It is a [pop-up menu](#menu) with the `kit-settings` class, made of `kit-seg` groups whose buttons use the `kit.js` attributes you already know (`data-kit-theme-set`, `data-kit-fs-set`, `data-kit-layout-set`). Unlike a normal menu it stays open after each choice, so you can change several things in a row; it closes with Esc or by clicking outside. All choices are remembered. The rows are independent: remove the ones you do not need. `data-kit-reset` (or `Kit.reset()`) brings everything back to the starting value: system theme, normal text, the width written in the HTML. It is the "Settings" menu at the top right of these pages.

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-dropdown">
  <button class="kit-btn" data-kit-toggle="#demo-settings" aria-haspopup="true" aria-expanded="false"><svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-sliders"/></svg><span class="kit-d-none kit-d-sm-inline">Settings</span><svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-chev"/></svg></button>
  <div class="kit-pop kit-pop-right kit-settings" id="demo-settings" role="group" aria-label="Settings" hidden>
    <div class="kit-settings-row">
      <span class="kit-settings-label">Theme</span>
      <div class="kit-seg" role="group" aria-label="Theme">
        <button data-kit-theme-set="auto"><svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-auto"/></svg>Auto</button>
        <button data-kit-theme-set="light"><svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-sun"/></svg>Light</button>
        <button data-kit-theme-set="dark"><svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-moon"/></svg>Dark</button>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="kit-settings-row">
      <span class="kit-settings-label">Text size</span>
      <div class="kit-seg" role="group" aria-label="Text size">
        <button data-kit-fs-set="md" aria-label="Normal" title="Normal">A</button>
        <button data-kit-fs-set="lg" aria-label="Large" title="Large">A</button>
        <button data-kit-fs-set="xl" aria-label="Extra large" title="Extra large">A</button>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="kit-settings-row">
      <span class="kit-settings-label">Content width</span>
      <div class="kit-seg" role="group" aria-label="Content width">
        <button data-kit-layout-set="boxed">Centered</button>
        <button data-kit-layout-set="fluid">Full page</button>
      </div>
      <small>Noticeable on screens wider than the content.</small>
    </div>
    <div class="kit-settings-foot"><button class="kit-btn kit-btn-ghost" data-kit-reset>Reset</button></div>
  </div>
</div>
```

---

# Sidebar
Page: https://n1k1tas95.github.io/dashboard-kit/en/sidebar.html

The navigation bar on the left, with header, items, sub-items, account and utilities at the bottom. Slide-in on small screens, compact (icons only) on large ones.

## Structure

The sidebar sits inside `.kit-app`, next to `.kit-app-main`: on the left the full-height bar, on the right the column with the header (`.kit-header`) and the content (`.kit-main`). The bar has three parts: `kit-sidebar-head` (logo), `kit-sidebar-body` (the items, scrolls by itself if there are many) and `kit-sidebar-foot` (account and utilities, always at the bottom).

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-app">
  <aside class="kit-sidebar" aria-label="Main (example)">
    <div class="kit-sidebar-head">
      <a class="kit-brand" href="#base"><svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-folder"/></svg><span class="kit-side-text">Invoices <span>app</span></span></a>
    </div>
    <nav class="kit-sidebar-body" aria-label="Sections">
      <ul class="kit-side-nav">
        <li><a class="kit-side-link" href="#base" aria-current="page"><svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-home"/></svg><span class="kit-side-text">Overview</span></a></li>
        <li><a class="kit-side-link" href="#base"><svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-bell"/></svg><span class="kit-side-text">Alerts</span><span class="kit-badge kit-badge-danger">3</span></a></li>
      </ul>
      <div class="kit-side-title">Documents</div>
      <ul class="kit-side-nav">
        <li><a class="kit-side-link" href="#base"><svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-file"/></svg><span class="kit-side-text">Invoices</span></a></li>
        <li><a class="kit-side-link" href="#base"><svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-calendar"/></svg><span class="kit-side-text">Due dates</span></a></li>
        <li><a class="kit-side-link" href="#base" aria-disabled="true"><svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-folder"/></svg><span class="kit-side-text">Archive</span></a></li>
      </ul>
    </nav>
    <div class="kit-sidebar-foot">
      <button class="kit-side-user" type="button">
        <span class="kit-side-avatar" aria-hidden="true">MS</span>
        <span class="kit-side-user-text"><b>Maria Smith</b><small>maria@example.com</small></span>
      </button>
    </div>
  </aside>
  <div class="kit-app-main">
    <header class="kit-header"><h2 class="kit-fs-4 kit-m-0">Overview</h2></header>
    <main class="kit-main"><p class="kit-mute">The page content.</p></main>
  </div>
</div>
```
- Each item is `kit-side-link` on an `<a>` or a `<button>`: icon, then the text inside `<span class="kit-side-text">` (needed, because it disappears in the compact version), then an optional badge.
- The current page is marked with `aria-current="page"` (or `is-active`); an unavailable item with `aria-disabled="true"`.
- `kit-side-title` is the title of a group of items; in the compact version it becomes a separator line.
- Give the `<aside>` an `id` and an `aria-label`.

## Together with the header

The header is the usual one (`kit-header`), but it sits inside `kit-app-main`, above the content. The button that opens the sidebar lives there: `data-kit-sidebar-toggle` with, if needed, the bar's selector. The logo sits at the top of the sidebar, with the same height as the header (`--kit-hh`), so the two separator lines meet.

```html
<div class="kit-app kit-app-expand-lg">
  <aside class="kit-sidebar" id="sidebar" aria-label="Main"> … </aside>
  <div class="kit-app-main">
    <header class="kit-header">
      <button class="kit-btn kit-btn-ghost kit-btn-icon" data-kit-sidebar-toggle="#sidebar"
              aria-controls="sidebar" aria-expanded="false" aria-label="Side menu">
        <svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-menu"/></svg>
      </button>
      …
    </header>
    <main class="kit-main"> … </main>
  </div>
</div>
```

A complete example, to try by resizing the window: [dashboard with sidebar](https://n1k1tas95.github.io/dashboard-kit/en/dashboard-sidebar.html).

## When it stays inline

| Class on `kit-app` | Inline from |
|---|---|
| `kit-app-expand-md` | 768px |
| `kit-app-expand-lg` | 992px |
| `kit-app-expand-xl` | 1200px |
| none | never: it is always slide-in |

Below that point the sidebar leaves the flow and sits off screen; the `data-kit-sidebar-toggle` button slides it in from the left, with the background darkening. It behaves like a dialog: the rest of the page cannot be reached (`inert`), focus moves to the bar, and it closes with Esc, with a click on the background or by choosing a link, returning focus to the button. If the window widens past the breakpoint, the "open" state is reset.

## Compact, icons only

On large screens the same button compresses the bar into a column of icons (`--kit-side-wc` wide) and expands it again. The choice is `<html data-kit-sidebar="collapsed|expanded">` and is remembered, like theme and text size. To start compact just write the attribute in the HTML.
- Texts, badges, arrows and sub-items disappear. Hovering the mouse or moving focus with Tab onto an icon, its name appears right next to it (with the badge number, for example "Alerts (3)"); this applies to items, utilities and the account. The name is taken from the item's `kit-side-text` or, for icon buttons, from their `aria-label`. Each item also gets an `aria-label` by itself, because the hidden text does not reach screen readers.
- Pressing an item with sub-items expands it again.
- `Kit.reset()` and the `data-kit-reset` button restore the state written in the HTML.

## Items with sub-items

An item with a submenu is a `<details class="kit-side-details">` with `<summary class="kit-side-link">`: it works without JavaScript and with the keyboard. The arrow is `kit-side-chev`; the sub-items are a second `kit-side-nav kit-side-sub`.

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-app">
  <aside class="kit-sidebar" aria-label="Sub-items (example)">
    <nav class="kit-sidebar-body" aria-label="Sections">
      <ul class="kit-side-nav">
        <li>
          <details class="kit-side-details" open>
            <summary class="kit-side-link"><svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-file"/></svg><span class="kit-side-text">Invoices</span><svg class="kit-icon kit-side-chev"><use href="#i-chev"/></svg></summary>
            <ul class="kit-side-nav kit-side-sub">
              <li><a class="kit-side-link" href="#subitems" aria-current="page"><span class="kit-side-text">Received</span></a></li>
              <li><a class="kit-side-link" href="#subitems"><span class="kit-side-text">Issued</span></a></li>
            </ul>
          </details>
        </li>
        <li><a class="kit-side-link" href="#subitems"><svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-user"/></svg><span class="kit-side-text">Customers</span></a></li>
      </ul>
    </nav>
  </aside>
</div>
```

## Account and utilities at the bottom
