In `kit-sidebar-foot` go the utilities (`kit-side-tools`: icon buttons, settings, help) and the account. The account is `kit-side-user` with `kit-side-avatar` (the initials) and `kit-side-user-text` (name and secondary line); its menu is a normal [pop-up menu](https://n1k1tas95.github.io/dashboard-kit/en/overlays.html) opened upwards with `kit-pop-up`.

```html
<div class="kit-sidebar-foot">
  <div class="kit-dropdown">
    <button class="kit-side-user" data-kit-toggle="#account" aria-haspopup="menu" aria-expanded="false">
      <span class="kit-side-avatar" aria-hidden="true">MR</span>
      <span class="kit-side-user-text"><b>Maria Smith</b><small>maria@example.com</small></span>
    </button>
    <div class="kit-pop kit-pop-up" id="account" role="menu" hidden>
      <a class="kit-opt" role="menuitem" href="#">Profile</a>
      <button class="kit-opt kit-opt-danger" role="menuitem">Sign out</button>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

## JavaScript

| What | Effect |
|---|---|
| `data-kit-sidebar-toggle="#id"` | Button: opens or closes the slide-in sidebar, or compresses or expands the inline one. Without a value it acts on the first `.kit-sidebar`. `aria-expanded` updates by itself. |
| `Kit.sidebar.get()` · `set("collapsed\|expanded")` · `toggle()` | The compact state, remembered. |
| `Kit.sidebar.open(selector)` · `close(selector)` | The slide-in sidebar; they do nothing if it is inline. |
| `kit:sidebar` event | On the sidebar (bubbles): `detail` is `{ collapsed, open }`. |

## Tokens and print
- `--kit-side-w` (16.5rem): width of the bar; `--kit-side-wc` (4.667rem): width of the compact one. They can be overridden on `:root` or on a single `.kit-app`.
- When printing the sidebar disappears, like the header.

---

# VS Code snippets
Page: https://n1k1tas95.github.io/dashboard-kit/en/snippets.html

Type the prefix and press Tab: the editor writes the component's markup, with the fields to fill in.

## Installation
- **One project only**: copy `vscode/dashboard-kit.code-snippets` into the project's `.vscode/` folder.
- **All projects**: in VS Code open _Preferences: Configure Snippets → New Global Snippets file_ and paste the file's content.

Then, in an `.html` file, type for example `kit-card` and press Tab. With `kit-page` you get a whole page; with `kit-dash` the layout of a dashboard (KPIs, chart with side panel, table).

## List of prefixes

| Prefix | Component |
|---|---|
| `kit-accordion` | Accordion with openable items (details), optionally only one open |
| `kit-alert` | Alert with colored border (success, warning, danger, neutral) |
| `kit-alert-close` | Alert with a close button |
| `kit-alert-icon` | Alert with icon (the symbol must be in the SVG sprite) |
| `kit-badge` | Badge (success, warning, danger, neutral) |
| `kit-bar` | Bar of side-by-side elements (toolbar, filters) |
| `kit-breadcrumb` | Navigation path (breadcrumb) |
| `kit-btn` | Button (variants: primary, ghost, danger, icon, lg) |
| `kit-btn-icon` | Square button with an icon only (SVG sprite) |
| `kit-btn-primary` | Primary button |
| `kit-card` | Card with header, body and footer |
| `kit-chart` | Bar chart in SVG (requires kit.js) |
| `kit-check-cards` | Radio buttons as cards |
| `kit-chip` | Removable chip |
| `kit-code` | Highlighted code block (with Copy button) |
| `kit-col` | Grid column (12 on phone, N/12 from a breakpoint) |
| `kit-combo` | Field with a list of suggestions (requires kit.js) |
| `kit-container` | Centered container (follows the data-layout switch; -boxed always centered) |
| `kit-container-fluid` | Container that is always full width |
| `kit-control` | Field with an icon on the left and a button on the right (also show/hide password) |
| `kit-dash` | Typical scheme: KPIs on top, chart + side panel, table |
| `kit-date` | Date field with the kit's calendar (locale format, ISO value) |
| `kit-daterange` | From–to range with a two-month calendar and quick picks |
| `kit-datetime` | Date and time field with calendar and hour and minute columns |
| `kit-dialog` | Dialog with an opening button (requires kit.js) |
| `kit-dropdown` | Button with a pop-up menu (requires kit.js) |
| `kit-empty` | Empty-state message |
| `kit-field` | Field with a label |
| `kit-field` | Field with label, help text and error message |
| `kit-float` | Field with the label inside that floats up |
| `kit-form` | Form with fields in a column and browser validation |
| `kit-form-h` | Form with the label on the left |
| `kit-grid` | Responsive grid (kit-grid-2 / kit-grid-3 for fixed columns) |
| `kit-header` | Fixed header with brand |
| `kit-header-container` | Header whose content aligns with the page's |
| `kit-icon` | Icon from the sprite (kit-icons.js) |
| `kit-input-group` | Field with attached text or button |
| `kit-kpi` | Card with label, value and change |
| `kit-kv` | Key/value list |
| `kit-layout` | Sets the width: boxed (centered) or fluid (full width) |
| `kit-layout-toggle` | Button that toggles centered / full-width content (requires kit.js) |
| `kit-list` | List of stacked items (joined cards) |
| `kit-meter` | Measure against a limit, with thresholds (needs kit.js for the automatic state) |
| `kit-navbar` | Navbar with items and collapsible menu (requires kit.js) |
| `kit-page` | Page skeleton with Dashboard Kit (CSS + optional JS) |
| `kit-pill` | Selectable pill with counter |
| `kit-progress` | Progress bar (0–100%) |
| `kit-prose` | Container for long texts: comfortable lines and generous line height |
| `kit-quote` | Quote with its source |
| `kit-row` | Row of the 12-column grid |
| `kit-row-cols` | Row with a fixed number of columns per row (2 on phone, 4 from lg) |
| `kit-search` | Search field with icon and shortcut |
| `kit-seg` | Segmented control (choose one item) |
| `kit-select` | Select with a list of options (requires kit.js) |
| `kit-settings` | Settings panel: theme, text size, width (requires kit.js) |
| `kit-sidebar` | Page with left sidebar and header (requires kit.js) |
| `kit-skeleton` | Loading placeholder |
| `kit-stats` | Stats row |
| `kit-switch` | On/off switch |
| `kit-table` | Table with header and a sample row |
| `kit-table-sort` | Table with sorting, search and pagination |
| `kit-tabs` | Tabs with panels (requires kit.js) |
| `kit-theme` | Sets the theme: auto, light or dark |
| `kit-time` | Time field (hh:mm) with hour and minute picker |
| `kit-tip` | Tooltip attributes (on any element) |
| `kit-toast` | Temporary message (requires kit.js) |

# Tables
Page: https://n1k1tas95.github.io/dashboard-kit/en/tables.html

Compact tables with a sticky header, selectable rows and aligned numbers.

## Table

Put the table in a card, inside `kit-table-wrap`, which makes it scroll horizontally on narrow screens. `kit-num` aligns right and gives the digits the same width; `kit-wrap` lets the text wrap.

Example markup:

```html
<section class="kit-card">
  <div class="kit-table-wrap">
    <table class="kit-table">
      <thead><tr><th>Date</th><th>Number</th><th>Customer</th><th class="kit-num">Amount</th></tr></thead>
      <tbody>
        <tr><td>03/12/2026</td><td>FT-0042</td><td class="kit-wrap">Alpha Services Ltd<small>VAT no. 01234567890</small></td><td class="kit-num">1,250.00</td></tr>
        <tr><td>03/02/2026</td><td>FT-0041</td><td class="kit-wrap">Beta Supplies Inc</td><td class="kit-num">830.40</td></tr>
        <tr><td>02/21/2026</td><td>FT-0040</td><td class="kit-wrap">Gamma Transport</td><td class="kit-num kit-danger">−310.00</td></tr>
      </tbody>
    </table>
  </div>
</section>
```

## Clickable and selected rows

`kit-table-hover` highlights the row under the mouse; `is-selected` on the `<tr>` marks it as chosen (useful with the [side panel](https://n1k1tas95.github.io/dashboard-kit/en/layout.html#split)).

Example markup:

```html
<section class="kit-card">
  <div class="kit-table-wrap">
    <table class="kit-table kit-table-hover">
      <thead><tr><th>Number</th><th>Status</th></tr></thead>
      <tbody>
        <tr><td>FT-0042</td><td><span class="kit-badge kit-badge-success">Issued</span></td></tr>
        <tr class="is-selected"><td>FT-0041</td><td><span class="kit-badge kit-badge-warning">Received</span></td></tr>
        <tr><td>FT-0040</td><td><span class="kit-badge kit-badge-danger">Discarded</span></td></tr>
      </tbody>
    </table>
  </div>
</section>
```

## Sorting

With `kit.js`, `data-kit-sort` on the table makes the headers clickable: the first click sorts ascending, the second descending, the third restores the starting order. The header gets `aria-sort` (`ascending`, `descending`, `none`) and a button is placed inside it, so it also works from the keyboard. The column type is recognized from its content: **numbers** in the page language's format (in English `1,250.00`, `−310.00`, `12 %`, `€ 5`; in Italian `1.250,00`), **dates** (`03/12/2026` in English, `12/03/2026` in Italian, `2026-03-12`, with the time if present) and **text**, compared ignoring case and accents and with "natural" numbers (`FT-9` before `FT-10`). Empty cells, or cells with just a dash, always go to the bottom; with equal values the starting order is kept. An `aria-sort="ascending|descending"` written in the HTML is the initial sort.

Example markup:

```html
<section class="kit-card">
  <div class="kit-table-wrap">
    <table class="kit-table" data-kit-sort>
      <thead><tr><th aria-sort="descending">Date</th><th>Number</th><th>Customer</th><th class="kit-num">Amount</th></tr></thead>
      <tbody>
        <tr><td>03/12/2026</td><td>FT-0042</td><td>Alpha Services Ltd</td><td class="kit-num">1,250.00</td></tr>
        <tr><td>03/02/2026</td><td>FT-0041</td><td>Beta Supplies Inc</td><td class="kit-num">830.40</td></tr>
        <tr><td>02/21/2026</td><td>FT-0040</td><td>Gamma Transport</td><td class="kit-num kit-danger">−310.00</td></tr>
        <tr><td>02/14/2026</td><td>FT-0039</td><td>Élite Consulting</td><td class="kit-num">12,400.00</td></tr>
        <tr><td>02/03/2026</td><td>FT-0038</td><td>Delta Systems</td><td class="kit-num">95.50</td></tr>
        <tr><td>01/28/2026</td><td>FT-0037</td><td>Alpha Services Ltd</td><td class="kit-num">2,100.00</td></tr>
        <tr><td>01/19/2026</td><td>FT-0036</td><td>Zeta Logistics</td><td class="kit-num kit-danger">−45.00</td></tr>
        <tr><td>01/09/2026</td><td>FT-0035</td><td>Beta Supplies Inc</td><td class="kit-num">1,980.00</td></tr>
        <tr><td>12/22/2025</td><td>FT-0034</td><td>Omega Studio</td><td class="kit-num">410.00</td></tr>
        <tr><td>12/11/2025</td><td>FT-0033</td><td>Gamma Transport</td><td class="kit-num">75.20</td></tr>
        <tr><td>11/30/2025</td><td>FT-0032</td><td>Delta Systems</td><td class="kit-num">3,300.00</td></tr>
        <tr><td>11/15/2025</td><td>FT-0031</td><td>Élite Consulting</td><td class="kit-num">620.00</td></tr>
      </tbody>
    </table>
  </div>
</section>
```

| Attribute | Where | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `data-kit-sort` | `<table>` | enables sorting on all columns; with `="multi"` also on several columns together |
| `data-kit-nosort` | `<th>` | excludes the column (for example the actions) |
| `data-kit-type="num\|date\|text"` | `<th>` | forces the column type instead of recognizing it |
| `data-kit-value="…"` | `<td>` | value to sort on, if different from the text (a date written "March 12", an amount with the currency) |

### Several columns

With `data-kit-sort="multi"` you can also sort by several columns together: **Shift + click** or **Ctrl/⌘ + click** on the header adds it as the next criterion (and again reverses it, and then removes it), while a normal click starts over from that column alone. The first criterion is the main one, the others decide ties; with several criteria the priority number appears next to the arrow. From the keyboard, Shift + Enter on the header button. Try it: Customer, then Shift + click on Amount.

Example markup:

```html
<section class="kit-card">
  <div class="kit-table-wrap">
    <table class="kit-table" data-kit-sort="multi">
      <thead><tr><th>Date</th><th>Number</th><th aria-sort="ascending">Customer</th><th class="kit-num" aria-sort="descending">Amount</th></tr></thead>
      <tbody>
        <tr><td>03/12/2026</td><td>FT-0042</td><td>Alpha Services Ltd</td><td class="kit-num">1,250.00</td></tr>
        <tr><td>03/02/2026</td><td>FT-0041</td><td>Beta Supplies Inc</td><td class="kit-num">830.40</td></tr>
        <tr><td>02/21/2026</td><td>FT-0040</td><td>Gamma Transport</td><td class="kit-num kit-danger">−310.00</td></tr>
        <tr><td>02/14/2026</td><td>FT-0039</td><td>Élite Consulting</td><td class="kit-num">12,400.00</td></tr>
        <tr><td>02/03/2026</td><td>FT-0038</td><td>Delta Systems</td><td class="kit-num">95.50</td></tr>
        <tr><td>01/28/2026</td><td>FT-0037</td><td>Alpha Services Ltd</td><td class="kit-num">2,100.00</td></tr>
        <tr><td>01/19/2026</td><td>FT-0036</td><td>Zeta Logistics</td><td class="kit-num kit-danger">−45.00</td></tr>
        <tr><td>01/09/2026</td><td>FT-0035</td><td>Beta Supplies Inc</td><td class="kit-num">1,980.00</td></tr>
        <tr><td>12/22/2025</td><td>FT-0034</td><td>Omega Studio</td><td class="kit-num">410.00</td></tr>
        <tr><td>12/11/2025</td><td>FT-0033</td><td>Gamma Transport</td><td class="kit-num">75.20</td></tr>
        <tr><td>11/30/2025</td><td>FT-0032</td><td>Delta Systems</td><td class="kit-num">3,300.00</td></tr>
        <tr><td>11/15/2025</td><td>FT-0031</td><td>Élite Consulting</td><td class="kit-num">620.00</td></tr>
      </tbody>
    </table>
  </div>
</section>
```

The small text (`<small>`) in a cell does not take part in sorting. With `Kit.table` you can also sort from code (`api.sort(2, "descending")`, or `api.sort([[2, "ascending"], [3, "descending"]])` with `multi`) and the `kit:sort` event arrives with `{ column, direction, criteria }` (`column` and `direction` are those of the first criterion, `criteria` lists them all); see [the API](#api).

## Text filter

`data-kit-filter="#id"` on a text field links the field to the table with that id: as you type, the rows that contain **all** the words remain (in any cell, ignoring case and accents). If nothing remains a "No results" row appears (`data-kit-empty` on the table to change the text). Sorting and filtering work together; the event is `kit:filter` with `{ query, count }`.

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-search" style="max-width: 320px; margin-bottom: var(--kit-sp)">
  <svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-search"/></svg>
  <input class="kit-input" type="search" placeholder="Search invoices…" aria-label="Search invoices" data-kit-filter="#invoices-filter">
</div>
<section class="kit-card">
  <div class="kit-table-wrap">
    <table class="kit-table" id="invoices-filter" data-kit-sort data-kit-empty="No invoices found">
      <thead><tr><th>Date</th><th>Number</th><th>Customer</th><th class="kit-num">Amount</th></tr></thead>
      <tbody>
        <tr><td>03/12/2026</td><td>FT-0042</td><td>Alpha Services Ltd</td><td class="kit-num">1,250.00</td></tr>
        <tr><td>03/02/2026</td><td>FT-0041</td><td>Beta Supplies Inc</td><td class="kit-num">830.40</td></tr>
        <tr><td>02/21/2026</td><td>FT-0040</td><td>Gamma Transport</td><td class="kit-num kit-danger">−310.00</td></tr>
        <tr><td>02/14/2026</td><td>FT-0039</td><td>Élite Consulting</td><td class="kit-num">12,400.00</td></tr>
        <tr><td>02/03/2026</td><td>FT-0038</td><td>Delta Systems</td><td class="kit-num">95.50</td></tr>
        <tr><td>01/28/2026</td><td>FT-0037</td><td>Alpha Services Ltd</td><td class="kit-num">2,100.00</td></tr>
        <tr><td>01/19/2026</td><td>FT-0036</td><td>Zeta Logistics</td><td class="kit-num kit-danger">−45.00</td></tr>
        <tr><td>01/09/2026</td><td>FT-0035</td><td>Beta Supplies Inc</td><td class="kit-num">1,980.00</td></tr>
        <tr><td>12/22/2025</td><td>FT-0034</td><td>Omega Studio</td><td class="kit-num">410.00</td></tr>
        <tr><td>12/11/2025</td><td>FT-0033</td><td>Gamma Transport</td><td class="kit-num">75.20</td></tr>

        <tr><td>11/15/2025</td><td>FT-0031</td><td>Élite Consulting</td><td class="kit-num">620.00</td></tr>
      </tbody>
    </table>

```

## Pagination

`data-kit-page="N"` on the table shows N rows at a time and adds the `kit-pagination` bar below: the count ("1–5 of 12"), the previous and next buttons and the page numbers with ellipses when there are many. The current page has `aria-current="page"`, the count is an `aria-live` area and focus stays on the pressed button. It works together with sorting and filtering: changing either returns to the first page, and the count is that of the filtered rows. When printing the bar is not there and the page shown is printed.

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-search" style="max-width: 320px; margin-bottom: var(--kit-sp)">
  <svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-search"/></svg>
  <input class="kit-input" type="search" placeholder="Search invoices…" aria-label="Search invoices" data-kit-filter="#invoices-pages">
</div>
<section class="kit-card">
  <div class="kit-table-wrap">
    <table class="kit-table kit-table-hover" id="invoices-pages" data-kit-sort data-kit-page="5">
      <thead><tr><th>Date</th><th>Number</th><th>Customer</th><th class="kit-num">Amount</th></tr></thead>
      <tbody>
        <tr><td>03/12/2026</td><td>FT-0042</td><td>Alpha Services Ltd</td><td class="kit-num">1,250.00</td></tr>
        <tr><td>03/02/2026</td><td>FT-0041</td><td>Beta Supplies Inc</td><td class="kit-num">830.40</td></tr>
        <tr><td>02/21/2026</td><td>FT-0040</td><td>Gamma Transport</td><td class="kit-num kit-danger">−310.00</td></tr>
        <tr><td>02/14/2026</td><td>FT-0039</td><td>Élite Consulting</td><td class="kit-num">12,400.00</td></tr>
        <tr><td>02/03/2026</td><td>FT-0038</td><td>Delta Systems</td><td class="kit-num">95.50</td></tr>
        <tr><td>01/28/2026</td><td>FT-0037</td><td>Alpha Services Ltd</td><td class="kit-num">2,100.00</td></tr>
        <tr><td>01/19/2026</td><td>FT-0036</td><td>Zeta Logistics</td><td class="kit-num kit-danger">−45.00</td></tr>
        <tr><td>01/09/2026</td><td>FT-0035</td><td>Beta Supplies Inc</td><td class="kit-num">1,980.00</td></tr>
        <tr><td>12/22/2025</td><td>FT-0034</td><td>Omega Studio</td><td class="kit-num">410.00</td></tr>
        <tr><td>12/11/2025</td><td>FT-0033</td><td>Gamma Transport</td><td class="kit-num">75.20</td></tr>
        <tr><td>11/30/2025</td><td>FT-0032</td><td>Delta Systems</td><td class="kit-num">3,300.00</td></tr>
        <tr><td>11/15/2025</td><td>FT-0031</td><td>Élite Consulting</td><td class="kit-num">620.00</td></tr>
      </tbody>
    </table>
  </div>
</section>
```

If the server does the pagination (the pages arrive ready-made) you write the bar by hand and use only the CSS: the buttons are normal `kit-btn`s.

Example markup:

```html
<nav class="kit-pagination" aria-label="Pagination" style="border: 1px solid var(--kit-line); border-radius: var(--kit-rad)">
  <p class="kit-pagination-info">21–30 of 87</p>
  <div class="kit-pagination-pages">
    <a class="kit-btn kit-btn-ghost kit-btn-icon" href="#" aria-label="Previous page">‹</a>
    <a class="kit-btn kit-btn-ghost" href="#" aria-label="Page 1">1</a>
    <span class="kit-pagination-gap" aria-hidden="true">…</span>
    <a class="kit-btn kit-btn-ghost" href="#" aria-label="Page 2">2</a>
    <a class="kit-btn" href="#" aria-label="Page 3" aria-current="page">3</a>
    <a class="kit-btn kit-btn-ghost" href="#" aria-label="Page 4">4</a>
    <span class="kit-pagination-gap" aria-hidden="true">…</span>
    <a class="kit-btn kit-btn-ghost" href="#" aria-label="Page 9">9</a>
    <a class="kit-btn kit-btn-ghost kit-btn-icon" href="#" aria-label="Next page">›</a>
  </div>
</nav>
```

## With Django and htmx

When there are many records the server does pagination, sorting and filtering, one page at a time, and `data-kit-sort`, `data-kit-filter` and `data-kit-page` are not needed: they work on the rows already present. Only the CSS is used (`kit-pagination`, `kit-sort-btn`, `aria-sort`) and htmx replaces the block. If `kit.js` is present, fragments inserted by htmx initialize by themselves (`htmx:load` event): selects, comboboxes, tabs, highlighted code and sortable tables inside the response work without calling `Kit.init`.

The scheme: a container with an id (`#invoices`) that is the `hx-target` and holds the card with table and bar; the search field sits _outside_, so it is not replaced and the cursor stays where it is. `hx-boost` on the container turns normal links (headers, pages) into htmx requests with the browser history; the links keep working even without JavaScript.

The full page (`invoices/list.html`) contains the field and the container; the view responds with only the fragment (`invoices/_table.html`) to htmx requests.

```html
<!-- invoices/list.html -->
<input class="kit-input" type="search" name="q" value="{{ q }}" placeholder="Search invoices…" aria-label="Search invoices"
       hx-get="{% url 'invoices' %}" hx-trigger="input changed delay:300ms, search"
       hx-target="#invoices" hx-push-url="true" hx-include="#invoices [name=sort]" hx-indicator="#invoices">

<div id="invoices" hx-boost="true" hx-target="#invoices" hx-swap="innerHTML" hx-indicator="#invoices">
  {% include "invoices/_table.html" %}
</div>
```

```html
<!-- invoices/_table.html -->
<input type="hidden" name="sort" value="{{ sort }}">
<section class="kit-card">
  <div class="kit-table-wrap">
    <table class="kit-table">
      <thead><tr>
        <th aria-sort="{% if sort == 'customer' %}ascending{% elif sort == '-customer' %}descending{% else %}none{% endif %}">
          <a class="kit-sort-btn" id="sort-customer"
             href="{% if sort == 'customer' %}{% querystring sort='-customer' page=None %}{% else %}{% querystring sort='customer' page=None %}{% endif %}">Customer</a>
        </th>
        <!-- the other columns are the same; without kit-sort-btn and aria-sort a column is not sortable -->
      </tr></thead>
      <tbody>
        {% for f in page %}
          <tr><td>{{ f.customer }}</td></tr>
        {% empty %}
          <tr class="kit-table-empty"><td colspan="4">No results</td></tr>
        {% endfor %}
      </tbody>
    </table>
  </div>
  <nav class="kit-pagination" aria-label="Pagination">
    <p class="kit-pagination-info">{{ page.start_index }}–{{ page.end_index }} of {{ page.paginator.count }}</p>
    {% if page.paginator.num_pages > 1 %}
    <div class="kit-pagination-pages">
      {% if page.has_previous %}
        <a class="kit-btn kit-btn-ghost kit-btn-icon" id="invoices-prev" href="{% querystring page=page.previous_page_number %}" aria-label="Previous page">‹</a>
      {% else %}
        <span class="kit-btn kit-btn-ghost kit-btn-icon" aria-disabled="true">‹</span>
      {% endif %}
      {% for n in pages %}
        {% if n == page.paginator.ELLIPSIS %}
          <span class="kit-pagination-gap" aria-hidden="true">…</span>
        {% elif n == page.number %}
          <a class="kit-btn" href="{% querystring page=n %}" aria-current="page" aria-label="Page {{ n }}">{{ n }}</a>
        {% else %}
          <a class="kit-btn kit-btn-ghost" href="{% querystring page=n %}" aria-label="Page {{ n }}">{{ n }}</a>
        {% endif %}
      {% endfor %}
      {% if page.has_next %}
        <a class="kit-btn kit-btn-ghost kit-btn-icon" id="invoices-next" href="{% querystring page=page.next_page_number %}" aria-label="Next page">›</a>
      {% else %}
        <span class="kit-btn kit-btn-ghost kit-btn-icon" aria-disabled="true">›</span>
      {% endif %}
    </div>
    {% endif %}
  </nav>
</section>
```

```python
# invoices/views.py
from django.core.paginator import Paginator
from django.db.models import Q
from django.shortcuts import render

ORDERINGS = {"date": "date", "customer": "customer__name", "amount": "amount"}

def invoices(request):
    qs = Invoice.objects.select_related("customer")
    q = request.GET.get("q", "").strip()
    if q:
        qs = qs.filter(Q(number__icontains=q) | Q(customer__name__icontains=q))
    sort = request.GET.get("sort", "-date")
    field = ORDERINGS.get(sort.lstrip("-"))
    if field:
        qs = qs.order_by(("-" if sort.startswith("-") else "") + field, "pk")   # "pk" keeps the order stable between pages
    page = Paginator(qs, 10).get_page(request.GET.get("page"))
    pages = list(page.paginator.get_elided_page_range(page.number, on_each_side=1, on_ends=1))
    # htmx asks for the fragment, but the "back" button with no cached history wants the full page
    partial = request.headers.get("HX-Request") and not request.headers.get("HX-History-Restore-Request")
    return render(request, "invoices/_table.html" if partial else "invoices/list.html",
                  {"page": page, "pages": pages, "q": q, "sort": sort})
```

```css
/* while the request is in progress htmx puts .htmx-request on the hx-indicator element */
#invoices.htmx-request { opacity: .55; pointer-events: none; transition: opacity .2s; }
```

A few details that matter: `{% querystring %}` (Django 5.1) keeps the other URL parameters, so search and sort stay while changing page, and `page=None` removes the page when the sort changes; before 5.1 you need an equivalent template tag. The `id`s on the previous and next links are for htmx, which after the swap puts focus back on the element with the same id: keyboard users do not lose it. For headers, `kit-sort-btn` also works on an `<a>`; with multi-column sorting written by the server the priority number is a `<span class="kit-sort-n">2</span>` inside the link.

## JavaScript

Attributes are enough in most cases. If the rows change after loading (a table filled by a request) call `api.refresh()`; otherwise `Kit.table(table, options)` does everything from code and `Kit.paginate(table, rows)` is the shortcut for pagination only. Both return the same object.

```js
const api = Kit.table("#invoices", { sort: true, size: 10, empty: "No invoices" });

api.sort(3, "descending");   // column (from 0) and direction: "ascending", "descending" or "none"
api.sort([[2, "ascending"], [3, "descending"]]);   // several columns (with data-kit-sort="multi")
api.filter("alfa");          // like typing in the search field
api.page(2);                 // go to page 2; api.page() reads it
api.pageSize(25);            // rows per page; 0 = all
api.refresh();               // after adding, removing or changing rows
api.state();                 // { sort: { column, direction, criteria }, query, page, pages, size, total, count }

document.querySelector("#invoices").addEventListener("kit:page", (e) => {
  console.log(e.detail);     // { page, pages, size, total }
});
```

| Option | Attribute | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `sort` | `data-kit-sort` | active only if the attribute is present |
| `size` | `data-kit-page` | `0`: no pagination |
| `empty` | `data-kit-empty` | `No results` |
| `labels` | – | bar texts: `of`, `prev`, `next`, `page` (con `{n}`), `nav`, `empty` |
| `filter`, `page` | – | initial filter and page |

## Sticky header and columns

By default the headers (`<th>`) stay stuck under `.kit-header` while the page scrolls. Inside `kit-table-wrap` the box scrolls only horizontally, so the header has nothing to detach from. For a long table add `kit-table-scroll` to the box: it has a maximum height (`--kit-table-h`, by default `28rem`), also scrolls vertically and the header stays attached to its top edge. Cell spacing is adjusted with `--kit-row` (vertical) and `--kit-cell` (horizontal).

`kit-table-fix` on the table locks the **first column** on the left while scrolling horizontally. It works with CSS only, even on rows added later (for example by htmx), and goes well with highlighted and selected rows. The corner cell (header of the fixed column) stays above everything. Try scrolling the table from one side to the other.

Example markup:

```html
<section class="kit-card">
  <div class="kit-table-wrap kit-table-scroll" style="--kit-table-h: 16rem">
    <table class="kit-table kit-table-hover kit-table-fix">
      <thead><tr><th>Number</th><th>Customer</th><th>Date</th><th class="kit-num">Net</th><th class="kit-num">VAT</th><th class="kit-num">Total</th><th>Status</th><th>Due date</th><th>Notes</th></tr></thead>
      <tbody>
        <tr><td>FT-0042</td><td>Alpha Services Ltd</td><td>03/12/2026</td><td class="kit-num">1,025.41</td><td class="kit-num">225.59</td><td class="kit-num">1,251.00</td><td><span class="kit-badge kit-badge-success">Issued</span></td><td>04/11/2026</td><td>Payment in 30 days</td></tr>
        <tr><td>FT-0041</td><td>Beta Supplies Inc</td><td>03/02/2026</td><td class="kit-num">680.66</td><td class="kit-num">149.74</td><td class="kit-num">830.40</td><td><span class="kit-badge kit-badge-warning">Received</span></td><td>04/01/2026</td><td>Partial delivery</td></tr>
        <tr><td>FT-0040</td><td>Gamma Transport</td><td>02/21/2026</td><td class="kit-num">−254.10</td><td class="kit-num">−55.90</td><td class="kit-num kit-danger">−310.00</td><td><span class="kit-badge kit-badge-danger">Discarded</span></td><td>–</td><td>Credit note</td></tr>
        <tr><td>FT-0039</td><td>Élite Consulting</td><td>02/14/2026</td><td class="kit-num">10,163.93</td><td class="kit-num">2,236.07</td><td class="kit-num">12,400.00</td><td><span class="kit-badge kit-badge-success">Issued</span></td><td>03/16/2026</td><td>Annual consulting</td></tr>
        <tr><td>FT-0038</td><td>Delta Systems</td><td>02/03/2026</td><td class="kit-num">78.28</td><td class="kit-num">17.22</td><td class="kit-num">95.50</td><td><span class="kit-badge kit-badge-success">Issued</span></td><td>03/05/2026</td><td>–</td></tr>
        <tr><td>FT-0037</td><td>Alpha Services Ltd</td><td>01/28/2026</td><td class="kit-num">1,721.31</td><td class="kit-num">378.69</td><td class="kit-num">2,100.00</td><td><span class="kit-badge kit-badge-warning">Received</span></td><td>02/27/2026</td><td>Contract renewal</td></tr>
        <tr><td>FT-0036</td><td>Zeta Logistics</td><td>01/19/2026</td><td class="kit-num">−36.89</td><td class="kit-num">−8.11</td><td class="kit-num kit-danger">−45.00</td><td><span class="kit-badge kit-badge-danger">Discarded</span></td><td>–</td><td>Reversal</td></tr>
        <tr><td>FT-0035</td><td>Beta Supplies Inc</td><td>01/09/2026</td><td class="kit-num">1,622.95</td><td class="kit-num">357.05</td><td class="kit-num">1,980.00</td><td><span class="kit-badge kit-badge-success">Issued</span></td><td>02/08/2026</td><td>January order</td></tr>
        <tr><td>FT-0034</td><td>Omega Studio</td><td>12/22/2025</td><td class="kit-num">336.07</td><td class="kit-num">73.93</td><td class="kit-num">410.00</td><td><span class="kit-badge kit-badge-success">Issued</span></td><td>01/21/2026</td><td>–</td></tr>
        <tr><td>FT-0033</td><td>Gamma Transport</td><td>12/11/2025</td><td class="kit-num">61.64</td><td class="kit-num">13.56</td><td class="kit-num">75.20</td><td><span class="kit-badge kit-badge-warning">Received</span></td><td>01/10/2026</td><td>Urgent shipment</td></tr>
      </tbody>
    </table>
  </div>
</section>
```

To lock several columns write `data-kit-fix="2"` (up to 4): `kit.js` measures the width of the first columns and measures again when the table changes size (window, larger text, new rows). Without `kit.js` the cumulative widths must be written by hand as `--kit-fix-1` (width of the first), `--kit-fix-2` (first + second) and so on, for example `style="--kit-fix-1: 8rem"`. The thin line on the right marks where the last fixed column ends.

Example markup:

```html
<section class="kit-card">
  <div class="kit-table-wrap kit-table-scroll" style="--kit-table-h: 16rem">
    <table class="kit-table kit-table-hover kit-table-fix" data-kit-fix="2">
      <thead><tr><th>Number</th><th>Customer</th><th>Date</th><th class="kit-num">Net</th><th class="kit-num">VAT</th><th class="kit-num">Total</th><th>Status</th><th>Due date</th><th>Notes</th></tr></thead>
      <tbody>
        <tr><td>FT-0042</td><td>Alpha Services Ltd</td><td>03/12/2026</td><td class="kit-num">1,025.41</td><td class="kit-num">225.59</td><td class="kit-num">1,251.00</td><td><span class="kit-badge kit-badge-success">Issued</span></td><td>04/11/2026</td><td>Payment in 30 days</td></tr>

        <tr><td>FT-0037</td><td>Alpha Services Ltd</td><td>01/28/2026</td><td class="kit-num">1,721.31</td><td class="kit-num">378.69</td><td class="kit-num">2,100.00</td><td><span class="kit-badge kit-badge-warning">Received</span></td><td>02/27/2026</td><td>Contract renewal</td></tr>

        <tr><td>FT-0035</td><td>Beta Supplies Inc</td><td>01/09/2026</td><td class="kit-num">1,622.95</td><td class="kit-num">357.05</td><td class="kit-num">1,980.00</td><td><span class="kit-badge kit-badge-success">Issued</span></td><td>02/08/2026</td><td>January order</td></tr>
        <tr><td>FT-0034</td><td>Omega Studio</td><td>12/22/2025</td><td class="kit-num">336.07</td><td class="kit-num">73.93</td><td class="kit-num">410.00</td><td><span class="kit-badge kit-badge-success">Issued</span></td><td>01/21/2026</td><td>–</td></tr>
        <tr><td>FT-0033</td><td>Gamma Transport</td><td>12/11/2025</td><td class="kit-num">61.64</td><td class="kit-num">13.56</td><td class="kit-num">75.20</td><td><span class="kit-badge kit-badge-warning">Received</span></td><td>01/10/2026</td><td>Urgent shipment</td></tr>
      </tbody>
    </table>
  </div>
</section>
```

On very narrow screens fixed columns take space from the scrolling ones: keep few and short (a number, a short name). When printing the maximum height and the lock do not apply.

# Themes and tokens
Page: https://n1k1tas95.github.io/dashboard-kit/en/theming.html

The whole look comes from a few CSS variables. Changing them in `:root`, or on a single element, changes colors, density and corners of the whole interface.

## Light and dark theme

Colors are written once with `light-dark(light, dark)`. By default the theme follows the system; to force it set `data-theme` on `<html>`. With `kit.js` buttons with `data-kit-theme-set` are enough (the choice is remembered); the same goes for the [settings panel](https://n1k1tas95.github.io/dashboard-kit/en/overlays.html#settings), which gathers them with text and width.

```html
<html lang="en" data-theme="dark">           <!-- forced dark; without the attribute it follows the system -->

<button class="kit-btn" data-kit-theme-set="light">Light</button>
<button class="kit-btn" data-kit-theme-set="dark">Dark</button>
<button class="kit-btn" data-kit-theme-set="auto">Automatic</button>
```

### Theme selector (menu)

The header's "Theme" menu is a [pop-up menu](https://n1k1tas95.github.io/dashboard-kit/en/overlays.html#menu) (`.kit-pop`) whose items have `data-kit-theme-set`: on click `kit.js` applies the theme, remembers it and closes the menu. Each item has an icon and a title, and can have a gray line; `kit-pop-right` aligns the panel to the right edge, useful in a header. This example is really wired to the page's theme.

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-dropdown">
  <button class="kit-btn" data-kit-toggle="#menu-theme" aria-haspopup="menu" aria-expanded="false"><svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-auto"/></svg>Theme<svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-chev"/></svg></button>
  <div class="kit-pop" id="menu-theme" role="menu" hidden>
    <div class="kit-opt" role="menuitemradio" aria-checked="false" data-kit-theme-set="auto"><svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-auto"/></svg><span class="kit-opt-text"><b>Automatic</b><small>Follows the system</small></span><svg class="kit-icon kit-opt-check"><use href="#i-check"/></svg></div>
    <div class="kit-opt" role="menuitemradio" aria-checked="false" data-kit-theme-set="light"><svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-sun"/></svg><span class="kit-opt-text"><b>Light</b></span><svg class="kit-icon kit-opt-check"><use href="#i-check"/></svg></div>
    <div class="kit-opt" role="menuitemradio" aria-checked="false" data-kit-theme-set="dark"><svg class="kit-icon"><use href="#i-moon"/></svg><span class="kit-opt-text"><b>Dark</b></span><svg class="kit-icon kit-opt-check"><use href="#i-check"/></svg></div>
  </div>
</div>
```

Add `<meta name="color-scheme" content="light dark">` in the `<head>` to avoid a white flash on load in the dark theme.

## Font and text size

The kit uses [Inter](https://rsms.me/inter/) (OFL license, 65 KB, file `dist/fonts/inter-var.woff2`), designed for the screen and with a **slashed zero** that is not confused with the letter "o". The file sits next to `kit.css` and loads by itself; if it is not reachable the system font remains. To use another font just change `--kit-font`; for the slashed digit alone, `font-variant-numeric: slashed-zero` works with any font that provides it.

```css
:root { --kit-font: "IBM Plex Sans", system-ui, sans-serif; }   /* another font */
td.code { font-variant-numeric: slashed-zero tabular-nums; }  /* slashed zero and equal-width digits */
```

All text sizes are in `rem`, so they follow the base size `--kit-fs` (`1rem`). The base grows by itself with the screen: 15px up to 1279px, then 16px, 17px (from 1600px), 19px (from 1920px) and 22px (from 2560px). Control height, icons, header and content width are also in `rem` and grow along with the text.

The user can enlarge or shrink everything: `--kit-zoom` multiplies the base and `data-kit-fs` on `<html>` sets it (`md` normal, the default; `lg` large; `xl` extra large). With `kit.js` buttons with `data-kit-fs-set` or `data-kit-fs-step` are enough; the choice is remembered. These choices are also in the [settings panel](https://n1k1tas95.github.io/dashboard-kit/en/overlays.html#settings).

```html
<button class="kit-btn" data-kit-fs-step="-1" aria-label="Smaller text">A−</button>
<button class="kit-btn" data-kit-fs-step="1"  aria-label="Larger text">A+</button>

<button class="kit-btn" data-kit-fs-set="xl">Extra large</button>
```

```css
:root { --kit-fs: 16px; }                                   /* fixed base, no automatic growth */
@media (min-width: 2000px) { :root { --kit-fs: 24px; } }   /* or a threshold of your own */
```

## Layout tokens

They adjust the interface's breathing room, the text size and the heading scale (see [Typography](https://n1k1tas95.github.io/dashboard-kit/en/typography.html#tokens)). Below 760px `--kit-sp` goes down from 16 to 8px.

| Token | Value | What it controls |
|---|---|---|
| `--kit-fs` | `15px` | base text size (1rem) |
| `--kit-lh` | `1.5` | text line height |
| `--kit-h1` | `2.2rem` | h1 heading (and kit-fs-1) |
| `--kit-h2` | `1.75rem` | h2 heading (and kit-fs-2) |
| `--kit-h3` | `1.4rem` | h3 heading (and kit-fs-3) |
| `--kit-h4` | `1.2rem` | h4 heading (and kit-fs-4) |
| `--kit-h5` | `1.05rem` | h5 heading (and kit-fs-5) |
| `--kit-h6` | `1rem` | h6 heading (and kit-fs-6) |
| `--kit-zoom` | `.875` | multiplier chosen by the user: 0.875 (normal), 1, 1.125 |
| `--kit-sp` | `16px` | single spacing unit: margin, distance between cards, inner padding |
| `--kit-row` | `8px` | vertical padding of table rows |
| `--kit-cell` | `12px` | horizontal padding between columns |
| `--kit-rad` | `12px` | radius of surfaces: cards, dialogs, menus, code, toasts |
| `--kit-rad-sm` | `8px` | radius of controls: buttons, fields, segmented, menu items |
| `--kit-hh` | `4.8rem` | header height |
| `--kit-ctl` | `2.667rem` | height of buttons and fields |
| `--kit-container-w` | `80rem` | maximum width of centered content (.kit-container) |
| `--kit-side-w` | `16.5rem` | sidebar width (.kit-sidebar) |
| `--kit-side-wc` | `4.667rem` | width of the compact, icons-only sidebar |

## Color tokens

Each color has a value for the light and for the dark theme. The kit's classes always use tokens, never fixed colors: changing a token changes it everywhere.

| Token | Light | Dark | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--kit-bg` | `#f4f5f8` | `#0f1319` | Page background |
| `--kit-card` | `#fff` | `#171d26` | Background of cards, header, tables |
| `--kit-ink` | `#18202c` | `#e8edf4` | Main text |
| `--kit-mute` | `#5f6a7c` | `#8d99ab` | Secondary text |
| `--kit-line` | `#e4e8ee` | `#262e3a` | Borders |
| `--kit-line-soft` | `#eef1f5` | `#1f2630` | Light borders, table rows |
| `--kit-hover` | `#f1f5ff` | `#1c2736` | Background on mouse hover |
| `--kit-accent` | `#2559d8` | `#6ea2ff` | Accent color (buttons, links, selection) |
| `--kit-accent-ink` | `#fff` | `#0b1220` | Text on the accent |
| `--kit-accent-soft` | `#e9effd` | `#1b2a45` | Soft accent background |
| `--kit-danger` | `#b0301f` | `#ff7d6e` | Errors, negative values |
| `--kit-success` | `#147236` | `#4fca8b` | Positive outcome |
| `--kit-warning` | `#8f5200` | `#f0b04e` | Warnings |
| `--kit-c1` | `#2f6fe4` | `#6ea2ff` | Chart series 1 |
| `--kit-c2` | `#e39320` | `#f2a84c` | Chart series 2 |
| `--kit-c3` | `#1b8f82` | `#4ccbbb` | Chart series 3 |
| `--kit-c4` | `#8a4fd1` | `#b88cf0` | Chart series 4 |
| `--kit-hl-tag` | `#116329` | `#7ee787` | Code: tags and selectors |
| `--kit-hl-attr` | `#0550ae` | `#79c0ff` | Code: attributes and properties |
| `--kit-hl-str` | `#0a3069` | `#a5d6ff` | Code: strings |
| `--kit-hl-kw` | `#cf222e` | `#ff7b72` | Code: keywords |
| `--kit-hl-fn` | `#8250df` | `#d2a8ff` | Code: functions and pseudo-classes |
| `--kit-hl-num` | `#953800` | `#ffa657` | Code: numbers and class names |
| `--kit-hl-com` | `#6e7781` | `#8b949e` | Code: comments |

## Scrollbars

All scrollbars (page, tables, menus, dialogs) are thin, with the thumb in the secondary text color and an invisible track. The color is the `--kit-sb` token, which follows the light and dark theme by itself. The `kit-no-scrollbar` class hides the scrollbar of an element that still scrolls (useful for a row of tabs on narrow screens).

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-card kit-p-3" style="height: 130px; overflow: auto; max-width: 360px">
  <p>A scrolling box: the bar on the right is the kit's.</p><p>Second line.</p><p>Third line.</p><p>Fourth line.</p><p>Fifth line.</p><p>Sixth line.</p>
</div>
```

```css
:root { --kit-sb: color-mix(in srgb, var(--kit-accent) 50%, transparent); }   /* another color */
* { scrollbar-width: auto; scrollbar-color: auto; }                          /* or the system's */
```

## Customizing

Override the tokens in `:root` after loading `kit.css`:

```css
:root {
  --kit-accent: light-dark(#0f766e, #5eead4);
  --kit-accent-soft: light-dark(#e6f6f4, #12312e);
  --kit-rad: 6px;      /* less rounded surfaces */
  --kit-rad-sm: 4px;   /* less rounded controls */
  --kit-row: 5px;      /* more compact tables */
  --kit-ctl: 36px;     /* shorter buttons and fields */
}
```

Tokens can also be changed on a single element, and apply to everything it contains. Here an area with another accent:

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-bar" style="--kit-accent: light-dark(#0f766e, #5eead4); --kit-accent-soft: light-dark(#e6f6f4, #12312e)">
  <button class="kit-btn kit-btn-primary">Primary</button>
  <button class="kit-pill is-on">Active pill</button>
  <span class="kit-badge">Badge</span>
  <a href="#">A link</a>
</div>
```

Note: the inline `style` attribute requires `style-src-attr 'unsafe-inline'` if the site has a Content-Security-Policy; in a CSS file it is not needed.

---

# Typography
Page: https://n1k1tas95.github.io/dashboard-kit/en/typography.html

Headings, body text, quotes, lists and the classes to control size, weight, line height and line width. It all starts from a few tokens, so it is adjusted from a single place.

## Base text

The kit uses the [Inter](https://n1k1tas95.github.io/dashboard-kit/en/theming.html#text) font at `1rem` with line height `--kit-lh` (1.5). `1rem` is the base size `--kit-fs`, which grows with the screen and can be chosen by the user (see [Font and text size](https://n1k1tas95.github.io/dashboard-kit/en/theming.html#text)): all the sizes below are in `rem` or `em`, so they follow it. Zeros are slashed, so they are not confused with the letter "o".

## Headings

The `<h1>`…`<h6>` elements already have the kit's style. The `kit-h1`…`kit-h6` classes give the same look to another element (a `<p>`, a `<div>`) without changing the document structure. A `<small>` inside the heading becomes a gray secondary text.

Example markup:

```html
<h1>h1. Page title</h1>
<h2>h2. Section title</h2>
<h3>h3. Group title</h3>
<h4>h4. Block title</h4>
<h5>h5. Small title</h5>
<h6>h6. Smallest title</h6>
<h3>With secondary text <small>gray subtitle</small></h3>
<p class="kit-h4">A paragraph that looks like an h4 (kit-h4)</p>
```

The sizes are the `--kit-h1`…`--kit-h6` tokens: changing them in `:root` changes the scale of the whole page, including the `kit-fs-1`…`kit-fs-6` classes.

```css
:root {
  --kit-h1: 2.6rem;   /* bigger headings */
  --kit-h2: 2rem;
}
```

## Display

For an opening title, bigger and lighter than the normal ones (`kit-display-1` is the largest, `kit-display-4` the smallest). Below 576px they shrink by themselves.

Example markup:

```html
<p class="kit-display-1">Display 1</p>
<p class="kit-display-2">Display 2</p>
<p class="kit-display-3">Display 3</p>
<p class="kit-display-4">Display 4</p>
```

## Lead paragraph

With `kit-lead` the first paragraph stands out from the rest.

Example markup:

```html
<p class="kit-lead">A lead paragraph: a bit bigger than normal text, to introduce the topic.</p>
<p>The text that follows has the normal size.</p>
```

## Inline text

Example markup:

```html
<p>You can <mark>highlight</mark> a part (<code>&lt;mark&gt;</code>), <del>delete</del> (<code>&lt;del&gt;</code>), <ins>insert</ins> (<code>&lt;ins&gt;</code>), <u>underline</u> (<code>&lt;u&gt;</code>), make <strong>bold</strong> or <em>italic</em>, and write in <small>smaller type</small> (<code>&lt;small&gt;</code>).</p>
<p>Abbreviations show their meaning on mouse hover: <abbr title="Value added tax">VAT</abbr>, and in small caps with <code>kit-initialism</code>: <abbr class="kit-initialism" title="HyperText Markup Language">html</abbr>.</p>
<p>For a key use <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>K</kbd>; for code <code>kit-card</code>.</p>
```

## Classes to control the text

All with `!important`, like the [utilities](https://n1k1tas95.github.io/dashboard-kit/en/utilities.html), to win over the components' style.

### Size

`kit-fs-1`…`kit-fs-6` use the same scale as the headings; `kit-fs-sm` and `kit-fs-lg` are relative to the text that contains them (`.875em` and `1.2em`), useful inside a component.

Example markup:

```html
<p class="kit-fs-1 kit-lh-1">kit-fs-1</p>
<p class="kit-fs-2 kit-lh-1">kit-fs-2</p>
<p class="kit-fs-3 kit-lh-1">kit-fs-3</p>
<p class="kit-fs-4 kit-lh-1">kit-fs-4</p>
<p class="kit-fs-5 kit-lh-1">kit-fs-5</p>
<p class="kit-fs-6 kit-lh-1">kit-fs-6</p>
<p>Normal text, <span class="kit-fs-sm">smaller (kit-fs-sm)</span> and <span class="kit-fs-lg">larger (kit-fs-lg)</span>.</p>
```

### Weight and style

Example markup:

```html
<p class="kit-fw-light">kit-fw-light — light (300)</p>
<p class="kit-fw-normal">kit-fw-normal — normal (400)</p>
<p class="kit-fw-medium">kit-fw-medium — medium (500)</p>
<p class="kit-fw-semibold">kit-fw-semibold — semibold (600)</p>
<p class="kit-fw-bold">kit-fw-bold — bold (700)</p>
<p class="kit-fst-italic">kit-fst-italic — italic</p>
<p class="kit-fst-italic kit-fst-normal">kit-fst-normal — removes the italic</p>
```

### Alignment and wrapping

Example markup:

```html
<p class="kit-left">kit-left — left</p>
<p class="kit-center">kit-center — center</p>
<p class="kit-right">kit-right — right</p>
<div class="kit-card kit-p-3" style="max-width: 260px">
  <p class="kit-nowrap kit-mute" style="margin: 0 0 8px; overflow: hidden">kit-nowrap: a long line that never wraps and so overflows the space</p>
  <p class="kit-wrap" style="margin: 0 0 8px">kit-wrap: removes the ban on wrapping and the text goes back into the available space.</p>
  <p class="kit-break" style="margin: 0">kit-break: also breaks very long identifiers like IT01234567890ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789</p>
</div>
```

### Case, decoration and spacing

Example markup:

```html
<p class="kit-uppercase">kit-uppercase — all uppercase</p>
<p class="kit-lowercase">KIT-LOWERCASE — ALL LOWERCASE</p>
<p class="kit-capitalize">kit-capitalize — capitalized words</p>
<p class="kit-underline">kit-underline — underlined</p>
<p class="kit-line-through">kit-line-through — struck through</p>
<p><a class="kit-no-underline" href="#utilities">kit-no-underline — a link without underline</a></p>
<p class="kit-ls-tight">kit-ls-tight — tighter letters</p>
<p class="kit-ls-wide kit-uppercase kit-fs-sm">kit-ls-wide — spaced letters</p>
```

### Line height

`kit-lh-1` (1), `kit-lh-sm` (1.25), `kit-lh-base` (the value of `--kit-lh`) and `kit-lh-lg` (1.8). To change it everywhere just change `--kit-lh`.

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-row">
  <div class="kit-col-12 kit-col-md-6"><p class="kit-lh-sm"><b>kit-lh-sm</b> — A line of text long enough to wrap at least once, to see how close the lines are to each other.</p></div>
  <div class="kit-col-12 kit-col-md-6"><p class="kit-lh-lg"><b>kit-lh-lg</b> — A line of text long enough to wrap at least once, to see how close the lines are to each other.</p></div>
</div>
```

### Monospace font and color

`kit-mono` uses the code font (`--kit-mono`), useful for identifiers and amounts in a column. Text colors are in [Utilities](https://n1k1tas95.github.io/dashboard-kit/en/utilities.html#text); `kit-ink` brings back the normal color inside a colored element.

Example markup:

```html
<p><span class="kit-mono">FT-0042 · €1,250.00</span> · <span class="kit-mute">kit-mute <span class="kit-ink">kit-ink</span></span></p>
```

## Quotes

With `kit-quote` on a `<blockquote>`: a bar in the accent color on the left. The source goes in a `<footer>` (or in a `<figcaption>` if the quote is inside a `<figure>`), preceded by an em dash.

Example markup:

```html
<blockquote class="kit-quote">
  <p>A good dashboard shows the things you need, at the moment you need them.</p>
  <footer>From the project notes</footer>
</blockquote>
```

## Lists

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-row">
  <div class="kit-col-12 kit-col-md-4">
    <p class="kit-fw-semibold kit-mute kit-fs-sm">Normal</p>
    <ul><li>Received invoices</li><li>Issued invoices</li><li>Credit notes</li></ul>
  </div>
  <div class="kit-col-12 kit-col-md-4">
    <p class="kit-fw-semibold kit-mute kit-fs-sm">kit-list-unstyled</p>
    <ul class="kit-list-unstyled"><li>Received invoices</li><li>Issued invoices</li><li>Credit notes</li></ul>
  </div>
  <div class="kit-col-12 kit-col-md-4">
    <p class="kit-fw-semibold kit-mute kit-fs-sm">kit-list-inline</p>
    <ul class="kit-list-inline"><li>Received</li><li>Issued</li><li>Notes</li></ul>
  </div>
</div>
```

For label/value detail lists there is [key / value](https://n1k1tas95.github.io/dashboard-kit/en/cards.html#kv).

## Long texts

An article, a guide or some notes read better with shorter lines and more space between lines. `kit-prose` limits the width to `--kit-measure` (65 characters), brings the line height to 1.7 and spaces paragraphs, headings and lists regularly, without you having to put classes on the single elements. To limit only the width of a block there is `kit-measure`.

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-prose">
  <h3>How a long text is read</h3>
  <p>When a line goes past about seventy characters the eye struggles to return to the start of the next line. This is why long texts should not take up the whole width of a large screen.</p>
  <p>Line height matters too: lines that are too close blur together, lines too far apart read as separate paragraphs.</p>
  <h4>Some tips</h4>
  <ul>
    <li>Keep lines under 65–75 characters.</li>
    <li>Use a line height between 1.5 and 1.7.</li>
    <li>Give headings more space above than below.</li>
  </ul>
</div>
```

```html
<article class="kit-prose">
  <h2>Title</h2>
  <p>Text…</p>
</article>
```

```css
:root { --kit-measure: 72ch; }   /* slightly longer lines */
```

## Typographic tokens

| Token | Value | What it controls |
|---|---|---|
| `--kit-font` | `"Kit Inter", system-ui, …` | Text font |
| `--kit-mono` | `ui-monospace, Consolas, …` | Code font |
| `--kit-fs` | `15px` | Base size (1rem), grows with the screen |
| `--kit-zoom` | `.875` | Multiplier chosen by the user |
| `--kit-lh` | `1.5` | Text line height |
| `--kit-measure` | `65ch` | Maximum length of a line (`kit-prose`, `kit-measure`) |
| `--kit-h1`…`--kit-h6` | `2.2rem`…`1rem` | Size of headings and of `kit-fs-1`…`kit-fs-6` |

---

# Utilities
Page: https://n1k1tas95.github.io/dashboard-kit/en/utilities.html

One-line classes, as in Bootstrap: spacing, display, flexbox, sizes, text and visibility. Almost all use `!important` to win over components.

## Margins and padding

Format `kit-{m|p}{side}-{n}`. Sides: _none_ (all), `t` top, `b` bottom, `s` start, `e` end, `x` horizontal, `y` vertical. The `n` scale goes from 0 to 5; margins also have `auto`.

| n | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Value | 0 | 4px | 8px | 16px | 24px | 48px |

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-bar">
  <div class="kit-card kit-p-0">p-0</div>
  <div class="kit-card kit-p-1">p-1</div>
  <div class="kit-card kit-p-2">p-2</div>
  <div class="kit-card kit-p-3">p-3</div>
  <div class="kit-card kit-p-4">p-4</div>
  <div class="kit-card kit-px-5 kit-py-2">px-5 py-2</div>
</div>
```

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-card kit-card-body kit-mt-4 kit-mb-2">kit-mt-4 kit-mb-2</div>
<div class="kit-d-flex"><button class="kit-btn">Left</button><button class="kit-btn kit-ms-auto">kit-ms-auto: to the right</button></div>
```

## Display

`kit-d-{value}` with value `none`, `inline`, `block`, `inline-block`, `flex`, `inline-flex`, `grid`. With a breakpoint it applies from there up: `kit-d-md-none`.

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-card kit-p-3 kit-d-none kit-d-md-block">Visible from md (768px) up: <code>kit-d-none kit-d-md-block</code></div>
<div class="kit-card kit-p-3 kit-d-md-none">Visible only below md: <code>kit-d-md-none</code></div>
<p class="kit-mute">Resize the window to see the two boxes alternate.</p>
```

## Flexbox

With `kit-d-flex` you enable direction (`kit-flex-row`, `-column`, `-row-reverse`, `-column-reverse`), wrapping (`kit-flex-wrap`, `-nowrap`), `kit-justify-content-{start|end|center|between|around|evenly}`, `kit-align-items-{start|end|center|baseline|stretch}`, `kit-align-self-*`, `kit-flex-grow-1`, `kit-flex-shrink-0`, `kit-flex-fill` and `kit-gap-0…5`. Direction, justify and align also have a per-breakpoint version.

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-d-flex kit-justify-content-between kit-align-items-center kit-card kit-p-3">
  <b>Title</b>
  <span class="kit-badge kit-badge-success">justify-content-between</span>
</div>
<div class="kit-d-flex kit-gap-3 kit-align-items-center">
  <button class="kit-btn kit-flex-shrink-0">Does not shrink</button>
  <div class="kit-card kit-p-3 kit-flex-grow-1">flex-grow-1: takes the remaining space</div>
</div>
<div class="kit-d-flex kit-flex-column kit-flex-md-row kit-gap-2">
  <div class="kit-card kit-p-3 kit-flex-fill">In a column on the phone</div>
  <div class="kit-card kit-p-3 kit-flex-fill">in a row from md up</div>
</div>
```

## Sizes

`kit-w-100`, `kit-w-auto`, `kit-h-100`, `kit-h-auto`. `kit-h-100` is often needed to make a card reach the height of the column that contains it.

## Text and color

Example markup:

```html
<div class="kit-bar">
  <span class="kit-mute">kit-mute</span>
  <span class="kit-accent">kit-accent</span>
  <span class="kit-success">kit-success</span>
  <span class="kit-warning">kit-warning</span>
  <span class="kit-danger">kit-danger</span>
  <span class="kit-num">1,234.50 (kit-num: aligned digits)</span>
</div>
<div class="kit-card kit-p-3 kit-mt-3" style="max-width: 220px"><span class="kit-truncate" style="display:block">kit-truncate cuts with an ellipsis a text that is too long for the available space</span></div>
```

Others: `kit-nowrap`, `kit-center`, `kit-right`. Size, weight, line height, case and line width are in [Typography](https://n1k1tas95.github.io/dashboard-kit/en/typography.html#utilities).

## Visibility
- `kit-hidden` and the `hidden` attribute: hide the element.
- `kit-sr`: hides it visually but it stays readable by screen readers (labels for icon-only controls).
- `kit-hide-sm` (below 760px) and `kit-only-sm` (only below 760px): shortcuts tied to the phone breakpoint. For the other breakpoints use `kit-d-*`.

## Print

The kit prepares the page for printing: always on light (even if it is dark on screen), without header, alerts and tabs, without shadows, with the page margins reset. Badge and chart colors are kept. Cards, lists, KPI cards and table rows do not split between two pages, and the table header repeats on every page.
- `kit-no-print`: the element is not printed (buttons, filters, toolbars).
- `kit-print-only`: the element is only visible when printing (document title, date, notes).
- `kit-print-break`: goes to a new page; `kit-print-avoid`: does not split between two pages.

The sheet size and margins are left to the app: `@page { size: A4; margin: 14mm }` in your CSS.
